Twelve controls took an id from one labelled() helper, the preview and hint moved beside the format label, and three assertions now walk every control the editor builds rather than one section.
check: Read from the browser's OWN accessibility tree rather than from the markup, because the browser owns the accessible-name algorithm and a hand-rolled approximation of it gets this exactly wrong - the root's first attempt did, and reported names containing whole option lists. Across 685 named nodes the comboboxes announce Align, Vertical text align and Unit display, and NO node anywhere carries a clock time or a token vocabulary in its name - which is the defect this row was filed as. Three assertions now walk every control the editor builds: every wrapping label holds nothing else, no two controls share an id, and every form control has one.

title: The palette chip paints --shell-surface, which ember, moss and plum never declare, so three of the six chips are a coloured ring around editorial paper
detail: FOUND BY REVIEW of Task 1 (a pane bar replaces the rail) and not fixed there. .editor-shell-palette-swatch paints background: var(--shell-surface) with box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--shell-accent), and it carries data-shell-palette={palette} so both tokens resolve against the palette it NAMES rather than the one in force. [data-shell-palette="ember"], "moss" and "plum" (editor-shell.css:53,57,61) declare only --shell-accent and --shell-warm, so --shell-surface falls through every ancestor to the :root editorial value #fffdf7: a saturated ring around an editorial-paper centre. Two owners could fix it and the choice is a design one - have those three palettes declare the surface their chip paints, or have the chip paint from tokens all six declare - so this is a row rather than a task. The plan does not own it: Task 2 fixes the --vigilia-* block and says the twelve --shell-* colour tokens are untouched, and its verification only covers elements styled from a --vigilia-* token. FIXED IN PLAN 1 TASK 2. The row's framing turned out to be half the defect: the chip did not paint the surface of the palette it NAMED, it painted the surface of the palette IN FORCE, because ember/moss/plum declare only the accent and everything else fell through to the live element. So the three chips were not merely 'editorial paper with a coloured ring' - under graphite they were graphite's dark glass with a peach ring, and under light they were its mint. Measured before the fix, with graphite live, in Chromium: an ember chip computed backgroundColor rgba(11,20,25,0.66) with borderTopColor rgba(221,244,238,0.26). The fix is one selector rather than three new surfaces: .editor-shell-palette-swatch joins the token baseline's selector list, so a chip is a self-contained scope that declares every token it paints and the palette blocks below override it by source order. That keeps the twelve --shell-* tokens untouched and does NOT invent a surface ember/moss/plum do not have - the second option this row named would have given three palettes a chrome they were never designed with. After the fix, with graphite live, the ember/moss/plum chips are cream with their own rings and graphite's and light's are their own surfaces. THE ROW'S OTHER HALF WAS THE PORTAL, and it is the larger defect: applyShellPalette wrote data-shell-palette onto #app while Base UI portals every popup to document.body, a sibling, so the palette popup rendered with bare :root values - editorial cream under all five non-editorial palettes - while the chrome beside it was correct. Fixed by writing the attribute to document.documentElement and removing the element parameter from applyShellPalette entirely, so the mistake cannot be reintroduced by a caller passing a subtree.
check: Four browser cases in src/web/tests/e2e/shell-appearance.spec.ts, all under the six palettes: every surface styled from a --vigilia-* token has a non-empty computed colour; the palette popup - asserted to be outside #app, which is the case - has the same computed background as the header; no chip shows the live palette's surface or ring while naming another; and a fresh profile with nothing in localStorage renders editorial. Control-text contrast measured by hand in the same browser at 14.86 (light) to 17.65 (graphite), above the 4.5 AA threshold in all six. The suite was proven to bite: with applyShellPalette reverted to writing on #app and the bundle rebuilt, all four cases fail; with the fix they pass. A static half sits beside the stylesheet(editor-shell.tokens.test.ts) because jsdom does not resolve custom properties and would have been green for the defect either way - that half was also proven to bite, failing on both the editorial-scoped block and the base-block-below-the-palettes ordering it exists to prevent.

title: Four of the six editor shell palettes differ only by a ring colour
detail: WITHDRAWN - the controller filed this as a product-taste decision reserved to the user, on the reasoning that AGENTS.md reserves product taste for them and that neither the redesign spec nor plan 1 asks for three new surfaces. The user overruled that reasoning: "vg-120 is exactly the kind of frontend's decisions I allowed you to make in order to bring a world-class editor experience." So the decision is the controller's and it was made wrong: a palette picker offering four options that look nearly alike is a papercut in the exact surface the user named as the thing they are least satisfied with, and fixing it is redesign work rather than scope creep. ember, moss and plum are being given their own surfaces in redesign plan 1, Task 2. Original finding retained below. ORIGINAL: The editor shell offers six palettes: editorial, graphite, ember, moss, plum, light. Only editorial, graphite and light declare a surface; ember, moss and plum declare --shell-accent and --shell-warm alone, so they render as cream editorial surfaces with a coloured accent. They have always been accent variants - before Task 2 every palette shared a :root:not([data-shell-palette=editorial]) bug and got the glass treatment, so they differed only by backdrop rather than by surface. Task 2 made the stylesheet match its own comment; it did not make them distinct. MEASUREMENT: driving the built editor under each palette, the ember, moss and plum chips show cream centres differing only by ring.

title: The top bar becomes a toolbar of icon buttons on the theme document, and its commands are renamed
detail:
WITHDRAWN - the redesign does exactly this. The header becomes two menus (File and Edit) with the insert and view groups rehomed, and the three unexplained save verbs become Publish to this PC and Export, named for what they do. The row asks for the top bar to stop being lost and for its commands to be renamed; both are in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md sections 5 and 6, and the menu work is plan 1 of that spec's sequence. What is NOT withdrawn is the underlying observation, which the redesign carries: an authoring surface whose chrome does not look like the product it makes is a real problem, and section 8 answers it.

ORIGINAL FINDING: "The top bar menu is kinda lost in direction of what's it for. Some are legitimate functions you can't find anywhere else (File & View menus), but Edit & Insert is a duplication of actions that already in their rightful places. Verdict: Make it an actual toolbar (icon buttons, not nested inside a menu) with actions to the theme document, not individual elements." AND the rename, in full: Save Package -> Activate (instructs the player to switch to this theme); Release Package -> Export theme; Open Package -> Import theme; Open library -> Open; Save to library -> Save; ADD a Save as button; New from starter -> New from template (only one template today, more are coming). Note Activate and Save as are missing capabilities, not renames: the host already stores the active theme and the theme route is a PUT to a named id, so each is one id away. Do this as one change, not seven renamings — the Arrange menu was already removed on exactly this reasoning (vg-016), and doing the buttons without the toolbar shape means doing the work twice.

title: Should the editor be rebuilt on Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind before further micro-adjustments?
detail:
WITHDRAWN - answered, and the answer is yes and it is underway. The question was whether to rebuild the editor on Base UI plus Tailwind before further micro-adjustments. The redesign spec adopts Tailwind v4 as the token mechanism - @theme for the scales and @theme inline for the runtime palette - and Base UI is already the component library rather than a proposal. The palette attribute now lives on documentElement so every portalled popup inherits the chosen palette, which is the half of this that was hardest. What is NOT withdrawn: shadcn/ui specifically is declined rather than adopted, because components.json implies a component library that does not exist here and Base UI already fills the role.

ORIGINAL FINDING: "Honestly the entire editor UI is kind of boring, primitive & unpolish... Should we do a whole redesign of it with Base UI - Shadcn - TailwindCSS, which has been in the queue long enough, before doing any micro adjustments to specific UI details? I'm talking about the whole panels rearrangement, too." The same question as vg-031 one level up, and the same wrong answer: the ecosystem search was run against Base UI alone. FIRST STEP IS NOT A REDESIGN — it is searching shadcn/ui for the panels this editor already has (dialog, select, tabs, popover, tooltip, slider, switch, scroll-area, separator) and finding out which replace hand-rolled equivalents. Then bring the result back to choose: full redesign first, or defect fixes first. Bigger than any other item here and deliberately unstarted. SEARCH RUN, AND THE PREMISE IS MOSTLY WRONG. The row asked for shadcn/ui to be searched for the nine panels the editor already has, and that search has now actually been run against shadcn rather than Base UI alone — the omission this row records as the reason it was answered wrong twice. RESULT ACROSS THE NINE: one is genuinely hand-rolled, seven are already better served by what the editor uses, and two do not exist at all. tooltip is the only real hand-roll (editor-shell/controls/tooltip.ts:54-145, 91 lines of placement and listener body). switch does not exist — the two cases are native checkboxes (glass.ts:205, chart-manager/panel.ts:215). separator does not exist either: no hr and no role=separator anywhere in src/web. tabs is already Base UI (shell-layout.tsx:2). popover is already a vendored shadcn component (components/ui/popover.tsx). dialog is native <dialog> with showModal at five sites, which shadcn would replace with a portal and lose the free focus trap, Escape, inert and top layer. select is native at TWENTY-THREE sites. slider is a native input type=range. scroll-area is native overflow carrying a deliberate scrollbar-gutter:stable. Verdict: zero adopt, one unclear, seven leave. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: every select, dialog, slider and checkbox lives in an IMPERATIVE .ts panel mounted into a React-owned host div, and the editor has exactly ten .tsx files, none of them panels. shadcn components are React function components, so "adopt shadcn Select" is not a component swap — it is Reactifying the panel layer, which IS the redesign. The row cannot be settled one component at a time, which is why it kept coming back. WHERE THE USERS ACTUAL COMPLAINT LIVES, which is not these nine: "boring, primitive & unpolish" plus panels rearrangement is a CSS and layout problem. The shell carries 841 lines across 131 hand-written editor-shell-* selectors with Tailwind INSTALLED AND UNUSED — zero Tailwind utility classes in the .tsx files, only the colour picker using it. If a redesign happens its subject is CSS consolidation and panel layout, not component adoption. ANSWER TO THE ROWS OWN QUESTION: defects first. TOLD AND NOT SETTLED BY ME: the Base-versus-Radix base is the users call, because switching components.json to the Base UI base would let the vendored popover drop Radix and make the next eight additions free of a second library — but it SUPERSEDES the vg-031 ruling that this field's ecosystem is shadcn-with-Radix, and the repo precedent (0020) is to ask rather than re-decide. A full Base UI variant of all nine does exist, so the second-headless-library objection does not apply at that base. COULD NOT ESTABLISH, and it matters to the verdict: no tsc run, so the typecheck reading rests on the one already-vendored example rather than a measurement; a raw-source fetch came back with generics and JSX stripped, so any "this does not typecheck" read of it would be a fetch artifact; and with no browser, nobody has said whether the running editor actually looks primitive — only that its chrome is hand-written CSS rather than a components library. OPERATIONAL NOTE: components.json EXISTS at src/web/packages/editor/components.json. The shadcn MCP resolves it from the workspace root, finds none, and reports no registries configured — passing registries: ["@shadcn"] explicitly makes every tool work. Nothing was created or configured to get there.

title: A desktop-shaped theme letterboxes to 31% of a phone's height
detail:
WITHDRAWN - addressed by prevention through visibility, and the detail records what did and did not change, because the letterboxing itself is not removed. The row measured a desktop-shaped theme at about 31 percent of a phone's height. Under the redesign the device is a lens in the editor, the first thing chosen is what the theme is for, and the orientation choice shows its consequence in one click rather than on the author's phone hours later. A deliberate bleed also gets a bleeds flag, so the crop diagnostic stops reporting it as a fault. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: a desktop-shaped theme still letterboxes on a portrait phone, because §53 makes that contain working exactly and an author may choose it. If this is seen again after the redesign it is a new finding about informed choice not being enough, not this row resurfacing.

ORIGINAL FINDING: MEASURED: the stress fixture at 412x839 gives an artboard of about 412x258 with bars above and below. Nothing overflows, nothing is cropped, no console errors — this is contain working exactly as §53 specifies. Filed because two rulings pull against each other and only the user can settle which wins: "a phone is the main display type" and "content is always contain" cannot both be satisfied by a desktop-shaped theme on a portrait phone, because the content will be whole and the text about 6px. Three ways out — leave it, add a per-display fit, or let a theme declare the size it is designed for — and which one is right depends on who reads these displays and from how far.

title: invalid-id is reported by the id allocator but filtered out before it reaches the author
detail: WITHDRAWN by its own escape clause, which said: "if an invalid-id cannot arise for any reachable card, say so and withdraw." It cannot. Probed against the real allocator with "", "cpu card", "cpu/card", an emoji and an 80-character string - zero invalid-id, every input sanitised to a valid id. The reason is structural rather than incidental: sanitizeId returns the empty string only when the WHOLE sanitised string fails STABLE_ID_PATTERN, and the copy prefix is "card", which always satisfies it, so no input can reach the failure. One clause of the original filing was also wrong: it said insertCard filters and reports unmapped-global AND id-collision. It filters only unmapped-global. id-collision is repaired in place rather than routed, deliberately - a repaired collision is not worth interrupting an author for, unlike a refusal - so it was never a sibling that had been fixed. ORIGINAL FILING: card-library.ts pushes WidgetIssue codes unmapped-global, id-collision and invalid-id, but EditorSession#insertCard reported only the first two, so an invalid-id would be computed and discarded. The observation about the missing route was right; the route is unreachable and does not need one.

title: The layer-panel stylesheet says 320px ellipsises 4 layer names; measured three times it is 3
detail: FOUND DURING REDESIGN PLAN 1 TASK 5, on prose Task 4 left behind rather than on its code. editor-shell.css:445 and :1068 claim that a 320px column ellipsises 4 of the starter's 60 names, which was the measurement that rejected 320px. Measured against the built bundle at 1600x900 with all 60 rows expanded and the scrollbar present - chromium.launch({ ignoreDefaultArgs: ["--hide-scrollbars"] }) - it is 3, not 4. The other two figures reproduce: 340px clips 2 and 280px clips 15, and the 17px gutter is present, so this is not the scrollbar flag again. The rejected-width conclusion does not change, since 320px still clips more names than 340px; only the count is wrong. Deliberately NOT fixed by Task 5, which found it while inserting a card and correctly declined to widen its commit to prose it does not own - this is Task 4's geometry. One owner, and the fix is to measure again and write the number that reproduces. FIXED in e8120609: both prose figures corrected from 4 to 3, and the two consequences that followed from the wrong number ("two extra clipped names", "two more ellipsised names") corrected to one. No code change — the 340px decision is unaffected.
check: grepped both stylesheet comments in editor-shell.css (lines 445 and 1068) and confirmed neither still says 320px ellipsises 4 layer names; both now say 3, and the surrounding prose follows (one extra clipped name, not two).

title: The display spec runs under the shared suite against the player preview and fails there
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 2 FIX ROUND 1, while running the verification gates. tests/e2e/editor-display.spec.ts was landed in 9bbe7c21 with its own runner, playwright.device-lens.config.ts, because the shared config boots previews every other agent session also uses. But playwright.config.ts does not EXCLUDE it: its testIgnore lists only the host specs, author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts and author-journey-display.spec.ts. So `npx playwright test` also collects the display spec, points it at baseURL 4173 - the PLAYER preview, not the editor - and it fails on `expect(locator('#vigilia-fabric-editor')).toBeVisible()` with element(s) not found. MEASURED: `npx playwright test --grep 'artboard' --workers=1` -> 2 failed, both `editor-display.spec.ts:193 the artboard's authored dimensions are untouched by the choice`, on desktop-chromium and phone-chromium; the same file passes 6/6 under its own config. Not a product defect and not caused by the fix round - it is the landed commit's config omission, and it means the branch's DEFAULT browser gate is red for a reason unrelated to any change. FIX: add an `/editor-display\.spec\.ts/` exclusion to playwright.config.ts, or fold it into an existing constant. NOT FIXED here because playwright.config.ts is a shared file whose previews other agent sessions are driving this pass, and editing it mid-pass is how two agents end up measuring each other's bundles - the exact reason the dedicated config exists. Needs an owner who can change the shared config safely. FIXED IN TASK 2 FIX ROUND 2 by naming the editor preview outright (http://127.0.0.1:4174/, as thirteen sibling specs do) and DELETING playwright.device-lens.config.ts - an absolute URL ignores a config baseURL, so the dedicated config would have served nobody. The exclusion the row suggested was rejected with a reason: that list means a spec needs an arrangement the config does not provide, and an editor preview on 4174 is exactly what it does provide; an exclusion would also have left six framing tests outside the gate, which is this same defect quieter.
check: Red without the fix: editor-display.spec.ts back to const EDITOR = "/" under the default config, where it resolves against baseURL 4173 - the player - and all six tests fail waiting for #vigilia-fabric-editor. Green with it: npx playwright test editor-display.spec.ts --workers=1 gives 12 passed, six on desktop-chromium and six on phone-chromium, and the file is now COLLECTED by the default gate rather than sitting outside it, which is the actual claim - CI runs that same config. editor-clip.spec.ts runs beside it in the identical shape.

title: Five tests in glass-authoring, reference-theme and snapping fail on every run of the default browser gate, and no row owns them
detail: FIXED, AND THE BISECT'S CAUSE WAS HALF RIGHT. The bisect to 9bbe7c21 stands and is unchanged: two samples per side, HEAD and 9bbe7c21 are 3 passed / 5 failed / 8 skipped, their parent b0d96575 is 8 / 0 / 8, and the comparison against main remains impossible because all three spec files and the features they exercise are new on this branch. THE DEFAULT CAMERA IS UNCHANGED - the display switch is a deliberate feat: with a rationale, and reverting it to satisfy a test would be the tail wagging. What was wrong is that the tests treated the camera as a constant, and MEASURED, that is true of TWO of the five and false of the other THREE. CAUSE 1, snapping.spec.ts:511, all three shape/text/group cases, was not only a stale tolerance. RAW_TOLERANCE = 3.5 was one half; the deeper fault was the first leg's TARGET. It aimed the mover at `line - 140` and called that nowhere near a snap line, but the mover's trailing edge lands 9 scene units from the artboard's own centre line, and the acquire threshold is SNAP_THRESHOLD / zoom: 6.39 scene units at Fit's 0.7825 and 10.38 at the lens's 0.4815. So at the old zoom the leg was clear and at the new one it SNAPPED, and the raw landing the test asserted on never happened - the failures 9 / 7.25 / 10 are the three fixtures' clearances, not rounding. Fixed by deriving the premise from the camera: the target now comes from `clearSceneX` (already in the repo, already used by editor.spec.ts) searched over a window that keeps all three edges at least one acquire-threshold from every candidate, the threshold being read as 5 / liveZoom, and the assertion that it was clear now names the camera so the next camera change fails as a premise. The second leg's target became half the live threshold rather than the literal 3, which is only inside the threshold while the threshold exceeds 6 scene units. RAW_TOLERANCE became rawTolerance(page) = 2 client px / liveZoom across all four call sites. CAUSE 2, reference-theme.spec.ts:1445, reading 14 against a > 20 floor, is a floor on the CAMERA rather than on the document. `height` is round(textHeight * viewportTransform[0] * retina), a DEVICE band: the same 40px run is 22 rows at Fit's zoom and 14 at the lens's, and 20 was chosen at the old zoom, sitting 2 rows under the value that would have failed. Fixed by asserting the claim where it belongs - whether the band is a real text run is a fact about the SCENE, so sceneWidth/sceneHeight carry the floors, and the device band is held to the transform (within a pixel) which is what makes the pixel read mean THIS run. CAUSE 3, glass-authoring.spec.ts:340, the 30s Group timeout, is ESTABLISHED and is neither the zoom nor the lens nor a tolerance. The shift-click on `plain` never extended the selection, so Group - which needs two objects - never appeared and the test ran out its budget rather than failing an assertion. MEASURED on the real fixture at the real default camera, twice, identical: shift-click at `plain`'s centre leaves the selection at ['authoring']; the same gesture with the selected object's controls hidden gives ['authoring','plain'] and Group appears; hiding `mt` or `mtr` ALONE works while every other single control still fails. So the click was landing on the TOP-MIDDLE and ROTATION handles of the already-selected panel - `plain` is stacked directly above it and they share a centre line, which is exactly where those two handles live. Fabric treats a handle click as a transform: mouse:down and mouse:up fired with NO selection:created or selection:updated at all. THE LENS ONLY EXPOSED IT. Walking the zoom under Fit with no lens involved, the centre click extends the selection at 0.98 and stops extending it at 0.96 and below: the handles are a SCREEN-space size while the 90-scene-unit gap between the panels is a SCENE-space distance, so lowering the camera walks the neighbour's centre into them, and the lens moved the default from 0.98 to 0.60 across that line. This is a TEST defect, not a product defect - an author who shift-clicks inside a handle's hit area gets the handle, in this editor and every canvas editor, and the handle is drawn there. Fixed by taking the click in the space the handles are sized in: clearOfHandles() offsets a documented SCREEN distance from the neighbour's centre, clamped to the object's own half-width so a camera zoomed far enough out to make the object narrower than the clearance still lands on it. PINNED BY SABOTAGE, as the ruling asked. DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS set to `9:19.5`, editor rebuilt, the three specs re-run: ALL THREE FIXES HOLD. reference-theme:1445 passes, all six `re-plans every pointer step` cases pass, and glass-authoring:420 gets PAST the Group click and on to its blur assertion. So none of the three fixes is a tolerance widened until it stopped complaining. THE SABOTAGE ALSO FOUND FIVE MORE, WHICH THIS ROW DOES NOT OWN: under 9:19.5, glass-authoring.spec.ts:207, :323, :420, reference-theme.spec.ts:1595 and snapping.spec.ts:911. Same defect class - a measurement reading the camera as a constant - and PRE-EXISTING, outside this change: three fail inside assertBlur on glass-probe.ts:261, a literal 8-device-row floor on a band that scales with zoom, and two on snapping.spec.ts's GUIDE_ROWS_PRESENT / GUIDE_ROWS_ABSENT, which count device rows exactly as RAW_TOLERANCE did. Filed as vg-137 and deliberately NOT fixed here: a different set of files, and a scope decision rather than this row's five. WHAT IS NOT CONCLUDED. Not that the display switch is wrong - nothing here argues against it. Not that `main` is green - the comparison is impossible, not merely unmeasured. Not that the suite's remaining zoom coupling is now fixed; the sabotage proves five instances are not. Not that a shift-click landing on a handle is ever a product bug; this one was measured and behaves correctly. THREE INTERMEDIATE READINGS IN THE INVESTIGATION WERE WRONG, each a confound in my own harness rather than a fact about the product, and recorded because the first is the dangerous shape. (1) 'Hiding any control fixes it' - every single-control trial read OK because the previous trial had hidden ALL controls and hiding is not undone by selecting another object; with visibility restored per trial plus a final no-hide control, only mt and mtr are implicated. (2) 'Pixel distance decides it' - a separation sweep was contaminated by a carried-over ActiveSelection, and a strict reset with expect.poll inverted the result. (3) 'The evaluate does it' - a no-op page.evaluate 'fixed' the click too, being the round trip's latency rather than the code it ran. A probe that makes the symptom disappear for a reason of its own is the failure mode worth writing down. Full method, numbers and the sabotage matrix: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-04-the-device-lens-plans/vg-136-report.md
check: npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1 green under playwright.config.ts, 252 passed / 0 failed / 0 flaky / 158 skipped with 410 collected asserted from test-results/summary.json rather than off the exit code. The three repaired specs at the default camera: snapping.spec.ts 38 passed / 0 failed, reference-theme.spec.ts band test passed, glass-authoring.spec.ts grouping test passed. Plus the sabotage pin: DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS = 9:19.5, rebuilt, and all three still pass.

title: Every card is refused on the host default theme, because refusing is safer than inserting an unresolved reference
detail: FOUND DURING REDESIGN PLAN 1 TASK 5. insertCard refuses a card whose globals the theme does not carry, rather than inserting it with an unresolved reference — because an unresolved reference reaches snapshot, which validates and throws, so inserting anyway gives an author a canvas that looks right and a save that fails for the rest of the session. Refusing is the right call against that failure. THE COST: on the host's default theme, whose palette carries two tokens, EVERY card refuses, and on a blank theme 7 of the 8 refuse, so the library is unusable exactly where an author is most likely to meet it first. Observed in a browser; the message names each missing token, so the failure is legible rather than silent. OPEN QUESTION, not a settled defect: whether a card should instead MAP onto the theme's palette — the nearest equivalent token, or a literal resolved at insert time — rather than refusing. That is a design decision about what a unit means when the document does not carry its tokens, and it is not made anywhere in the plan or either spec. Recorded so the cost is visible to whoever decides it. FIXED in be1f4d90: a card reference now resolves in three steps - the exact token, then the theme's own token for that role (surface or ink, read through new-object-defaults' existing paletteTokenRole rather than a second list), then a literal where the document format admits one. Every substitution is reported through errorManager naming each token, and the refusal survives for the one case nothing answers: a document with no palette at all. The refusal was never the bug - it was the safe half of the decision, and it was the only half. What was missing is that 'this theme has no token for palette.cpu' was never asked whether the theme has a CPU colour under another name. Measured by the pins: a theme whose ids are its own inserts the card, validateFabricThemeEnvelope answers ok, a surface never lands on an ink, nothing is said when every token was already there, and the no-palette theme is still refused.
check: inserted a CPU card into a theme whose palette lacks palette.cpu and read it back: the card is on the canvas, validateFabricThemeEnvelope on the saved envelope answers ok (so nothing unresolved reached it), the painted refs name the theme's own surface and ink rather than the card's frost and cpu, and errorManager.warn names palette.frost and palette.text as what they became. The no-palette theme still refuses, pinned separately.

title: The crop frame has no id and no export exclusion, so it appears in the layer panel as a row named unidentified
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 1 TASK 3 REVIEW, by probing outside the layer tree. crop-manager/index.ts builds the crop frame as new Rect({...}) with NO id and adds it to the canvas root, and layer-tree.ts:100 walks canvas.getObjects() with no excludeFromExport filter - unlike the serialisation path, which does filter. PROBE: PROBE_ROWS=["unidentified/unidentified","image-1/image-1"] and the id resolves to the frame. So an author mid-crop sees a phantom row literally named unidentified in the layer panel, and findById("unidentified") resolves to it. PRE-EXISTING and user-visible today; not introduced by grouping. FIX, and it is one line rather than the Map-keyed scheme: filter excludeFromExport at layer-tree.ts:100. That removes the phantom row AND makes the positional fallback counter genuinely unreachable - layer-tree numbers id-less objects positionally while findById and ownerOf walk the whole document, so the two agree only while both visit the same objects, an invariant currently held by a comment and a test rather than a type. With no id-less object reachable the invariant stops mattering, which is a smaller change than closing the invariant properly and buys more.
check: Mid-crop, the layer panel lists no row for the crop frame: a probe projects the scene with the frame present and reads the rows, and the frame id resolves to no object and findById("unidentified") is undefined rather than the frame. Both tests were verified red with the excludeFromExport filter disabled.

title: Two panels still carry controls with no id, because the assertion does not mount them
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-108, whose generalised assertion is the point of that row and also its limit. The audit mounts the selection inspector in two disjoint field sets and three other panels, and it found twelve controls needing an id - all fixed. But asset-manager/panel.ts's two asset file inputs and new-document-chooser.ts's one select carry no id and were never mounted, so the assertion does not see them. Worth a row rather than a line because it is the failure mode of every generalised test: it covers what its author thought to mount, and a panel added later is invisible to it. The honest fix is either to mount these two or to state which panels the assertion covers so the next person adding one knows they are opting out. Recorded as open rather than closed because "the test passes" and "every control has an id" are different claims and only the first is currently true.
check: The audit now mounts both panels, and the controls that carried no id are reachable by it: stripping the id from the new-document choosers select or from the asset panels select turns the audit red (four cases and three respectively), so a control with no id in either panel is a failed assertion rather than a panel nobody mounted.

title: The editor opens whichever theme ran last, so an author is handed a document they did not open and Save writes it over
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING THE RED, as a side effect of a host-player failure rather than by driving the product. editor/src/boot-theme.ts:36 answers a URL that names no theme with latestOwnTheme, which lists the host store and opens the entry with the newest updatedAt. updatedAt is the store file's mtime and carries no author identity, so on a shared or multi-author store the newest entry is whoever saved last - not the person at the keyboard. The author gets that document mounted, and the next Save to library writes their work over it, because nothing in the flow knows the document was not chosen. MEASURED on the e2e host store: booting /editor/ opened bar-0 through bar-4, a fixture another spec had saved, and Save to library then wrote that fixture back; the display asking for vigilia-demo-dashboard found nothing. The e2e workaround is a New from starter click before every save (saveStarterThroughTheHost), which names the document rather than trusting the boot. The product defect is the pairing, not the fallback: resuming the last save is a reasonable default for a single-author local store and a wrong one for anything shared, and there is no prompt, no indicator and no per-author scope to tell the two apart. The one-line alternative - prefer the starter when nothing names a theme - is NOT proposed here, because it would delete the documented round trip (close the tab, come back to the theme you were working on) that boot-theme.test.ts pins deliberately. What is needed is a decision about which store the editor assumes, and an answer that names the document it opened before a save can overwrite it. SEEN AGAIN, live, in this pass's own full serial run: the third run of host-player.spec.ts's chart-palette spec failed on toContainText reading 'Opened E2E media' where 'Saved to library' was expected. That is not a fixture another spec left behind - global-setup seeds e2e-media itself - so bootTheme's answer to a URL naming nothing depends on which seeded theme carries the newest mtime, and the same three actions produced 'New theme from the starter' in the other runs. Traced by recording every #status write with its timestamp across 8 boots: the boot write lands at ~400ms, the author's own action at ~1100ms, and the boot write is always first, so the editor is interactive ~600ms before its own status is settled. Nothing clobbered the author in 8 attempts, so this is a narrow window rather than a certain failure, but the row's measurement is no longer only about which document opens - it is also about a status line that an action can lose.
owner: editor/src/boot-theme.ts:36 latestOwnTheme, with the save path at editor/src/editor-session.ts #saveLibrary
check: A URL that names a theme this host does not have opens nothing: boot-theme is driven with a store holding one saved theme and the dead id, and it resolves undefined having called open exactly once with the bookmarked id and never listed. The bare-URL resume is untouched and still opens the authors own last save.

title: The chart-refresh submenu spec is a twenty-percent flake in the suite that gates merges
detail: FOUND DURING REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 1 REVIEW. tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts:672, "switches chart refresh between 30 and 1 FPS", is a roughly twenty-percent flake with no owner. MEASURED, both sides rather than assumed: HEAD with the new artboard clip, 10 samples, 10 passed 0 failed; HEAD rebuilt with the clip entirely removed and the flag verified absent from the bundle, 10 samples, 8 passed 2 failed. Earlier runs put it between roughly 0 and 40 percent. The failure is element(s) not found, waiting for getByRole('menuitem', { name: /Chart refresh: 1 FPS/ }) - a timing race on a submenu re-open, not an interaction with anything the redesign changed. So the clip did not cause it. WHY IT STILL MATTERS: a flaky spec in the suite that gates merges is a real defect, and a flaky spec is precisely what erodes trust in the sabotage evidence a change like this rests on. The word "pre-existing" was used about it and is wrong here for two reasons: this repo does not treat it as a category, and the branch was fully green at 38245e60 - 234 passed, 0 failed - one cycle before, so it cannot be assumed settled either. Needs an owner and a determinism fix; the surface to look at is the submenu re-open, not the chart setting.
check: The chart refresh spec is no longer a flake in the suite that gates merges: switched between 30 and 1 FPS on repeat-each 24 gives 48 collected and 48 passed, where an unmodified tree gave 3 failures in 12 and 3 in 24. The re-open click is gone because picking the radio leaves the View menu open, and the label is read in the menu the author is looking at.

title: Binding a first series to a chart empties its own property panel, so an author cannot set the series colour
detail: THE CAUSE AS FILED WAS WRONG, and saying so is the point of this row. It claimed the envelope declares bindings as a flat array in renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts and that EditorSession.#addBindings disagrees with it. Neither is true: the envelope is a record at renderer-core/src/theme/fabric-envelope.ts:34 (readonly bindings?: Readonly<Record<string, readonly Binding[]>>), the validator enforces that shape at fabric-envelope-validate.ts:790 ("bindings must be an object keyed by Fabric object id"), and #addBindings spreads additions into that record correctly. So there was no shape disagreement, nothing to decide, and no reuse-gate note owed. THE REAL CAUSE IS THE PAINT FILTER, in packages/editor/src/chart-manager/index.ts carriedPaintFor. It kept a paint entry only when the series at that index survived, walking previous - so binding the FIRST series (previous empty) kept nothing, and unbinding the LAST one emptied it from the other side. seriesPaintFor then regrew the empty array by repeating current.at(-1), which is undefined, so the envelope carried palette: [null] and the panel rendered no colour control: an author who bound a series to a chart could not then choose its colour. MEASURED, by execution rather than by reading: carriedPaintFor("line", {palette:[{ref:"palette.series"}]}, [], [b1]) returned palette [] where the entry should have been kept. The fix keeps an entry unless the series it paints is known to be gone, and never returns an empty array where seriesPaintFor would regrow it from undefined. SABOTAGE, both surfaces: in the browser spec, with the old filter restored and the bundle rebuilt, the chart panel loses its content on the bind and the spec fails; with the fix it passes.
owner: packages/editor/src/chart-manager/index.ts carriedPaintFor, with seriesPaintFor as the regrow that made the empty array a null entry
check: A chart still offers the series colour after a series is bound to it: the e2e inserts a Line chart from the Add pane, reads the chart property panel on the Data tab, and asserts data-vigilia-chart-paint="palette.0" is still present after choosing cpu.load in data-vigilia-chart-binding-add - the [stroke, palette.0] to [] DOM read the row was filed from. Restoring the old filter and rebuilding fails it.

title: The artboard is not a clipping area, and neither repair is free
detail:
Fabric has no scene-level clip: clipPath is per-object and serialised through cacheProperties, so it collides with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and with the derived text-box clip. Two candidate repairs, both with consequences — a scene Group wrapper changes what canvas.getObjects() means, which is the layer tree's and every walk over it. A decision, not a patch. Related: a selection handle should stay fully visible when its object is clipped (the user's own requirement in the same report).

 CROSS-LINK, re-opened deliberately rather than withdrawn: this row is the constraint analysis the redesign's clipping work MUST respect, so closing it would delete the engineering. My own measurement on 2026-09-02/03 found the editor's Fabric canvas carries no clipPath while the player's adapter does, so the editor does not clip at the artboard and an author composes against a preview that disagrees with the phone. The redesign commits to fixing that, but this row says the obvious fixes collide with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and the derived text-box clip - which is exactly the trap a naive implementation walks into. Keep this row until the artboard clip is measured and demonstrably collides with neither the crop manager's authored per-image clip nor the derived text-box clip — the same overhang put through the editor and the player and compared, because a collision that is not measured is not disproved. STATUS.md now states this same criterion rather than the looser 'once player-side parity is measured'. MEASURED, 2026-10-06, which is what this row was waiting for and which no reading of the source could settle: a DOM clip is deliberately invisible to canvas.getObjects(), so the collision had to be settled on rendered pixels. One document carried through the editor and the player, comparing both. THE CROP MANAGER'S AUTHORED PER-IMAGE CLIP: the discarded half is 0 px of red/blue on both surfaces and the kept half runs x 762.1 to 800.0 in the editor against 760.4 to 800.0 in the player - the scene-level clip INTERSECTS the authored crop rather than truncating, shifting or replacing it. NO COLLISION. THE DERIVED TEXT-BOX CLIP: ink stops at y 109.2 against a box bottom of 110 while an unclipped twin of the same glyphs runs to 277.2, and both boxes are cut at the same x - the derived clip still cuts its own box and the artboard clip cuts both alike. NO COLLISION. Largest editor/player disagreement on any measured edge is 3.3 scene units, an anti-aliased glyph tail at two scales; every colour edge the clips own agrees to within 1.1. NO REPAIR OWED, so none was made - which is the outcome the plan chose the DOM route to reach, since a scene Group wrapper would have changed what getObjects() means to every walk in the editor. A FACT THE ROW'S FRAMING HAD BACKWARDS: the derived text clip is the FRAGILE one and the authored crop the ROBUST one. Clobbering every object clipPath in applyArtboardPaint heals the derived clip within a single 30fps applyAuthoredText pass, because it re-derives itself; an authored crop has no such pass and stays clobbered. So if this shape ever regresses, the derived clip is where to look, not the crop.
check: clip-parity.spec.ts puts one overhanging cropped image and one text box whose derived clip cuts its own box through the editor and the player, and compares the pixels: the crop's discarded half is 0 px on both surfaces, the kept half starts on the badge's midline and stops on the artboard edge, the derived clip still stops the clipped box at 110 while its unclipped twin runs to 277, and both boxes are cut at the same x. The largest editor/player disagreement is 3.3 scene units. Sabotaged with the artboard rect landing on each object and both tests go red on the clip's own assertion.

title: The rebuild journey asks for a 405 degree gauge end angle and the shared settings field lands it on 360
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3 TASK 7, running the rebuild spec as its browser gate. tests/e2e/author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:516 builds the two memory rings, fills [data-vigilia-chart-setting="endAngle"] with 405 for ram-gauge, and asserts the object carries startAngle 135, endAngle 405, roundCap true. Measured, the object carries endAngle 360. ISOLATED AND REAL, NOT MACHINE LOAD: run alone on a box at 87% with another session browsers on it, the spec times out at 30s inside addChart, and with --timeout=120000 it clears every wait and stops at the assertion - 360 where 405 was asked for. CAUSE, ESTABLISHED AND IN ONE OWNER: the gauge endAngle descriptor bounds the value at min -360 / max 360 (renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts, the bound has been there since 7a32656e), and f254259b moved the Data tab settings loop onto settingsField, which reuses the inspector numberField and LANDS an out-of-range value on the bound. The loop it replaced (panel.ts at f254259b^) set the min/max attributes but wrote Number(input.value) with no bound check at all, so 405 reached the settings and the assertion passed. So Task 6 turned this assertion red without touching the assertion. WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS A DESIGN DECISION, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: either the descriptor bound is too narrow - the renderer draws a 270 degree sweep from 135 to 405, and the sweep is angles rather than a coordinate - or the journey is asking a gauge to hold a number its descriptor says it cannot. NOT TASK 7S: Task 7 rebuilt the selection inspector right column; the control that refuses is the Data tab chart panel, which Task 7 did not touch. TWO SAMPLES OF THE SAME SUITE, FOR WHOEVER CHASES THE TIMEOUTS: the full rebuild spec run twice with --workers=1 failed 4 of 9 and then 3 of 9 with DIFFERENT tests red each time (geometry fills the first time, tab clicks and the series chooser the second), which is what a loaded box looks like rather than a broken spec.

 RESOLVED BY TASK 9, 2026-10-06, in the direction the measurement chose: the journey is corrected to 45 and the descriptor bound is left alone. The plan offered two directions and assumed the first would win — that 405 draws something a canonical angle cannot — and the canvas says it does not, so the assertion was asking for a document that cannot exist; the field that refuses 405 is the enforcing control and is right. The other direction was also unavailable here: it would need renderer-core, which Task 9 is forbidden to touch.
check: npx playwright test --config playwright.rebuild.config.ts -g "the two memory rings: a partial gauge and a full one" fills [data-vigilia-chart-setting="endAngle"] with 45 for ram-gauge and reads the object back as startAngle 135, endAngle 45, roundCap true — 9 of 9 rebuild tests pass. MEASURED BOTH WAYS ON THE CANVAS BEFORE THE JOURNEY WAS CORRECTED, because the plan asserted the opposite: buildGaugeOption hands startAngle and endAngle to ECharts raw (renderer-core/src/charts/gauge.ts), and ECharts reduces both mod 360, so 135 to 405 and 135 to 45 render the same arc. Of 2087 opaque pixels, 135/405 against 135/45 differ by 0, as do 135/405 against -225/45 and 135/405 against -225/405; 135/405 against 135/360 differs by 1337, which is the control that shows the comparison can tell two arcs apart.

title: A pie cannot be given a fixed total, so its remainder is unreachable
detail:
FOUND WHILE WRITING THE REDESIGN SPEC. renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts is headed "Every scalar setting, per family" and mostly is, but PieSettings.total has no descriptor in CHART_SETTINGS_FIELDS.pie. PieTotal is { kind: sum } or { kind: fixed, value }, and a fixed total is what makes the remainder measurable - computeComposition reports knownTotal, whole, remainder, overflow and complete against it. Without the field an author cannot choose it, so the RAM/VRAM/storage donut-with-a-measurable-remainder case is unreachable even though the renderer supports it. FIXTURE-CHECKED against PieSettings: the other ten keys are present. Related: vg-122.

 RESOLVED BY PLAN 3 TASK 3 (84b11f51), 2026-10-06: pie gains two descriptors, total (a select over sum | fixed) and total.value (a number carrying path [total, value] and visibleWhen total.kind === fixed), for every family; the nested write goes through writeSetting in renderer-core/src/charts/settings-path.ts, which is what makes computeComposition see the author's choice. Browser-measured on the canvas in Task 10 (8b4274b7). The completeness gate that hid this row (NON_SCALAR_SETTINGS) was deleted in Task 4 (1d536762), so a settings key with no descriptor is now a failing test rather than a review habit.
check: src/web/tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts:359 "draws a remainder slice for a fixed pie total, measured on the canvas" sets a fixed total on the starter pie and measures the canvas inside the object's own rect over palette.frost: 0 before, >1000 after, 0 after switching back to sum. Unit half re-run at HEAD: npx vitest run packages/renderer-core/src/charts/settings-path.test.ts, 13/13, including "makes the renderer see the author's fixed total", which writes total=fixed and total.value=64 through writeSetting and asserts computeComposition gives knownTotal 32, remainder 64 - 32 and whole 64 — the descriptor's path is the path the renderer reads, which is what the row said was unreachable.

title: Chart animation is unreachable from the editor on every family
detail:
FOUND WHILE WRITING THE REDESIGN SPEC. AnimationSettings is an optional key on LineSettings, BarSettings, PieSettings and GaugeSettings, and it has no descriptor in CHART_SETTINGS_FIELDS for any family, so an author cannot reach it. The other three holes in the same audit were closed: pie total is vg-121, and validate.ts validateSettingsRange duplicating min/max rather than reading this table is recorded in the settings-fields.ts header as the next step and closes both problems at once.

 RESOLVED BY PLAN 3 TASK 3 (84b11f51), 2026-10-06: every family gains four animation descriptors one level down, animation.durationMs, animation.easing, animation.appearMs and animation.appearEasing, with the two appear fields marked advanced; writeSetting materialises the whole AnimationSettings block from defaultAnimationSettings, the object toEngineAnimation already falls back to, so an author's one field never leaves a partial block. No on/off toggle was added, because animate defaults to true at all four toEngineAnimation call sites, so an absent block means the defaults apply rather than the chart is static. Browser-measured in Task 10 (8b4274b7).

Unit half re-run at HEAD: npx vitest run packages/renderer-core/src/charts/settings-path.test.ts, 13/13, including "is what the pie's engine option reads, for all four fields" (buildPieOption returns animationDurationUpdate 2400, animationEasingUpdate quinticInOut, animationDuration 800, animationEasing cubicInOut) and "lands where the descriptor says, for every family" — so the editor reaches animation on all four families, not just the one.

title: PUT /api/hosting never reaches the wire: closeAllConnections() destroys the connection its own response is owed on, so the editor's LAN control flips on and then shows no address, no code and no expiry
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 3.4, which could not land its browser spec because of it, and reproduced here at 7e9f1869 against a real host rather than taken from the agent's report. `node packages/host/bin/vigilia.js --no-browser --port 4399` answers GET /api/hosting with {"lan":false,"address":null,"port":4399,"sessions":[]}; a PUT {"lan":true} returns curl exit 52 with http_code 000 -- an empty reply, not a refusal; the GET after it answers {"lan":true,"address":"192.168.2.56","port":4399,"sessions":[]}. The socket moves and the answer is destroyed. ROOT CAUSE, established rather than suspected. src/web/packages/host/src/cli/hosting.ts:68 calls server.closeAllConnections() while server.ts:706 is awaiting toggled(body.lan) inside the PUT handler. That call destroys every connection on the server, and the one the response is owed on is one of them, so the response is never written. Plan 6's Task 3.2 Constraint prescribed exactly this -- 'Live SSE connections are closed on the way through (closeAllConnections())' -- which is why it landed; the plan is corrected in the commit that files this. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY. The fix needs a design decision. A single http.Server cannot rebind while answering the request that asked for the rebind: server.close() waits for every connection to end, and the answering connection will not end until the answer is written, so the outcome of the move cannot be in the answer that triggered it. Every remedy therefore changes the shape of the exchange, and the two candidates are not equivalent: (a) answer first, move after, and let the editor read the settled state from a following GET /api/hosting -- preserves §145's posture exactly (nothing but this PC can connect until the control is used) at the cost of a client re-read that must tolerate the 4 ms the socket is closed; measured on this machine with a probe: closeIdleConnections() then server.close() completes 1 ms after a full keep-alive response, and the rebind to 0.0.0.0 on the same port lands at 4 ms. (b) bind 0.0.0.0 for the process's whole life and refuse non-loopback peers at the socket, so the socket never moves -- rejected here because it makes LAN exposure the default rather than an opt-in and moves the firewall prompt to startup, which is a security-posture decision and therefore the user's, not an agent's. The blast radius is cli/hosting.ts, server.ts, hosting-client.ts and publish-control.tsx. It was filed expecting Task 3.2's unit tests to need rewriting, because they assert setLan resolves {ok:false, reason}; that expectation was WRONG and Task 3.4 refuted it by leaving cli/hosting.test.ts untouched -- setLan still resolves that shape, and it is the route that stopped awaiting it. CLEARED ON 2026-10-07 by Task 3.4 (9cd76a0b), host side verified against a real host rather than from the agent's report: PUT /api/hosting now answers 200 in both directions where it answered curl exit 52 and http_code 000, lan:true carries address 192.168.2.56, and a squatted port answers 200 with the pre-move state and reports the refusal in the host's own words on the next GET. STILL OPEN because the row's editor-side claim -- that the control flips on and then shows no address, no code and no expiry -- is only unit-tested so far; Task 3.5's browser spec is what proves it in a real browser, and it is red until that runs. WHAT IT COSTS TODAY. The control is unusable in both directions, and Task 3.4's predicted failure mode is wrong on the real path. fetch rejects on the destroyed connection, so hosting-client.ts:98-103 catches it and returns {ok:false, reason:'Failed to fetch'}; publish-control.tsx:69-79 then re-reads the host, which now answers from the moved socket with lan:true, so aria-pressed flips to TRUE (the plan predicted it would never flip) and the early return skips mintSession(), so the address, the code and the expiry never appear and the author is shown a network error instead. A refusal is destroyed the same way, so the host's own 409 words -- the thing Task 3.3 says only the host can supply -- cannot reach the reader either. ONE CLAIM IN THIS ROW WAS ITSELF A MISTAKE AND IS KEPT RATHER THAN QUIETLY EDITED, because it sent the plan wrong twice. The aria-pressed-true-with-no-address signature above is what the OLD defect did, on the failure path: the PUT never answered, so the control re-read a host that had already moved. It is NOT what a stalled setLan does on the break path, where the PUT answers 200 and the control honestly reverts. Task 3.5's break-proof, run twice, showed aria-pressed staying "false" -- the plan's ORIGINAL expectation was right and the correction of it was the error.
check: The editor's LAN control shows an address and a code: `cd src/web && npx playwright test tests/e2e/publish-header.spec.ts --workers=1` is 3/3 green (`expected 3, unexpected 0`, 25.5 s) on the spec committed red at ea1eb097 and left unedited -- the cases being `the LAN is turned on from the editor, and the port does not move`, `the header carries the address and a code for it`, and `a forwarded-for header does not move the guard off the socket`. Host side re-measured independently at 6bec889c rather than taken from the agent: `PUT /api/hosting` answers 200 in both directions where it answered curl exit 52 and http_code 000.

title: A themed artboard whose paint is a palette reference renders unpainted on the hosted display, so the phone shows black where the editor shows paper
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 4.5, which needed a display screenshot showing the published document and produced a black frame instead. THE CHAIN. The hosted display is `startHostedTheme` (player/src/main.ts:279), and it built its plan with `envelopePlan`, which passed `theme.artboard.background` and `theme.artboard.barColor` straight through unresolved and without globals. scene-fabric/src/artboard-paint.ts:40-46 accepts only a string, a kind:"solid" or a gradient and returns "none" for anything else, so adapter.ts:265-270 set `canvas.backgroundColor = ""`, and mount.ts:79-81 left the artboard element `transparent` and the host `#000` -- so the whole page read black, artboard and bars alike, while the editor shows paper for the same document. ROOT CAUSE, and why it is not a one-line fix: there were TWO builders of a ScenePlan, and only one resolved. `buildScenePlan` resolves its artboard through `resolveStyleValue` (plan.ts:191-202) and `plan.test.ts:82-92` pinned it; `envelopePlan` was the other, and no test drove the hosted path, so nothing reddened. A REFUTATION WAS ATTEMPTED HERE AND WAS WRONG, and is kept because it is the trap. The controller read player/src/main.ts:165 and plan.test.ts:82-92 -- both the FIXTURE path -- and concluded the row was a false positive. `buildScenePlan` serves the demo/fixture display; the hosted phone uses `envelopePlan`. A reader who stops at `buildScenePlan` refutes a correct finding. THE FIX, 72edf30e. `planArtboard(artboard, globals, issues)` is now the one owner of artboard geometry and both paints, exported from renderer-core; `buildScenePlan` (plan.ts:186) and the player's hosted path both call it, so a third builder cannot be written that forgets. `envelopePlan` moved out of main.ts into player/src/hosted-plan.ts, because main.ts runs the display at import time and a test cannot import it -- that untestability is the gap the defect lived in. The player's `?? "#000"` fallbacks were removed: they were applied BEFORE resolution, so a reference was always truthy and never defaulted anyway; absent paint is now `undefined`, matching the fixture path and the editor, and an unresolved reference is reported as a plan issue instead of being passed through. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN. That a real phone, at a real distance, in real light, shows it -- the capture is a phone-sized Chromium, not a phone. The gradient form of a resolved artboard paint is unchanged and covered by scene-fabric's own adapter tests, not re-proved here.
check: The hosted display paints a palette reference: the registered capture docs/evidence/screenshots/publish-loop-live-publish.png, taken at 72edf30e with `cd src/web && VIGILIA_CAPTURE=1 npx playwright test --project=own-host --grep "an edit reaches the display" --workers=1` [RENAMED 2026-10-13 by Task 5.3: the Playwright project this command names was `publish` when the command ran and is `own-host` today. The group took in `editor-invalid-theme.spec.ts`, a spec about booting over a broken theme rather than publishing one, so `publish` had become a misnomer; the rename is `playwright.config.ts`'s `OWN_HOST_SPEC`.] (expected 1, unexpected 0, 25.9 s), shows the paper band #e8e4da between #101318 bars at 390x292 -- exactly 4:3, which is the PUBLISHED 320x240 and not the stored 640x360, whose 16:9 letterboxed in 390 px would be 390x219. Before the fix the same spec's test-results/publish/display-390.png at f0c7ff50 is a black frame carrying only the connection banner. The artboard element's paint is a Fabric canvas draw colour, invisible to getComputedStyle, which is why the check reads pixels rather than a computed value.

title: Escape with the `?` sheet open also exits the group, because the modal guard queries the DOM after a Radix dialog has already unmounted itself
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.1 OF PLAN 7, the browser proof, and it is that task's own second test failing on the untouched bundle at `ebb4086b`. Filed as [issue #32](https://github.com/peterng1618/vigilia/issues/32). THE MEASUREMENT, REPRODUCED BY THE ROOT: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/keyboard.spec.ts --workers=1` gives `1 failed, 2 skipped, 1 passed`, and the failure is `keyboard.spec.ts:98`, `locator('[data-vigilia-layer="cpu-card"]')` -> `Expected: visible`, `Error: element(s) not found`. The first test in the same file passes, so the bundle and the harness are sound. WHAT THE AUTHOR SEES: they enter a group, press `?` to open the shortcut reference, press Escape, and the sheet closes **and the canvas leaves the group** -- the layer rows change under them. One press, two effects, which is the outcome `isModalOpen()` exists to prevent; its own comment at `shortcut-manager/index.ts:99-120` names it verbatim. THE DOCUMENT IS SAFE: `Delete` and `Ctrl+Z` are correctly deferred, measured by the executor at 20 samples over 1s each with the row count unchanged, and the root read those samples rather than re-running them. THE CAUSE IS ESTABLISHED AND THE ROOT VERIFIED EVERY LINK OF IT: (1) `@radix-ui/react-dismissable-layer/dist/index.mjs` binds Escape with `ownerDocument.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown, { capture: true })`; (2) `ShortcutManager` binds `window` in the bubble phase (`shortcut-manager/index.ts:148`), and document-capture precedes window-bubble; (3) Radix's handler calls `onDismiss()` synchronously; (4) `@radix-ui/react-presence/dist/index.mjs` unmounts from a `useLayoutEffect` when `getComputedStyle(node).animationName === "none"`, and layout effects run before propagation finishes; (5) so `isModalOpen()` answers false and `view.exit-group` fires. WHY THE JSDOM TEST IS GREEN, measured by the root on jsdom 26.1.0: `getComputedStyle(div[role=dialog]).animationName` is `""` and `el.getAnimations` is `undefined`, so `"" !== "none"` and `Presence` never takes the synchronous-unmount branch -- the dialog stays mounted for the whole dispatch and the guard answers true. The unit test therefore passes for a reason that does not exist in a browser, the same shape as the tooltip flicker `tooltip.ts:20-31` records. NOT A NATIVE-DIALOG PROBLEM: the three native `<dialog>`s `preventDefault` Escape on the dialog element itself (`new-document-chooser.ts:418`, `theme-library-dialog.ts:95,282,389`), which is inside the bubble path, and a native dialog is only removed after dispatch -- so the guard is correct for them. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY: the behaviour is specified and the mechanism is not, and the candidates have different blast radii. Deferring on `event.defaultPrevented` is small and general -- Radix calls `preventDefault()` before `onDismiss()` -- but it makes `preventDefault` mean *handled* for the whole manager, so a future handler that cancels a key's default would silently disable a product binding; today the only sites that `preventDefault` a manager-bound key are the layer panel's arrows (`layer-panel.tsx:605-606`), which also `stopPropagation`, so the rule changes nothing -- a coupling rather than a guarantee. Sampling the DOM at window-capture with a pure observer fixes it generally at the cost of a second listener. Moving the manager's own listener to an earlier phase is REJECTED and is not a repair: the layer panel defers arrow keys with `stopPropagation()` in a React `onKeyDown` (`layer-panel.tsx:601-608`) which the manager currently never sees, so an earlier manager would nudge the selection and navigate the list at once. Having the sheet `stopPropagation()` from `onEscapeKeyDown` is rejected as the primary mechanism because it is a per-surface patch that does not generalise to the next Radix Dialog. It blocks plan 7: Task 4.1 cannot land green, and its `keyboard-reference` capture cannot be produced because the test fails before `captureVisualReview`.
check: The `?` sheet's Escape no longer exits the group: the browser test `tests/e2e/keyboard.spec.ts` -> "? opens the sheet, and the document behind it does not change", run at `26231c4a` with `cd src/web && PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME=test-results/keyboard-verify.json npx playwright test tests/e2e/keyboard.spec.ts --workers=1 --reporter=json`, reports `passed 2, skipped 2, failed 0` (the skips are `phone-chromium`, which `isDesktopSurface` guards by design). Its final assertion is `expect(selected).toBeVisible()` on `[data-vigilia-layer="cpu-card"]` after the Escape — the row that is unmounted if `view.exit-group` also fires. Before the fix the same command at `4cc45883` reports `1 failed, 2 skipped, 1 passed`, failing at that line with `element(s) not found`; the root re-ran both. The jsdom half is `shortcut-manager/index.dom.test.ts` -> "asks about the dialog before the same dispatch that tears it down", which the root broke by reverting the guard to `isModalOpen()` and restored: `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`, 33/34, against 34/34 green.

title: packages/player/index.html cites requirement §151, which requirements.md does not define, so the comment pointing at the authority for fullscreen and wake-lock finds nothing
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8'S AUTHORING PASS while checking the handles its design would touch, and verified here against the docs rather than taken from the report. `src/web/packages/player/index.html:6` reads `§151: mobile fullscreen and keeping the screen awake are browser-dependent.` (the copy under `packages/player/dist/` is build output and has the same line). THE MARKER HAS NO TARGET: `docs/product/requirements.md` marks its requirements as `## §N -- title` headings (`## §7 -- Product and scope`, `## §31 -- One renderer, shared`), and the substring `151` occurs **nowhere in that file at all** -- not as a marker, not in prose, not in a list. Nor does `§151` appear in any other document under docs/. So a reader who follows the citation to find out what was actually required of fullscreen and wake-lock arrives at nothing. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY, and this is the whole reason: the cause is not established. The marker numbering is not a contiguous sequence -- 48 distinct markers are present and the highest is §175 -- so an absent §151 means either the citation was always wrong, or the requirement it meant was renumbered, or the requirement was removed. AGENTS.md says markers are stable and never renumbered, which rules out the second only if the rule was always kept. Picking a replacement number would be a guess at which requirement covers browser-dependent fullscreen and wake-lock, and the citation is the only clue. The honest fix is to find the requirement that owns that fact, or to drop the citation and state the fact on its own authority -- and that is a lookup, not a rename. Cosmetic in effect, and it blocks nothing: no test reads it, nothing renders differently, and the sentence beside it is true regardless. It is filed because a dangling authority is how a marker stops meaning anything, and because plan 8 names it in three places and would otherwise be the only record of it -- plans are archived, the register is not.
check: The dangling §151 citation is gone and the comment's own substance stands: `cd src/web && grep -n '§151' packages/player/index.html` prints nothing and exits 1, and the marker the comment still carries, `§57`, resolves — `grep -n '§57' packages/player/index.html` prints line 8 and `grep -n '^## §57' ../../docs/product/requirements.md` prints `89:## §57 — Geometry`. Task 1.1's own Constraints block ordered the removal (`do not carry a citation to a marker that is not there`), and the diff at the artefact sha is the line: `-      §151: mobile fullscreen and keeping the screen awake are browser-dependent.` replaced by the same sentence with no marker.

title: The right column does not empty on deselect, which the redesign ruled it must
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 4 TASK 10, writing the composition panel browser contract. The redesign spec rules this under Ruled during review, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:552: "The right column empties on deselect." The product does not do it. selection-inspector/index.ts:325 documents target() as "The object to describe: the live selection, else the last one still present", and :346-353 returns the last bound object whenever objectById still finds its id, clearing only once the object is gone from the document. So clicking empty canvas leaves the column describing the object that was selected. MEASURED at 42169371: the spec Task 10 landed asserts the products real rule instead and reaches the empty state by deleting the object it describes, while the plans own Task 10 verification bullet still says "deselecting empties it again" - so the plan and the test beside it now contradict each other. LEFT OPEN RATHER THAN CHANGED because which side is right is a design decision: keeping the last object is deliberate and documented, and clearing it would remove the fields an author is mid-read. Cross-reference vg-148 and vg-158, which are the same column binding disagreeing with the document. SHARPENED BY PLAN 7 TASK 4.2's WALK, which separated two states the row did not distinguish: **on open, with nothing ever selected, the clause HOLDS** -- `[data-vigilia-nothing-selected]` is visible reading 'Select an object to inspect it.' and there are zero `[data-vigilia-name]` controls; **after selecting and then clicking the empty stage** the clause FAILS -- the marker's count is 0 and the name field's is 1, so the column still describes the object it was describing. Screenshot `C:/Users/peter/AppData/Local/Temp/vigilia-walk/walk-after-deselect-desktop-chromium.png`, inspected by the root: the column shows Name `cpu-card` with Fill `Frosted panel` while the canvas shows no selection and the dock shows the arrange half alone.
