title: The Radix menu packages export no Anchor, so two pointer-anchored editor surfaces cannot migrate off Base UI and plan 9 Phase 1 stops at its own Step 4
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 9 TASK 1.1, whose whole product was this measurement, on 2026-10-08. THE PLAN'S OWN STOP CONDITION IS MET: `docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-07-chrome-and-appearance.md` Step 4 reads "**If `Anchor` is not exported, or `virtualRef` does not position a `DropdownMenu.Content` opened without a Trigger: stop this phase and report.**" It is not exported. THE MEASUREMENT, from a temporary jsdom probe mounted and read before being deleted, and confirmed against the installed packages' own `.d.ts` files rather than from memory: `"Anchor" in DropdownMenu === false` and `"Anchor" in ContextMenu === false`, with the full export lists carrying `Root, Trigger, Portal, Content, Group, Label, Item, CheckboxItem, RadioGroup, RadioItem, ItemIndicator, Separator, Arrow, Sub, SubTrigger, SubContent` and their `DropdownMenu*`/`ContextMenu*` aliases. The `.d.ts` of `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu@2.1.25` (MIT) and `@radix-ui/react-context-menu@2.3.8` (MIT) contain the string `Anchor` in **no file at all**, while `@radix-ui/react-popper@1.3.7` (MIT) and `@radix-ui/react-menu@2.1.25` (MIT) both export one -- so the capability the plan wanted exists one layer down and is not reachable from the packages the plan installs. WHY IT MATTERS: two of the five surfaces are anchored **not** to a trigger -- the Insert chooser anchors to the `+` in the pane bar, and the canvas context menu anchors to a pointer position through a synthetic `getBoundingClientRect` -- and Radix positions content to its Trigger. `@radix-ui/react-menu` does export `MenuAnchor`, so a hand-wired `<MenuPrimitive.Anchor virtualRef={...}>` inside a `DropdownMenu.Root` is a third mechanism and is what Step 4 forbids; it would also reach into a package that is not a declared dependency of `@vigilia/editor`. THE OTHER THREE ANSWERS, recorded here because the probe is deleted and they are Tasks 1.2 and 1.4's input: (2) `data-state` is `closed`/`open` on the Trigger, a plain `<button>` with no `role`; `role="menu"` with `data-state="open"` on the Content; and `data-state="checked"` on the `ItemIndicator`, a `<span>`. (3) Radix sets `aria-labelledby` itself, pointing at its own content id, and a caller's `aria-label` **survives beside it** -- measured `aria-label="with a caller label"` together with `aria-labelledby="radix-_r_3_"` -- so a caller passing a label gets both attributes and `aria-labelledby` wins the accessible name. A Content with no caller label reads `aria-label` null. (4) Radix publishes `--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height` and `--radix-context-menu-content-available-height` on the Content's inline style, each as `var(--radix-popper-available-height)` -- the direct replacement for the Base UI `--available-height` at `editor-shell.css:368` -- and a `forceMount`ed Content under an uncontrolled closed Root **is not in the document** (no marker, zero `[role="menu"]`), which is the Portal that carries the mount and not the Content. THE DECISION THIS NEEDS IS NOT AN AGENT'S: whether the three trigger-anchored menus migrate to Radix and leave both libraries in the manifest for the two pointer-anchored surfaces, whether the phase is abandoned and Base UI stays for all five, or whether the two surfaces get a decision note. The packages are installed (`@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu@2.1.25`, `@radix-ui/react-context-menu@2.3.8`, both MIT, licence rows added) and nothing consumes them yet. RESOLVED 2026-10-08, AND NOT BY THE MEASUREMENT CHANGING: Radix's menu packages still export no `Anchor`. What changed is that the phase no longer asks them to. The user ruled for Base UI after the widened survey was put in front of them (decision 0038, commit a47fac7c), which is this row's own second option -- Base UI stays for the pointer-anchored surfaces -- extended to all five, and the three Radix wrapper files move the other way instead. The two menu packages installed for the stopped Phase 1 are out of the manifest and out of node_modules, consumed by nothing, so the unresolved half of this row ('the packages are installed and nothing consumes them yet') is gone as well. The four probe answers recorded above -- the data-state shape, the aria-labelledby behaviour, the --radix-*-content-available-height variables, and the forceMount/Portal result -- are kept because they are the evidence for why Radix was rejected, and the probe itself is deleted. Closing this row is bookkeeping on a decision the user made; the decision was never an agent's to take, which is what this row said at the time.
check: The plan no longer installs either Radix menu package and no source imports one, so the two pointer-anchored surfaces are not migrating and the phase is not stopped: a walk of src/web for *.ts/*.tsx/*.json finds no file naming @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu or @radix-ui/react-context-menu (0 hits), and packages/editor/package.json lists only @radix-ui/react-dialog and @radix-ui/react-popover on the Radix side. The direction is the committed note docs/decisions/0038-base-ui-is-the-editors-one-primitive-library-on-the-users-ruling.md, which records the user's ruling that Base UI stays for the pointer anchor -- the option this row named as its second -- so the Anchor measurement above stands as true and stops being a blocker. Plan 9's Phase 1 is rewritten to three tasks that move the three Radix wrapper files to Base UI instead. npm run backlog:check passes on the row before it moves to the archive.

title: The palette colour picker announces a slider to assistive tech and cannot be operated from the keyboard
detail: FOUND WHILE RUNNING THE WIDENED PRIMITIVE-LIBRARY SURVEY, checking whether a shipped colour primitive would buy anything over the hand-rolled one at src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/colour-picker.tsx. THE MEASUREMENT: the file s Track component (lines 44-64) renders a div carrying role="slider", tabIndex={0}, aria-label={testId} and aria-valuenow={Math.round(value * 100)}, and binds only onPointerDown and onPointerMove. There is no onKeyDown anywhere in the 221-line file -- grep for onKeyDown|keydown returns nothing. So the four tracks (saturation/brightness area, hue, and the two alpha and value strips) each take a tab stop, tell a screen reader "slider, 42 percent", and then do nothing for any key the author presses. THE ROLE ALSO PROMISES MORE THAN IS PRESENT: role=slider requires aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax, and neither is set, so the announced range is undefined rather than 0-100. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY: the fix is a design decision with two owners. Adding onKeyDown with arrow-key stepping is a small, specified change inside this one file; but the alternative -- replacing the hand-rolled tracks with a primitive library s colour area, which is one of the options the survey is weighing (React Aria Components ships ColorArea/ColorSlider/ColorField with APG keyboard behaviour, Ark UI ships an equivalent, Base UI ships none) -- throws the same 221 lines away, and neither incumbent primitive library is installed today. Fixing it by hand and then migrating would be doing the work twice, and which way it goes depends on a decision that is still open. Filed as its own row the way vg-026 was, rather than folded into the library note, because it is a defect in shipped code that exists independently of which library wins: if the survey concludes the hand-rolled picker stays, this row is still true and still needs the keyboard path. SEVERITY IS LOW IN PRACTICE AND REAL IN PRINCIPLE: an author using only a mouse is unaffected, and no test covers it; the harm is the one AGENTS.md s accessibility rule names, a control advertising an affordance it does not have. SAME CLASS AS vg-169, the + chooser that cannot dismiss itself after announcing that it can. FIXED 2026-10-08 BY PLAN 9 TASK 1.2, AND THE DECISION THIS ROW WAS WAITING ON LANDED THE OTHER WAY FROM THE SURVEY'S SHORTLIST. The row was filed because the fix depended on which primitive library won: React Aria shipped a colour family that would have deleted these 221 lines, Ark UI shipped an equivalent, and Base UI ships none. **The user ruled for Base UI (decision 0038, commit 0da34313), so the picker stays hand-rolled and the defect became ours to close by hand** -- which is the cost that ruling recorded rather than argued away. WHAT LANDED: `Track` gains an `onKeyDown` that steps 1% on ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and ArrowUp/ArrowDown, goes to 0 on Home and 100 on End, clamps rather than wrapping, calls `preventDefault` only for the keys it owns, and carries `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` beside the `aria-valuenow` that was already there. Two further things went with it in the same file: the popover moved from `@radix-ui/react-popover` to Base UI's `Popover` with a `Positioner` between `Portal` and `Popup`, and `Track`'s `axis` parameter was deleted because it defaulted to "x" and no call site ever passed "y" -- the vertical branch was unreachable code, so every track is horizontal and the ARIA needs no orientation clause. **WHAT IS STILL NOT RIGHT AND IS NOT THIS ROW:** each track's `aria-label` is its `testId`, so what a screen reader announces is "picker-saturation, slider, 0", and the words an author would want are a copy decision rather than a mechanism one. That is a separate row, not a reopening of this one.
check: The picker's slider tracks are operable from the keyboard, in jsdom and in a browser. `packages/editor/src/components/ui/colour-picker.dom.test.tsx` (new, 3 cases) focuses a track and presses a key: "moves a track's value from the keyboard, which vg-194 recorded as missing" asserts the track declares `aria-valuemin=0`/`aria-valuemax=100` and that ArrowRight takes `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 1 with `onChange` called once; "steps downward, and clamps at both ends rather than wrapping" covers ArrowLeft, Home and End; "leaves a key it does not own to the panel behind it" reads `defaultPrevented` on `document` after React's own root listener, so an unowned key is not swallowed. **Both halves were shown to fail first**: restoring the reported shape -- no `onKeyDown` and no declared range -- fails the first at `{ now: 0, min: null, max: null }` and the second at `End` staying 0, and moving `preventDefault` above the unowned-key guard fails the third at `expected true to be false`. In the browser, `npx playwright test tests/e2e/keyboard.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` reports 3 passed on a rebuilt bundle; its new case asserts the picker's tracks carry `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`, and that ArrowLeft on the alpha track moves `aria-valuenow` from 100 to 99 **and** changes the hex readout in the popover. The colour maths is unaffected and still passes 5/5 (`colour-picker.test.ts`), and the palette panel's own jsdom suite is 17/17 with `editor.spec.ts --grep palette` 7/7 in the browser.

title: plan 7 Task 1.2 put seven pictographs into the copy table and reddened the full unit suite, because the net that forbids them is in a file no focused run loads
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7S PHASE 1 BOUNDARY GATE, which is the first thing to run the whole suite since Task 1.1. Measured at `e7c261c4`: `npx vitest run` is `3 failed | 3116 passed (3119)` in 452 s, and **exactly one of the three is this plan and this plan only**. The two others are vg-135 -- `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` `inserts the same objects from the Insert menu as the Add pane offers` and `refuses the chooser rather than offering rows that could insert nothing`, both `Test timed out in 20000ms`, both already filed. The new one is `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts > holds no pictographs, so an icon cannot be stored as copy`, failing `AssertionError: expected [ ...(7) ] to deeply equal []` -- seven items, which is the count of glyphs added. THE CAUSE IS NAMED AND IT IS TASK 1.2 (`337e1a1d`). That commit added `uiCopy.shortcuts` to `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts`, carrying `mac: { modifier: "⌘", shift: "⇧", alt: "⌥" }` and `named: { arrowleft: "←", arrowright: "→", arrowup: "↑", arrowdown: "↓" }`. All seven are Unicode Symbol (`U+2318`, `U+21E7`, `U+2325`, `U+2190`-`U+2193`), and `ui-copy.test.ts:27-48` walks every string in `uiCopy` rejecting `p{S}`. PROVED A REGRESSION RATHER THAN PRE-EXISTING, which is the claim worth checking: at `f264249e`, the commit immediately before, **no string value in that file contained a `p{S}` character** -- every such character was inside a comment -- and at HEAD exactly those seven do. So the test passed before this plan and fails because of it. WHY THE FOCUSED RUN COULD NOT SEE IT: Task 1.2 ran `npx vitest run packages/editor/src/shortcut-manager/`, and the net lives in `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts`, one directory up. A task that edits a shared table is not covered by a run scoped to the module that consumes it. The plan never mentions the pictograph rule and never lists `ui-copy.test.ts` in any task, so no executor was told it existed. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY: three of AGENTS.MDs filing conditions hold together. **Two owners could fix it** -- `ui-copy.ts` by changing the caps, or `ui-copy.test.ts` by narrowing the rule -- and they disagree about policy, so it is not one owner. **The fix needs a design decision**: whether a key cap is copy in the §35 sense at all. **It blocks the active plan**, because plan 7 cannot close with the suite red and the remaining ten tasks all run tests. THE DECISION, with the evidence for each side. The net is right that a *decorative* glyph must not be copy: its stated harms are that a glyph is announced as a word of its own, cannot inherit a shell colour, and does not render like the icons beside it, and the four marks it was written for (`▤ + ▣ ⚙` in the rail) were exactly that. But a `<kbd>` key cap is a different render path -- it is styled by its own rule and inherits shell colour by design -- and `⌘` has no non-symbol spelling, so §7s rule that a chord reads in the platform own caps cannot be satisfied without one. The narrowest reading that keeps the net: an explicit allowlist of those seven key-cap characters, so anything else is still caught, including anything future smuggled into `shortcuts`. The more principled reading: a key cap is not *translatable* copy, so it does not belong in the copy table at all and wants to live in `display.ts` beside the renderer that spells it. Not yet the users decision in writing -- the row records the question and the recommendation, and plan 7 continues on Phase 2 meanwhile because neither open task touches `ui-copy.ts`. CLOSED 2026-10-08 BY MOVING THE CAPS OUT OF THE COPY TABLE, which is the more principled of the two readings this row named, and the user asked for the red test to be fixed rather than ruled on. **A KEY CAP IS NOT COPY:** the table holds the words a translator would change, and `⌘`, `⇧`, `⌥` and the four arrows are the platform's own marks that stay put in every language -- as is `Ctrl`, which sat in the same table and was itself never translatable. So the seven entries left `ui-copy.ts` for `CAPS`/`NAMED_KEYS` in `shortcut-manager/display.ts`, the module that already read them and nothing else. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS REJECTED ON PURPOSE: an allowlist of those seven characters would have kept the glyphs where they were by narrowing the rule that caught them, and the row's own evidence says the rule is right -- a glyph in the copy table is announced as a word of its own, cannot inherit a shell colour, and does not render like the icons beside it. A `<kbd>` escapes the second and third by being styled by its own rule, so nothing was lost by moving it, and the table it left is stricter than before because nothing can now hide in it. WHAT MOVED WITH IT, UNASKED: `mac.alt` and `other.alt` (`⌥` and `Alt`) are deleted as unreachable -- `ShortcutBinding` carries no `alt` field and `caps()` reads only `modifier` and `shift`, so the cap could never reach a chord. THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND IS NOT THIS ROW'S: `<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>` is still read aloud by a screen reader as "place of interest sign Z". Moving the glyph out of the copy table stops the table being where a glyph hides; it does not fix the announcement, which needs an accessible name on the `<kbd>` and a copy decision (`Command` or `Cmd`) that is the user's.
check: The copy table holds no pictographs, and it passes without the rule being weakened. `ui-copy.test.ts` is byte-identical to the commit that found it, so the assertion `expect(pictographs(uiCopy)).toEqual([])` is the same one that went red with seven entries; it now collects zero, and the file's other four cases -- the three panels' own copy, the font picker's, the favourite toggle's two words, and the unit-display options' one owner -- are unchanged and green. The seven glyphs are not deleted: `CAPS` and `NAMED_KEYS` in `shortcut-manager/display.ts` hold them, beside the formatter that was already their only reader. That the visible behaviour did not move is asserted in two places that were not written for this fix: `display.test.ts` still reads `⌘Z` for `edit.undo` and `⌘⇧Z · ⌘Y` for `edit.redo`, and `tests/e2e/keyboard.spec.ts` is 3 expected / 0 unexpected on a rebuilt bundle, reading `Ctrl+D` out of the tooltip's own `kbd`. Full unit suite 3149 passed of 3149, 0 failed, at the artefact sha. The net's force was checked rather than assumed: it is the same walk over the same table, so a glyph smuggled into `ui-copy.ts` later still reddens it.

title: Text over a 16px-blurred glass panel measures 0.74 of the sharp control, under the 0.85 floor reference-theme.spec.ts pins
detail: FOUND WHILE RUNNING plan 4 Task 6's browser gate, not by that task. reference-theme.spec.ts:1441 ("text above a glass panel stays sharp through a real mount") failed on two samples, same tree: reading.blurred 0.74 against an assertion of > 0.85 x control, control 0.944, so the floor is 0.8024 and the blurred side is 8% under it. The task-11 report of the reference-theme-fidelity plan recorded 0.899 for the same measurement, so this is a change rather than a marginal case. NOT ATTRIBUTED TO THAT TASK'S DIFF: the diff is four e2e test files and no product source, and the failing test's body and helpers are byte-identical to base 9bc5ac25 - the only edit to that spec file is in another describe 800 lines above. The reading is taken inside the page from the canvas' own 2D context (getImageData after renderAll, toggling text.visible and vigiliaGlass.blurRadius between 16 and 0), so it is independent of the layer panel and of anything Task 6 changed. The control (blurRadius 0) still reads 0.944, so the glyphs render sharp; only the over-blur case dropped. Ruled out as a cause: test order (each test opens its own page), the entry work (the fixture draws no layer row), and a missing font (the sharp control depends on the same face). The machine was at 100% CPU with another session's Chromium on it, which is recorded as a possible cause and not as an explanation - a software rasteriser is deterministic, so a real rendering change is at least as likely. Cause not established, and the fix needs a decision about which side of the claim is wrong: the blur path or the 0.85 floor. MECHANISM, FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE VERIFYING THAT THE TASK'S OWN DIFF IS NOT THE CAUSE: the reading is not a constant of the document. The band it is taken from is sized at rect.width * vp[0] * retina (reference-theme.spec.ts:1501-1502) and the glyph over the panel is drawn at that same scale, so the ratio is a function of the FIT ZOOM - the class vg-136 named and vg-137 kept five more of. That makes the camera a candidate, and THIS PLAN MOVED IT: 104adefc (plan 4, Task 3, 'the row's role is paid for out of the stage's width, measured') widened the left column from 340px to 360px, taking 20px off the width the canvas fills, and the fit zoom is computed from that width. NOT ESTABLISHED as the cause, and the row stays open on that: 20px is a small stage change and nobody has read the zoom at either measurement, so this is a candidate with a mechanism rather than a finding. The bisect that settles it is one test at two commits - reference-theme.spec.ts:1441 at 75e9c6d4, which is before 104adefc, and again at plan 4's HEAD, rebuilding the editor bundle for each because the spec runs against a built bundle. Assigned to plan 4's Task 10, whose subject is re-measurement; if the earlier commit passes, the 0.85 floor is a zoom-coupled constant and the fix is where vg-137's five went, not a wider tolerance. BISECT DONE, run by plan 4 Task 10 at 42169371 and rebuilding @vigilia/editor for each commit because this spec measures a built bundle: 75e9c6d4 (104adefc^) PASSES; 104adefc FAILS at 0.74 against the 0.802300 the same run computes (control 0.944 x 0.85); ee58ef35 (plan 4 HEAD) FAILS, the same 0.74 / 0.8024. So the earlier commit passes and this row prediction holds: the floor is a zoom-coupled constant, and 104adefc, the left column widened 340px to 360px - which the controller confirmed in editor-shell.css - is what moved the fit zoom. THE ROW STAYS OPEN, deliberately and against plan 4 Task 10s instruction to close it: the test is still red at HEAD, so no honest check exists that proves the named problem was addressed, and closing it verified would be the false landed report this repo has already had to correct twice. WHAT THE FIX NEEDS: a decision about which side is wrong, either moving the floor into the zoom-coupled class where vg-137s five went or widening it, and that decision is the users. RESOLVED 2026-10-08, AND THE PREMISE IS REFUTED RATHER THAN THE FLOOR MOVED. The user was asked which side of the claim was wrong and answered with the question that dissolved it: "I don't understand the question. If the text is above the glass panel, why isn't it tack sharp?" -- which is what the product is supposed to do, so the other side was never really available. The user then approved replacing the metric outright and taking the threshold from measurement, and that landed as 1bbcebd4. The `max adjacent step / row range` amplitude is gone, replaced by the width of the glyph's own edge in device pixels -- the median over the rows the glyph crosses of that row's 10%-to-90% transition -- and the answer is 2 device pixels over the 16px-blurred panel and 2 over the sharp one at this fixture's 0.71 scale: the text is not softened and never was. WHY THE OLD READING MOVED IS NOW NAMED RATHER THAN GUESSED: the old comment claimed the text-less frame cancels the panel, and it does not -- the text is composited *over* the glass, so the difference retains a term in the panel's own pixels, and a single-pixel extremum read that backdrop term as softness. The zoom coupling this row established by bisect is real and was a second, independent way for the same number to move; it can no longer move this one, because a width in device pixels is what an antialiased edge is whatever the camera does. The instrument was probed before it was trusted -- giving `over-glass` its own `ctx.filter` blur takes the same measure to 30 at `blur(1px)` and past the row floor above that -- so the 2 is a measurement and not a blind read. WITHDRAWN AND NOT VERIFIED: nothing in the product changed, because nothing in the product was wrong. A `verified` row here would read as work landed on the glass blur path, and no such work exists; what landed is a better instrument.

title: Biome lints and formats no .tsx file at all, so every React surface in the editor is outside both gates
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 4 TASK 1 (61b9673d), while running the verification the plan specifies for a task that edits a .tsx test. MEASURED: biome.json at the repo root sets files.includes to ["src/web/**/*.ts", "src/web/**/*.json", "src/web/**/*.css"]. In Biome 2.x files.includes REPLACES the default includes rather than extending it, so a .tsx path matches none of the three globs and is never linted or formatted. git ls-files counts 23 tracked .tsx files against 467 .ts, so the gap is small in count and total in kind: it holds the editor shell components (editor-shell/layer-panel.tsx, shell-layout.tsx, pane-bar.tsx among them) and every React test. WHAT IT COSTS: `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` both report success while covering none of that code, so a plan can list "biome lint .. clean" as a gate on a task whose only source file is a .tsx and the gate is vacuous rather than absent - the failure mode AGENTS.md names when it says a capability that exists has still not been discharged by existing. Plan 4 Task 2 and Task 5 both edit layer-panel.tsx and both name a biome gate, so this is live for the active plan rather than theoretical. NOT FIXED HERE: adding .tsx to files.includes turns on formatting for 23 files that have never been formatted, which is a repo-wide reformat and a decision about scope rather than a one-line config fix, and it is not this plan's task. The linter rules enabled (noUnusedImports, noUnusedVariables, noFloatingPromises, noDoubleEquals) would likely find real results in that code. VERIFIED BY PLAN 1 TASK 1 OF THE EDITOR-GUI REDESIGN (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-gates-and-the-control-set.md) at base sha 153f5b85, where the counts above were re-measured and found stale: the tree holds 33 tracked .tsx against 499 tracked .ts, not 23 against 467.
check: The gate covers `.tsx`: `cd src/web && ./node_modules/.bin/biome lint ..` reports `Checked 560 files` against 527 before the glob, and exits 0. With `const unusedProbe = 1;` appended to `packages/editor/src/editor-shell/canvas-dock.tsx` the same command exits 1 and names the file — `canvas-dock.tsx:172:7 lint/correctness/noUnusedVariables` — while the identical probe under the old `.ts`-only glob exits 0 over 527 files, which is the defect itself. `npm run format:check` (`biome format ..`) exits 0 over the same 560 files; the pass that got it there reformatted 24 `.tsx` files and touched no `.ts`, `.json` or `.css` file.

title: The Add pane cannot carry a pane-level data-vigilia-panel name without colliding with new-object-panel.ts:182
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING plan 2 Task 2 (the panes' chrome), not by that task. src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/new-object-panel.ts:182 sets data-vigilia-panel="add" on its own root, so the Add pane cannot also be named at pane level without two elements answering to one selector. That collision is the reason the landed Pane component takes an OPTIONAL id and only the Composition pane is named: the brief declared `readonly id: string` as required, and a required id would have put data-vigilia-panel="add" on the pane section as well, where editor-rail.spec.ts reads that selector under Playwright strict mode and two matches are an error rather than a first match. So the deviation from the brief's declared interface was forced by this attribute, not chosen. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair is a naming decision spanning two owners - whether the panel keeps the attribute and the pane is named differently, or the panel's attribute is scoped to its own subtree - and it is a contract question rather than a task. SEVERITY: low; nothing reads an Add-pane selector today, and the pane is addressable through the rail slot words instead.
check: editor-rail.spec.ts reads [data-vigilia-panel="add"] and resolves exactly one element - the Add pane - with new-object-panel.ts:182s duplicate attribute deleted, so the pane carries its own name without colliding

title: The flat-elevation override wins on source order at equal specificity, so a later appended rule would silently re-glass the chrome
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING plan 2 Task 2 (the panes' chrome). The rule that takes the rail, the panes and the inspector to elevation 0 ties the palette's glass rules on specificity (0,3,0) and wins by source order alone - it is simply later in editor-shell.css. A later rule of equal specificity appended after it would silently re-glass the chrome, and nothing would notice: scripts/design-tokens.mjs checks values rather than cascade order, and the browser specs assert rendered elevation only for the elements they name, so the rail could return to a shadow and every gate would stay green. NOT FIXED HERE because the smallest change that removed the fragility was to restructure the palette's own selectors, which the next task owns. OWNER: plan 2 Task 3 (the header trimmed), which lands the palette block and should fold this override into it rather than leaving two rules whose order decides the result. SUPERSEDED BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11): the hazard this row fixed is gone rather than moved, so the mechanism the `check` above describes no longer exists in the file. `.editor-glass` is now the CHROME fill and the glass rule names the two clusters (`.editor-shell-dock.editor-glass`, `.editor-shell-zoom.editor-glass`), so no equal-specificity ordering decides the chrome's elevation any more - the glass rule cannot match a chrome region at all - and the (0,4,0) override is left carrying only the interior hairline reset. The `check` and its line numbers are therefore a description of what landed at the named sha rather than of the current file, and `editor-shell.css`'s own comment records the substitution.
check: editor-shell.css:438-444 raises the flat-elevation override to (0,4,0) against the palette rule at (0,3,0), so the override no longer depends on source order and a later appended rule cannot re-glass the chrome by being later

title: Locking an object through the layer row leaves the selection column offering its writing fields
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3 TASK 10, driving the built editor in Chromium and locking a starter card through the layer row's own control. MEASURED TWICE, 1.5 s apart and with no further interaction: after clicking [data-vigilia-layer="group-cpu-card"] [aria-label="Lock"], the object's Fabric `locked` property is already true (read through vigiliaEditorBridge) while the column still renders all five sections - content, position, layer, paint, spends - and still offers [data-vigilia-name], a geometry field and [data-vigilia-panel-fill]. Selecting another row and coming back renders the locked column correctly: one section (spends), the note "This object is locked. Unlock it to edit it." and no writing field. CAUSE, read rather than guessed: object-lock-manager/index.ts:74-81 `apply` sets the Fabric flags, calls canvas.requestRenderAll() and save(), and fires no canvas event; selection-inspector/index.ts:487-501 renders on object:modified, the four selection events, object:added, object:removed and editor:history-state-loaded, so a lock change reaches none of them. NOT FIXED HERE: Task 10 owns a spec and the evidence table, not product source, and its brief says a failing claim is a finding to report rather than one to fix. WHAT IT COSTS AN AUTHOR: between the lock and the next selection the panel advertises edits the object will refuse, which is the unreachability this plan exists to remove - and it is reachable from the panel's own control rather than from a hand-made document. The lock route through object-actions.ts and the layer footer is expected to share the manager and so the same silence, but that was not measured. RESOLVED 2026-10-09 (plan 3, Task 1, f1a35b82): object-lock-manager now fires OBJECT_LOCK_CHANGED_EVENT and the inspector subscribes and republishes, so locking through the layer row updates the column in place; the browser check below is the proof.
check: tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts:648 "withholds a locked object's writing fields and keeps its read-only ones" drives the row's own route ([data-vigilia-layer="group-cpu-card"] [aria-label="Lock"] at :661) and asserts [data-vigilia-locked] becomes visible at :664 - browser evidence in the built editor, and that spec passed 11/11 at 1ab06ad2.

title: The Document pane holds three scopes in one scroll, and the theme globals have no surface of their own
detail:
Raised by the user on 2026-10-07 while reviewing the redesign, and the ruling is to dissolve the pane. Measured here: editor-session.ts mounts four different things into panelHosts.document — createArtboardPanel at :292 (metadata plus artboard), createPalettePanel at :317, createTypePresetPanel at :332, and createDocumentReferencesPanel at :388 — so one scroll holds the document (metadata, artboard), the theme globals (palette and type presets, which are style libraries rather than the document), and a read-only derived view. That is the same defect the redesign spec names at 2026-10-02-frontend-redesign-design.md:227, no scope shares a scroll with another, reintroduced inside a column instead of between them. The user also states that the globals surface was requested in the past: searched both register files for global, palette and metadata and there is no row for it, and AGENTS.md records why — no UserPromptSubmit hook is registered, so a user message lives alone in the root session context and dies with it. So the request was made and never queued; this row is that request, recorded. The destination the user named is a surface of the globals own, with this pane dissolved rather than reorganised. Not this plan: plan 4 task 8 lands the document listing in the pane as an interim home so the Style tab can be deleted, and STATUS.md rules the follow-up out of the active plan. AMENDED 2026-10-09 BY PLAN 3'S ISLAND-FIX RE-REVIEW: the surface this row dissolves is also an imperative one. createDocumentReferencesPanel (selection-inspector/style.ts:43-97) and the document globals section (selection-inspector/appearance.ts:227-237) build their DOM with document.createElement, and a user reads the result in the Document pane, so the redesign spec's acceptance item (2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md:592, 'Every editor surface is React') is not met here either. It is not an island under a React wrapper, so the item's second clause does not apply. Recorded on this row, which already owns the pane, rather than as a second row about the same surface.
CLOSED 2026-10-10 BY PLAN 4 PHASE 2 (the Tokens pane, Tasks 5-7), WITH WHAT THE ROW ASKED FOR AND NOT MORE. The style libraries are a surface of their own: `palette-manager/panel.ts`'s rendering leaves became `panes/tokens/paint-list.tsx` under `panes/tokens/tokens-pane.tsx` (Task 5, ebe1743b), and `type-preset-manager/panel.ts`'s became `panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx` (Task 6, 56516ce0), both mounted by the `tokens` pane and neither inside the Document pane this row measured. The row's destination was a surface of the globals own with the Document pane DISSOLVED rather than reorganised; plan 4 landed the two libraries on their own surface, and the row's remaining clause is the pane's dissolution, which is the decision plan 4 deferred and this close does not claim: plan 4 Task 8 replaced the pane's three scopes with the document listing and References, so no style library is read there today. The amendment of 2026-10-09 (the two imperative builders) is discharged for both libraries: each panel now keeps only its host `section` and renders its list as React through the control set (`palette-manager/panel.ts:53,66`; `type-preset-manager/panel.ts:56,69`), so neither builds fields with document.createElement.
check: cd src/web && npx vitest run packages/editor/src/panes/tokens/ — 30 cases pass (paint-list.dom.test.tsx 11, preset-list.dom.test.tsx 19), which is the theme's globals rendering on a surface of their own: the paint list and the preset list under panes/tokens/, mounted by the tokens pane (editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:753, data-vigilia-panel="tokens") and not inside the Document pane the row measured (editor-session.ts:292-388). The panel built its own fields with document.createElement at the row's base; both libraries render React on the control set today, and neither is a native <select>.

title: The type preset panel is not bound to the selection, so it contradicts the inspector it sits beside
detail:
A DECISION, not a patch, and it is the real half of what vg-088 was filed as. Found while fixing vg-088. The type preset panel is constructed with (host, onChange, onDelete, fontActions) at editor-session.ts:320-337 — no canvas, no selection, no object reference — and its chooser defaults to Object.keys(presets)[0] at type-preset-manager/panel.ts:60-61. So it shows the first declared preset whatever the selection is set in. The vg-088 report established BOTH facts by probe, not inference: the inspector dropdown is correctly bound to typePresets.46-600, and the panel dropdown holds a bare 20-400 with CANVAS REFS: false. An author who sets a run to 24-400, opens the Type presets panel to see what that preset is, and finds 20-400 selected cannot tell a default from an answer. Note the shape: the two surfaces genuinely disagree, but not about a shared binding — one is bound and the other is unbound, so no fix to the binding reconciles them. Binding the panel to the selection changes what the panel IS (it is a document-level editor today), which is why it needs a decision rather than a patch.
CLOSED 2026-10-10 BY PLAN 4 TASK 7 (§5.3). The chooser no longer defaults to the first declared preset: the shell projects readonly selectionPresetId on EditorShellSnapshot (editor-shell/bridge.ts:45, produced at :181 from the same typePresetOf reader selection-inspector already used), and type-preset-manager/panel.ts:54 hands the projection to panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx as the list's `selection`. Measured at the close: Object.keys(presets) survives only as the library's membership enumeration (preset-list.tsx:143) and in tests that name the retired default, so no surface reads a first-declared answer. The row's two facts were that one surface is bound and the other unbound, and the fix is the binding the row asked for rather than a reconciliation of a shared one; the container case (a group or a multi-selection) reads as its children's presets through childrenAppearance, which is the same rule selection-inspector states, so the two surfaces cannot disagree.
check: cd src/web && npx vitest run packages/editor/src/panes/tokens/preset-list.dom.test.tsx — 19 cases pass, including "names the preset the selected run is set in" (:350), "says nothing is selected rather than showing the first declared preset" (:334) and "reads a group or a multi-selection as its children's presets, not as none" (:378). The preset panel's chooser opens on the selection's preset through the shell's projected selectionPresetId (bridge.ts:181, panel.ts:54), not on Object.keys(presets)[0]; the readout names the preset as the selection's, and the named inspector it sits beside reads the same rule.

title: `shell-surfaces.spec.ts` is red at the branch head and nothing registers it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 2'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 6cafe996..64fea389) AND NOT IN THE REPORT'S PRE-EXISTING-FAILURE CENSUS. The failure is before any `choosePalette` call and touches nothing plan 5 Task 2 changed (that task deleted the header's palette chip and its menu, and touched no pane). CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED BEYOND THE MECHANISM: which commit first made the pane ordering invisible to `.first()` was not bisected, and the last change to the spec itself is `9501542c` (plan 3's close). CONSEQUENCE: the six-palette pass of the re-pointed `choosePalette` helper is unproven for this one consumer - the helper is re-pointed and green elsewhere (`inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s single call was run and passed). NOT FIXED IN TASK 2 because a spec red before the task's own change is not the task's to repair and the fix is a locator decision (which pane's section the spec means). Related: the spec was already in the census of pre-existing browser reds that `STATUS.md` carries; it was not in that list before this review. CAUSE ESTABLISHED 2026-10-10 BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I: plan 4's Task 8 (`9f6252a8`) moved the Document pane onto `InspectorSection` after this locator was written (`9501542c`, plan 3's close), so an unscoped `[data-vigilia-section].first()` began resolving to that pane's hidden `theme` section. FIXED ON THE FLY at `09a82734` rather than filed, because the cause was named at file:line, the fix sits inside one owner (this spec), and the correct behaviour was already the file's own comment that the column "is always mounted"; the locator is now scoped to `.editor-shell-inspector` rather than `:visible`, so it names which column is meant instead of which section happens to be painted.

title: The display proof suite is red on a run colour the document does not carry, and no command runs that suite
detail: FOUND BY RUNNING author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts and author-journey-display.spec.ts during fix round 1 of the editor-left-column plan. Both are testIgnore d out of playwright.config.ts and run under playwright.rebuild.config.ts and playwright.display.config.ts, so npm run test:e2e never executes them and nothing else runs them either. Measured on 8adeb5c, the base before the pane bar landed: all 9 tests in the rebuild suite fail, and the display suite single test fails after 11.4m. Three causes, all predating that work. (1) author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:76 asserts the Insert pane holds 13 buttons; 6fc9f27d halved SHAPE_KINDS to six on the user ruling recorded as vg-078, so it holds 11. (2) Nine references to [data-vigilia-panel-fill], -stroke, -border and -radius across author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts and rebuild-driver.ts: no such attribute exists anywhere in packages/editor/src, and 5a563a1c removed the last one on 2026-10-02. (3) [data-vigilia-run-colour=\"0\"] is asked for an option a blank theme does not carry, so the select resolves and the option never does. Not fixed at the time: not one of the nine can go green from a single line, and the suite has to be migrated onto the inspector attribute names that exist today, which is its own task with its own owner. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-07 at f4647683: two of the three causes above no longer reproduce. (1) is fixed — author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:74-75 now reads "What the pane offers, not how many buttons that is" in place of the 13-button count. (2) is fixed — all four attributes exist again at selection-inspector/panel.ts:268 (vigiliaPanelFill), :286 (-Stroke), :300 (-Border), :313 (-Radius). The rebuild suite is therefore no longer red for any of these reasons: measured 8 passed, 1 failed, and the single failure is a 30s timeout on the wordmark test, which is vg-147s pre-existing edge (28.1s and 28.2s on two quiet samples, 36.2s on a loaded box), not this row. (3) alone stands, and it is the DISPLAY suite only: author-journey-display.spec.ts:191 calls buildComposition, reaching buildWordmarkAndClock at rebuild-composition.ts:140 and its colour: "text" at :148, while author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts never calls buildComposition, openBlankComposition or buildWordmarkAndClock at all, so the rebuild suite cannot reach the path. Nine sites in rebuild-composition.ts pass colour: "text" (:111, :148, :173, :207, :539, :583, :593, :650, :660) and the document declares palette-prefixed tokens, so the stale value is the tests rather than the control. Measured failure: [data-vigilia-run-colour="0"] has no option "text"; it offers palette.text, palette.dim, palette.panel, palette.frost, palette.panelStroke, palette.rule, palette.chartTrack, palette.frostInk, palette.frostArea, palette.colour, palette.colour-2, palette.colour-3 and palette.colour-4. It now fails in 16.6s rather than the 11.4m recorded above, because rebuild-driver.ts:200-224 choose() names a missing option instead of waiting for it. VERIFIED 2026-10-10 BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I (commit ab89957a, fix round 1). The run-colour half is fixed: all 19 `colour:` sites in `rebuild-composition.ts` now name `palette.text` / `palette.dim` instead of a bare id the document does not carry, and the ids match what the control commits (`data-vigilia-option` = `option.id`). SCOPE NOTE, because this row's title carries a second clause: "and no command runs that suite" is NOT discharged here - it is split out as `vg-282`, which owns the fact that `playwright.config.ts` testIgnores the display and rebuild specs and nothing passes `--config`. That clause is why this row stayed red long enough to be filed; it was never this row's colour defect.
check: cd src/web && npx playwright test --config playwright.display.config.ts — exit 0 at head 846e451c, run by the controller: 1 passed in 4.6m, `[display] › author-journey-display.spec.ts:175:3 › the rebuilt composition, on a display › the author's backdrop, the cards, and both display sizes`. title: A field row's value cell is a right-aligned flexible slot, so a number well, a text well, a select and a slider each take their own width where the drawing declares one
detail: FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-10, looking at the inspector panel: "The input boxes in the inspection panel aren't even aligned." THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: the row's value cell is a right-aligned flexible slot holding a content-sized box, so a number or text well is as wide as its <input>'s intrinsic width while a select or slider fills the whole slot, and the label that starts the slot has no declared width — FOUR widths in one section where docs/design/mockups/inspector-controls.html declares one. 11 instances, each with its element and line in the measurement: the shared row is src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-well.tsx — `justify-end` at :211, the well declaring no width at :78-84, the label declaring none at :187. THE OWNER IS THE SHARED CONTROL SET, NOT THE INSPECTOR, and the measurement's decisive evidence is that the same five different left edges appear in the parity fixture's own capture (control-set-desktop-chromium.png — Name 117, Shows 63, Fill 45, Width 100, Align 180): a defect local to the inspector could not appear in the fixture the control set is captured from. THREE COMMITTED CAPTURES ALREADY SHOW IT — editor-inspector-shape-desktop-chromium.png (the Paint section alone has left edges 34/52/85 and right edges 259/263), editor-inspector-card-desktop-chromium.png and control-set-desktop-chromium.png — which is a finding in its own right: they were taken and never read, by a plan that closed reporting parity. NOT CONFUSED WITH vg-098 / vg-108, both verified: those are TEXT alignment, a different property on a different cell. title: editor-shell.css's legacy unlayered input and label rules beat Tailwind and re-box an input inside a well that already draws one, and push every label ~6px below its control
detail: FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-10, looking at the inspector panel: "The input boxes in the inspection panel aren't even aligned." MEASURED by the same read-only measurement (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/inspector-alignment-measurement.md), as the second of the two owners of that defect. THE RULES: src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:986-1004 (the input/button box) and :845-851 (`label { display: block; margin-top: 12px }`). Both are UNLAYERED, so they beat Tailwind's utilities regardless of source order, which is why the product's wells show TWO border pairs (86/263 and 93/252) where the parity fixture shows ONE (117/276) — the only difference between the two being the `.editor-shell-inspector` ancestor (shell-layout.tsx:894), which control-fixture.tsx:62 omits. The label rule's 12px top margin is what shifts every label ~6px below its control against the row's `items-center`, measured on two rows and absent in the fixture; that is the misalignment a person is most likely looking at when they say the boxes aren't aligned. CONSEQUENCE: the control set's treatment is overridden by a stylesheet from the imperative era, so a control's box is decided in two places and one of them is unlayered and invisible to a utility class — the same two-owners-one-concept shape AGENTS.md forbids. MEASURED ADJACENT: the existing spacing ratchet would fail on the legacy `margin-top: 3px` if the file were gated, which is vg-274's gap and Task 7 of plan 7's work. OWNED BY plan 7 Task 8 Step 3. What would settle it: the legacy rules deleted where the control set owns the treatment or scoped to the surface that needs them, with the double border proven gone on the fixture AND on a real inspector.
check: restored the legacy unlayered input rule and confirmed the fixture reddens on an input drawing a box inside a well that already draws one, then confirmed it green with the rule removed

title: The control-set parity fixture does not mount .editor-shell-inspector, so the product-only half of the control row is invisible to the one gate built for it
detail: FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-10, looking at the inspector panel: "The input boxes in the inspection panel aren't even aligned." MEASURED by the same read-only measurement (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/inspector-alignment-measurement.md): control-fixture.tsx does not mount the `.editor-shell-inspector` ancestor that shell-layout.tsx:894 wraps the product's inspector column in, and the legacy shell rules (vg-298) only reach an input inside that ancestor. So the fixture — the surface the parity capture and the control-set assertions read — renders a control set that the product does not render, and the difference is exactly the half the user reported. THE MEASUREMENT'S OWN DECISIVE TEST: the product shows two border pairs (86/263, 93/252) and the fixture one (117/276); reverting the ancestor makes the fixture agree with the product, which is how the omission was found rather than inferred. CONSEQUENCE: this is vg-292's family again — an instrument claiming more coverage than it has — and it is the sharper case, because the fixture is not merely incomplete, it is *greener* than the product: every control assertion passes on a surface that has one fewer stylesheet applied to it. NOT FIXED HERE: plan 7 Task 8 Step 4 mounts the ancestor and proves the blindness by reverting the step and confirming the assertion goes green. What would settle it: the fixture mounting what the product mounts, with the assertion that fails on the un-mounted state recorded in the task's report.
check: mounted the ancestors the product mounts in the fixture, then put the ancestor-wide rule back and confirmed the gate sees the product-only half of the row by naming the doubled inputs

title: One control row now carries the inspector's 74px label column, and every surface that composes a row inherits it - the settings modal's drawing draws that row as a panel box with the label filling it, and the narrower panes ellipsize a filename
detail: FOUND by plan 7 Task 8 while making the control row one geometry (control-well.tsx). WHAT CHANGED: the row declared no label width, so a label was content-sized; Task 8 fixed it to the one value track its drawing declares - a `width:74px;flex:0 0 auto` label column and a `flex:1` cell (docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html, 13 rows), which is what makes the field boxes of one section share a left edge (vg-297). Two surfaces are not drawn that way and inherit the column anyway. FIRST, THE SETTINGS MODAL: editor-shell/settings.tsx:160 renders ControlToggle for "Follow the system", and docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:89-93 draws that row as a `--panel-2` panel box with the label at `flex:1` filling the row and the 26x14 toggle at the right - no label column at all - so the label wraps to two lines and the row grows a line taller. SECOND, THE PANES: the Add pane's asset row is a ControlSelect (panes/add/file-section.tsx:174) and the Document pane's metadata rows are control rows too, at 240-246px rather than the inspector's 276px, so `Release version` wraps and the asset trigger ellipsizes the chosen filename to `starter-backdro...` - the drawing that governs the panes draws no such row. The regenerated pane-document, pane-add, editor-shell-add and settings-appearance captures in Task 8's commit are the before/after evidence. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED THERE: the brief that owns Task 8 rules that a genuinely different width is a finding for the report rather than a fifth declaration, and this is a different SHAPE rather than a width - a per-surface label column, or a second full-width-label row component, is a design decision each surface's own plan has to make against its own drawing. OWNED BY plan 8 (settings parity, unwritten, for the modal) and by plan 7's remaining shell tasks for the panes. What would settle it: the settings drawing adopting the 74px column, or ControlRow gaining a nameable full-width-label row the modal renders, plus a ruling on whether a 240px pane takes the same label column as a 276px inspector - with the drawing as the comparator either way. RESOLVED 2026-10-11 by plan 7 Task 8, and ONE PREMISE IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG: it says the drawing that governs the panes "draws no such row", but shell.html:227 and eleven siblings declare `width:74px;flex:0 0 auto`, so the panes' metadata rows ARE drawn with the column and their column was never a drift - `Release version` wrapping is §7.7's own rule, a label wraps rather than widening a pane, and the drawing does not draw that row. What did drift is the two shapes the row got: ControlRow now takes `column` (the field row, the default), `boxed` (the modal's switch row, from settings.html:89-93) and `headed` (the Add pane's asset trigger, from shell.html:128-132), so the settings half and the asset half are discharged. NOTE FOR PLAN 8: settings.html:90 declares `padding:9px 10px` and 9 is not a §3 step (`4,6,8,10,12,14,16,20,24,32`), so the drawing is stale there and the product's 8px is right - filed as vg-303.
check: read the switch row in the settings drawing and the asset trigger in the pane drawing and confirmed each surface takes the shape its own drawing declares, with the panes' label column licensed at shell.html:227

title: The shell-appearance spec reads a surface whose painting rule Task 8 deleted, and its own docblock still describes that deleted rule
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 2 on 2026-10-11, while establishing which browser specs the flush body left red rather than assuming the answer. MEASURED TWICE, and the second measurement is the one that matters: with the working tree restored to HEAD 9fa722df's stylesheet and the editor bundle rebuilt, shell-appearance.spec.ts:85 ("every palette paints the surfaces its --vigilia-* tokens name") fails, reporting documentInput = rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) under all six palettes. It fails with Task 2's change in the tree in exactly the same way, which is not a coincidence: background-color does not inherit and no selector Task 2 touched names an input, so the assertion cannot see the change at all. CAUSE ESTABLISHED BY SOURCE: the rule that painted it, `.editor-shell-panel button, .editor-shell-panel input` and its :hover, was deleted in 0e7b3405 (plan 7 Task 8), an ancestor of the base - so this red is Task 8's, not Task 2's. The element the spec reads is the first `.editor-shell-panel input` in the document, and the spec's own docblock (shell-appearance.spec.ts, the shellColours docblock) says what it is: Base UI's hidden value-carrier `input` behind a select root, "not a surface an author types in". It says something else that is now false in the same sentence - that documentInput "resolves through the same legacy rule" - and that rule no longer exists, so the docblock and the surface list disagree with the stylesheet. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the two ways out are a decision, not a repair. Either the hidden value-carrier is a surface the palette is required to paint, in which case some rule must own it and the fix is in the stylesheet; or it is not a surface at all, in which case the assertion is reading a control the docblock itself says nobody types in and the row should name a real one - and a hidden carrier that happens to be first in DOM order is exactly the kind of surface a list like this should not be measuring. The spec's comment already warns that getComputedStyle answers rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) for a dropped declaration AND for a deliberately transparent surface, which is why the two cannot be told apart from the assertion alone. Owner: whoever holds the pane's control surfaces now (Task 8 changed them, plan 8 consumes them) and the spec's surface list, together. R25 applies: the value needs a rule before it needs an entry. ADJACENT, DIFFERENT MECHANISM: vg-285 already names shell-appearance.spec.ts:85 as one of four specs that time out at the default worker count - that is a timeout under load, and this is an assertion that fails at any worker count. What would settle it: decide which of the two readings is true, then propagate to the docblock and the surface list in the same commit as the rule, so the comment stops describing a rule that is gone. RESOLVED 2026-10-11 by the controller, not by Task 2, because the defect is Task 8's blast radius and the controller signed Task 8 off having verified the gate it was watching rather than what else the deleted rule painted. MEASURED, NOT READ: in the running editor at f31b000b the first `.editor-shell-panel input` is `id="base-ui-_r_37_-hidden-input"`, `aria-hidden="true"`, `tabindex="-1"`, `style="clip-path: inset(50%)"`, and its parent is the value cell rather than a well, while a real control input sits in a `bg-panel-2` well. So the sweep was requiring an opaque background from an element Base UI clips to nothing, and it passed before Task 8 only because the legacy rule painted every input indiscriminately. THE FIX: the entry is gone, and the docblock no longer credits the deleted rule - it now says `documentSelect` resolves through `--panel-2` on a control-set well, that the `data-vigilia-asset-select` hook it names is targeted by no CSS rule at all, and that the removed entry is not replaced by a real well because a well is painted by `--panel-2` and would not restore what the entry covered. CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: `--vigilia-control-bg` now paints only conditional surfaces (the Add pane's asset buttons, the crop row, the modal's buttons, the keyboard sheet's chips), so this sweep no longer verifies that token on an always-mounted surface; editor-shell.tokens.test.ts covers its declaration per palette, and whether the token should still exist now that the control set paints wells from `--panel-2` is a plan-8 question. BEFORE/AFTER MEASURED: with the entry restored the sweep fails on all six palettes (`editorial/documentInput = rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and five more); with it removed, 1 passed at `--workers=1` and `--workers=2`.
check: read the surface the shell-appearance sweep measures and confirmed it is a surface the palette paints, not a hidden carrier - measured in the browser at f31b000b as base-ui's aria-hidden, clip-path-clipped value input - then confirmed the sweep green at two worker counts

title: Four of the six shell palettes declare no `--shell-danger`, `--shell-primary-bg` or `--shell-primary-text`, so under ember, moss, plum and light `--hot` and the publish button's fill resolve to the baseline palette's values instead of their own, and the token test cannot see it because it asserts the alias rather than its source
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE SCOPING TASK 4 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11). MEASURED BY READING THE CASCADE: `applyShellPalette` (`packages/editor/src/editor-shell/palette.ts:103`) writes the palette to `document.documentElement`, so exactly one palette block applies at a time; of the six, only `[data-shell-palette="editorial"]`/`.editor-shell-palette-swatch` (`editor-shell.css:41-43`) and `[data-shell-palette="graphite"]` (`:132-134`) declare those three tokens, and the four middle blocks (`ember` `:166`, `moss` `:192`, `plum` `:216`, `light` `:242`) declare `--hot: var(--shell-danger)` (`:186`, `:210`, `:234`, `:258`) and neither the primary pair nor its source. Nothing sets them at runtime: `palette.ts` mentions neither, and no `.tsx` writes them. Under those four palettes `--shell-danger` is guaranteed-invalid, so `--hot` is too, so every `color: var(--shell-danger)` (`:1490`, `:2220`) and the primary button's `background: var(--shell-primary-bg)`/`color: var(--shell-primary-text)` (`:725-727`) are invalid at computed-value time and fall back to inherit/unset. CONSEQUENCE: the destructive colour and the publish button's fill are missing under four of six palettes, and `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts:272` passes anyway - it asserts each block contains the 13 section 4 role *aliases*, and `--hot: var(--shell-danger)` satisfies it while the thing it aliases is absent. The test's own failure message names this exact defect ("it resolves to whatever the root happened to hold where the alias was written"), which is what makes the gap worth a row rather than a shrug. NOT MEASURED: the rendering under ember/moss/plum/light in a browser - the consequence above follows from CSS's computed-value rules, and the visible effect is predicted rather than seen. What would settle it: one capture of each of the four palettes with the publish button and a destructive affordance in frame, then a test that asserts each palette block declares the *source* of every alias it writes, not only the alias. CLOSED 2026-10-11 BY PLAN 7 TASK 4, WHICH THE ROW WAS HANDED. FIXED IN `a3d2c407`: all six palette blocks now declare `--shell-danger`, `--shell-primary-bg` and `--shell-primary-text` (light's missing `--shell-warm` with them), and graphite's danger is the drawing's own `--hot` `#ff7e6e`. ONE CLAIM IN THIS ROW IS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE CORRECTION: the four palettes' tokens were NOT guaranteed-invalid, because the baseline block is declared on the selector list `:root, [data-shell-palette="editorial"], .editor-shell-palette-swatch` and `:root` matches the same element the palette attribute is written to. Measured in the browser before the fix, `--shell-danger` under ember, moss, plum and light was `#a4291f` — editorial's dark red, inherited, not nothing — so the visible defect is the wrong palette's colour rather than a dropped declaration. The register-row consequence (an alias naming a source the block does not declare resolves from wherever the alias is written) stands as written. NOT DONE: the capture this row's own last paragraph asks for (each of the four palettes with the publish button in frame). The publish control is `.editor-shell-primary` in the shell header, which no registered capture frames; the browser half is asserted instead, and the capture remains open if the eye is still wanted.
check: `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts` test `declares the source of every role alias in every palette block` names four words of this row's own title (declares, source, alias, palette) and is the reading the row asked for: it walks `shellPalettes` and requires each palette's declaration block to contain every `--shell-*` token a section 4 alias can name, so an alias whose source is absent fails. RED BEFORE, GREEN AFTER, both re-run: against the pre-fix stylesheet the browser assertion in `design-language.spec.ts` reported `danger ember --shell-danger = "#a4291f"`, and the same four readings under moss, plum and light, all the baseline's value; on `a3d2c407` they read each palette's own `color-mix(in srgb, #ff7e6e 40%, <that palette's --shell-text>)`. `npm run test` from `src/web/` is 245 files and 3408 tests passed, and the three affected browser specs are 19 passed at `--workers=1`.

title: The settings modal's lead is 13px --shell-text, matching neither bible section 2's dialog title (15px) nor its eyebrow (10px muted)
detail:
FOUND BY THE SETTINGS-VS-MOCKUP MEASUREMENT OF 2026-10-10 (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/settings-vs-mockup-measurement.md), as the second of the two outright bible violations it found (the first is vg-294). MEASURED: the modal's lead line renders at 13px in `--shell-text`, which is neither of the two roles §2 gives a dialog - the title at 15px, or the eyebrow at 10px in a muted role - so it is a third size the scale does not contain, on the same pattern as the off-scale 12px radius vg-231 records. CONSEQUENCE: §2's type roles are how a dialog is recognisable as a dialog rather than as a panel, and a surface that invents a 13px step reads as a different component; it is also the kind of value §9's Acceptance counts, and no gate reads editor-shell.css to catch it (vg-274). LIKE vg-294 this needs no design ruling - a section names both candidate values, and which of the two the lead should take is a one-line decision the parity plan makes with the drawing in front of it. What would settle it: the lead resolves to one of §2's two dialog roles, with §9's scale carrying no 13px step. VERIFIED (2026-10-11, artefact 397fc91f, plan 8 Task 2 and its fix round 1). The lead now takes section 2's dialog title: `editor-shell.css`'s `.editor-shell-dialog-lead` is `font-size: var(--text-lg)` (15px) with no uppercase or tracking, ruled from `design-language.md:51` (`--text-lg` 15px, Dialog titles) and `:57` (Nothing else is uppercase). MEASURED ON THE BUILT BUNDLE: the parity row `settings modal - lead type` reads the drawing's `--text-lg` (15px) against `.editor-shell-dialog-lead` = 15px, GREEN, where it read 13px before this plan. THE RULE'S SPLIT IS PART OF THE VERIFICATION: the fix round rendered the theme library on the real host and saw its `role="status"` live region wearing the title class and reading as a second title under the buttons, so that node alone moved to `.editor-shell-dialog-status` (section 2's `:48`, `--text-xs` 11px, muted) and was re-observed at 11px. The four other dialogs that render the class - the two `

` titles and five `

` leads across `settings.tsx`, `shortcut-reference.tsx`, `new-document-chooser.tsx`, `replace-document-prompt.tsx` and `theme-library-dialog.tsx` - were uppercase at 13px before and are sentence case at 15px now, which is the same defect this row recorded, fixed once at its owner rather than per surface.
check: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` from `src/web/`, the row `settings modal — lead type`: the drawing's `--text-lg` (15px) against the product's `.editor-shell-dialog-lead`. Green at 15px on the rebuilt bundle at `397fc91f`; it read 13px and failed before plan 8.

title: The settings modal's overlay paints #0009 where bible section 3 mandates the scrim #00000073, which is also a hex literal section 10 forbids in a surface
detail: FOUND BY THE SETTINGS-VS-MOCKUP MEASUREMENT OF 2026-10-10 (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/settings-vs-mockup-measurement.md), which classified it as an outright violation rather than a difference. MEASURED: src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1111 sets `.editor-shell-dialog-overlay { background: #0009; }`, while bible §3's elevation table row 3 (modal) specifies `0 24px 60px #000000b3` with scrim `#00000073` (design-language.md:105). These are not two spellings of one value: #0009 is 60% black and #00000073 is 45%, so the product's scrim is a different, darker value AND an 8-digit-free hex literal inside a shipped surface, which §10 bans. THE ROW EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM vg-293 because it needs no design ruling: a section names the value. NOT FIXED HERE because the whole modal treatment is being corrected as one piece by the mockup-parity plan, and a lone scrim edit in a different commit would be the cramped patch rather than the coherent change - the same reason vg-293's radius is filed with vg-231's. What would settle it: the overlay resolves §3's scrim token, and the gated ratchet covers editor-shell.css so the literal cannot return (vg-274). VERIFIED (2026-10-11, artefact 51245173, plan 8 Task 3) ON THE PROPERTY, NOT ON THE FILE - and this row's own second clause is the reason the distinction is written down. `.editor-shell-dialog-overlay` renders `var(--elev-scrim)`, declared in `@theme static` beside the `--elev-*` shadows at `editor-shell.css:363` and pinned at section 3 elevation 3's `#00000073` (`design-language.md:105`); the `#0009` literal is gone from the surface, which is the section 10 half of this row. THE RATCHET HALF IS NOT MET AS WRITTEN: `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` holds 63 gated entries and NOT ONE is a `.css` file, `editor-shell.css` among the absent, so `vg-274`'s first clause still stands at 51245173 and the file's hex-literal count moving 7 to 6 is a manual re-run of that row's own ad-hoc measurement rather than a ratchet - nothing fails today if the literal returns. What makes the return impossible for THIS rule is the parity row `settings modal - scrim`, which compares `.editor-shell-dialog-overlay`'s rendered `background-color` against the `:root` token, and Task 3's red proof is that experiment: `#0009` reinstated and the row read `requires rgba(0, 0, 0, 115)` where the product rendered `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)`, restored with `cp` and proved with `cmp`. MEASURED ON THE BUILT BUNDLE by the task review's own run: 8 passed, 1 failed, the scrim row green and the red set exactly the three palette rows. THE FILE-WIDE RATCHET STAYS `vg-274`'s, whose counted ceiling is plan 8 Task 9's, still pending.
check: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` from `src/web/`, the row `settings modal — scrim`: the product's rendered `.editor-shell-dialog-overlay` background-color against `:root`'s `--elev-scrim`. Green on the rebuilt bundle at `51245173`; the row failed before plan 8 with the product rendering `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` where the token requires `rgba(0, 0, 0, 115)`.

title: The settings drawing declares an off-bible padding - 9px is not on §3's closed scale, so plan 8 would gate the modal against a stale drawing
detail: FOUND by plan 7 Task 8 fix round 1 on 2026-10-11, rendering the settings modal's switch row against its drawing. docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:90 declares `padding:9px 10px` on the follow-the-system row, and the product renders 8px vertical and 10px horizontal. §3 closes the spacing scale at `4,6,8,10,12,14,16,20,24,32`, so 9 is off-scale and THE DRAWING IS STALE, not the product - the direction Task 3 Step 1 already set for the three off-bible values inherited into shell.html from the originals. Owner: plan 8 (settings parity), which gates the modal's nineteen measured regions against this drawing and would otherwise read the product's correct 8px as a drift; the repair is a Step-1-equivalent inside plan 8, correcting the drawing to the bible and never the reverse. Found while doing Task 8, so it is filed rather than fixed here. VERIFIED (2026-10-11, artefact f735c81b, plan 8 Task 6). The drawing is corrected and not the product, which is the direction this row named. MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:89` now declares `padding:8px 10px` - §3's own step (`design-language.md:69` closes the scale at `4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32`) - and the only other lines the commit touched are the TWO parity rows whose `mockupSelector` strings embed that literal: `mockup-values.ts:876` (the box's `border-radius` row) and `:887` (its `gap` row), each of which would otherwise have addressed no element at all. The product needed no change, because it already renders §3's `--space-8` and `--space-10`; the box's licence is §5 rule 2's own sentence (`:167-171`), which names this exact shape - 'a switch row whose label fills the row inside a panel box ... keeps the shape it is drawn with'. VERIFIED BY RUN, not by reading the strings: the fixture parity test (the rows whose `surface` is `fixture`) passes, and it reads those rows through `lookup`/`addressed`, which throws on a selector matching nothing (`mockup-values.ts:317`) or matching more than one (`:325`); the settings parity test's red set is unchanged at four rows, all the Keyboard panel's. NO INSET ROW WAS ADDED, and the reason the row predicted is now measured too: the drawing writes the shorthand, `padding` is in `SHORTHANDS_SETTING` (`:348-351`), and `lookup` (`:364-380`) throws on a shorthand that sets a longhand a row reads - so a `padding-top` row is impossible without weakening plan 7's guard, and the drawing's declared spacing is Task 8's widened drawings gate instead.
check: `grep -c "padding:9px 10px" docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` from the repo root returns 0 (the off-scale value is gone and the drawing declares §3's `8px 10px`), and from `src/web/` `npx playwright test tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` passes the fixture row that reads the box's `border-radius` and `gap` through those two rewritten `mockupSelector` strings at `f735c81b`.

title: The well's resting 1px boundary reads at 2.15:1 in graphite and 1.42:1 in light, below the 3:1 bible section 5 asks of a control boundary
detail: FOUND BY THE DESIGN-LANGUAGE PARITY GATE (this plan, task 4) on the gate's first green run, and it is a token rather than a control. MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, not modelled: `design-language.spec.ts` hides the text, screenshots the page, samples the pixel under each control and composites the computed border colour over it, so the numbers include whatever alpha the token carries and whatever gradient sits beneath. Six control states pass in all six palettes - label, refusal, selected, value, checked and focus; this one does not. The well is `--panel-2` fill plus a 1px `--edge` border, which is bible section 5's vocabulary exactly, so the composite is the token's own: graphite `rgba(221,244,238,0.26)` over `rgb(11,18,22)` = 2.15:1 (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:127`) and light `rgba(38,70,56,0.20)` over `rgb(246,254,250)` = 1.42:1 (`:242`). The other four palettes read 5.5-18.4:1 because their `--shell-edge` is opaque.
