title: Layer rows declare draggable but nothing consumes the drop, so reordering by drag does nothing
detail:
MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a row that does not reorder is only a finding if reordering is a thing the panel is offering. It is: every layer row carries draggable="true" in the DOM, which is an explicit promise that an HTML5 drag will be received and acted on. Nothing acts on it. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title changes the list not at all - the first eight rows are byte-identical before and after. That is true for a mouse drag and also for Playwright's dragTo, which is the technique that drives HTML5 drag-and-drop rather than mouse events, so this is not my probe using the wrong gesture. THE OPERATION ITSELF WORKS, which is what makes the dead attribute a real cost rather than an unimplemented feature: select the date text on the canvas, right-click, Bring to front, and the host's document moves date from index 6 to index 51 and every other object shifts down. So an author who wants to reorder can, by finding a context menu; an author who tries to drag, which is what the attribute invites and what every other layer panel in this class of tool invites, silently does nothing and gets no feedback. THE HONEST MITIGATING FACTOR: the row's cursor is default, not grab, so the panel does not visually advertise dragging - the promise is in the markup, not in the pixels. That is why this is filed as a smaller row than it first looks, and why the fix could legitimately be to drop the attribute rather than to implement the drop. What I would not accept is leaving an attribute that says draggable on an element where drag does nothing, because it is a false statement the next agent or the next tool will believe. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But the drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-vigilia-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents, the target row carries the same vigilia-layer-row class as before, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule. That is the row worth keeping, and it is filed as vg-099. vg-096 is CONFIRMED by the same measurement: cursor is auto on a draggable row. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But that drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-vigilia-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents the target row carries the same vigilia-layer-row class as before the drag began, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule - and cannot tell which case they are in until nothing happens. Filed as vg-099.

 CROSS-LINK, deliberately NOT withdrawn, for the same reason as vg-056: the drag handler lives in a panel being replaced, but drag-to-reorder is a requirement that has to be carried into the composition panel. The polish spec records it and the redesign's section 3 keeps row-level commands, so the requirement is carried in docs - but this row is the only place the DOM advertises draggable with nothing consuming the drop, and that advertisement has to not survive the rewrite.
check: `bridge.ts` `reorderLayer` consumes `draggable`; `bridge.dom.test.ts` proves sibling reorder. Residual cross-group refusal is `vg-099` (verified)

title: Fabric's coordinate cache goes stale after the authored box is restored, so the selection frame, snapping and arrange work off the pre-pass size
detail: FOUND WHILE REFUTING vg-109, and it is the real artefact under that row's wrong measurement. assertBoxWidth and assertBoxHeight in scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts:130,150 assign width and height DIRECTLY rather than through set, because a set re-enters initDimensions and would widen the object again - that is why they bypass it. But Fabric's aCoords is a separate cache, and bypassing set leaves it describing the PREVIOUS size. getBoundingRect() is makeBoundingBoxFromPoints(this.getCoords()), so everything that reads an object's box through the canvas reads a stale one: the SELECTION FRAME an author drags by, the SNAP positions the guides are computed against, and ARRANGE, which aligns selected objects to each other's edges. Measured: one text object read 172.78 x 102.7 stale, and 141 x 28.12 after a single dirty = true; setCoords(). A direct assignment or a setCoords after the restore would both be guesses until established, so the fix is to find where the pass leaves the object and mark it dirty once there - not to sprinkle setCoords at every reader. Left alone by the agent that found it because scene-fabric/ was held by another agent at the time, which is the disjoint-ownership rule working rather than a gap in it. This is worth its own row and its own dispatch: vg-089 already made a textbox's height a cache of its box, and this is the cost of that arrangement showing up somewhere the previous work did not measure.
check: `authored-box.ts` `markBoxWritten` sets `dirty` and `setCoords` where the pass restores the box

title: group() leaves every member cached box stale, so a bounding rect read right after Ctrl+G is the pre-grouping box
detail:
AMENDED after an independent review measured every consumer, because the row as first filed would have sent a fixer to two safe sites and past the broken one.

grouping-manager/index.ts:185 builds `new Group(members)`, which rewrites each member into group-local coordinates and leaves Fabric's aCoords cache holding the pre-grouping box. setCoords() is the only thing that refreshes it.

MEASURED, ON A 1200x800 ARTBOARD: before group() outside=5 of 30; immediately after, outside=11 of 30, which is what the artboard panel reads; after renderAll() outside=10; only after a forced refresh does it return to 5. An author who groups two objects sees "11 of 30 outside" when 5 are.

TWO OF THE SEVEN CONSUMERS FIRST LISTED ARE NOT AFFECTED. snap-manager/bounds.ts:71 calls setCoords() on the line immediately before getBoundingRect(), so snapping is immune - measured, it returns the correct 421 rather than the stale 983. scene-fabric/src/glass.ts:584 likewise refreshes what it samples. arrange.ts reads getBoundingRect() with no refresh, but its members are no longer canvas roots after grouping, so reaching it needs a gesture the current UI does not offer - weaker than first claimed, not zero.

THE ONE CONSUMER THAT IS BROKEN is the crop count: scene-fabric/artboard-crop.ts:167 walks getObjects() recursively including children, so it reads the stale cache. Note that renderAll() only partially heals it, 11 to 10, because the glass sampler touches the card's frosted Rect but not its other six members - cpu-card-icon, -title, -value, -caption, -sparkline and -freq all stay stale.

ALSO RECORDED because it is incidental and therefore fragile: renderAll() does NOT refresh the cache by design. It appeared to, only because glass.ts:584 - an unrelated frosted-glass sampler - happens to call setCoords() on what it samples. A change to the glass renderer could silently reintroduce this, so nothing may cite "renderAll does not refresh" as a property of Fabric.
check: `member.setCoords()` follows `new Group(members)` on both paths

title: The player fit-mode spec intermittently measures nothing inside fit-contain, in a suite that gates merges
detail: FOUND ON THE FULL GATE WHILE CLOSING vg-119, and it is not this sweep: nothing in b29ccc21..HEAD touches display-fabric.spec.ts, background-media.ts or anything they read. MEASURED: the serial full gate collected 410 and reported 409 passed / 1 failed, the one being tests/e2e/display-fabric.spec.ts draws each fit mode, and every icon, in its own box - "fit-contain drew nothing inside its own box", expected > 0.05, received 0. Re-run on its own, --repeat-each 3, that is 6 collected and 6 passed, so it is an intermittent and not a standing red. The claim is the INK, measured inside the box the fit mode is supposed to fill, and a reading of exactly 0 is what a frame that had not painted yet looks like - the same class as the chart-palette status race vg-131 recorded, where an action arrives before the surface has settled. NOT DIAGNOSED: whether it is the player waiting for a decode, the probe sampling before the first paint, or a genuine intermittent in the fit path is not established, and the one thing established is that 3 samples is not enough to call it fixed either. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: --repeat-each 20 on that spec with the ink reading captured per run, which separates a paint that is late from a fit that is wrong in a way that only sometimes shows. The base was green - STATUS.md at b29ccc21 records 252 passed 0 failed 0 flaky - so this appeared somewhere between there and here, and that is not narrowed to this sweep because this sweep did not touch the surface.

title: colour-picker.tsx reaches past the vendored popover to @radix-ui/react-popover directly, so two wrappers own one primitive and the spec's own "incoherence" survives the plan that was written to end it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 9'S AUTHORING PASS while verifying what §8 left it, and verified here against the source rather than taken from the report. `packages/editor/src/components/ui/colour-picker.tsx:1` and `packages/editor/src/components/ui/popover.tsx:1` both import `* as PopoverPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-popover"`, so the colour picker does not go through the vendored shadcn wrapper that the rest of the editor uses. WHY IT MATTERS: the spec names this as its motivating example -- §8's table row reads `popover | both -- the incoherence` (`:429`), and the paragraph above it says the app has 'two primitive libraries and two popover implementations'. Plan 9 migrates the five Base UI imports to Radix, which ends the two-LIBRARY half of that. It does not end the two-WRAPPER half, and plan 9's author named it Out of scope rather than folding it in. THE COST IS NOT COSMETIC: a change to the shared wrapper -- its accessibility attributes, its positioning, or a `--shell-*` token it should carry -- does not reach the colour picker, and nothing reddens when the two drift apart, because each is correct in isolation. That is the same shape as the two-ScenePlan-builders defect (vg-176) that this session fixed one layer down: duplication is invisible until the copies disagree. NOT A BLOCKER and not part of the redesign's acceptance: this is a pre-release internal duplication the repo may break cleanly, which is why it is a row and not a task inside plan 9. Whoever takes it should decide which wrapper is the owner -- keeping colour-picker's direct use and deleting the vendored one, or routing the picker through the wrapper -- and that is a small design decision rather than a rename.
check: `colour-picker.tsx` imports `@base-ui/react/popover`; no `@radix-ui` import in the editor

title: display-fabric's repaint check times out on every run, so the assertion that the update loop reaches the canvas never executes
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 9 PHASE 1'S BOUNDARY while re-reading a full browser suite that had reported 21 unexpected on a loaded box. THE MEASUREMENT, which separates this from a flake rather than from a hunch: `npx playwright test display-fabric --workers=1 --repeat-each=3` collected 144 and reported 6 unexpected, and all six are the SAME test - `keeps repainting as samples arrive`, two projects by three repeats - every one a `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded`. One run of it alone fails 2 of 2 the same way. So this is a STANDING RED, not an intermittent: different from `vg-140`, which files an intermittent in the same file but a different test (`draws each fit mode, and every icon, in its own box`, an ink reading of exactly 0), and different from the 30 s timeouts that appeared in the same suite under load and vanished when the spec set was re-run alone. **NOT ATTRIBUTED TO THE DIFF IN THE TREE, and that was measured rather than argued:** the same spec was run at `af499716` with the 22 `@radix-ui/*` packages reinstalled and both builds rebuilt, and it fails there identically - 2 collected, 2 unexpected, both 30 s timeouts. WHAT IT COSTS: the test's whole subject is that the player repaints when telemetry samples arrive, and its own comment records that the failure was verified by sabotage - `handle.update(plan())` cut, and it goes red. A test that times out before reaching its assertion cannot play that role, so the coverage this file believes it has for the update loop is currently absent rather than passing. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the shape narrows it to two candidates: the body awaits `openCanvasPlayer(page)`, reads the artboard canvas with `toDataURL()`, then awaits `page.clock.runFor(4000)` - Playwright's FAKE clock, standing in for the player's once-a-second plan rebuild - and reads the canvas again. A 30 s timeout on that sequence is a readiness wait that never resolves, so either the player never reaches the state `openCanvasPlayer` waits for, or the fake clock never advances it because the player schedules its rebuild off something `page.clock` does not drive. THE NEXT STEP is to separate those two and it is cheap: log which await the timeout lands on, and whether the artboard canvas is non-empty at the first read. A row rather than an immediate fix because the owner is not established - `openCanvasPlayer` is a shared helper several specs read, so a change there is not this file's to make alone - and because a fake clock that fails to drive a real timer is a decision about how the player is tested rather than a defect in one assertion.
check: `display-fabric.spec.ts` deleted by `ad94e5ed`; no `page.clock` caller remains. **See §3.3**

title: The visual-evidence README claims every capture uses `?static=1` and a controlled clock, which is false for the editor's captures
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 9's implementer while doing the parity capture, and REPORTED rather than obeyed: the brief it worked from carried the same sentence forward and told it to use `?static=1` and the controlled clock, and the implementer checked, found the editor has neither, used the harness the two existing editor captures use, and flagged the instruction as stale. MEASURED before filing, because 'the editor has no static mode' is the kind of claim that is easy to make and cheap to check. docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:14-15 states, as a rule for every capture: 'Captures use `?static=1` and a controlled clock.' Neither half holds for the editor. (1) The editor reads exactly ONE query parameter — packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:383 is bootTheme(window.location.search, libraryClient), which is `?theme`. There is no `static` branch anywhere in the editor bundle. (2) Every `?static=1` in the browser suite is against the HOST/PLAYER: tests/e2e/clip-parity.spec.ts:535, display-fabric.spec.ts:757, host-bleed.spec.ts:35 and :64, all `page.goto(`${HOST}/...`)`; and tests/e2e/canvas-probe.ts:201, which appends the parameter for the player probes, is imported by exactly three specs — display-fabric.spec.ts, host-player.spec.ts, player-chrome.spec.ts — none of them an editor spec. (3) No editor capture pins a clock: the shared capture helper tests/e2e/editor-canvas.ts contains no setFixedTime or setSystemTime, and neither editor.spec.ts's captures nor design-language.spec.ts's pin one. WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG: the README is the instructions a capture author follows, and this sentence sent one looking for a static mode and a pinned clock the editor has never had. It cost this task a rebuild-and-check cycle and a paragraph of report, and a less careful implementer would have 'fixed' it by pausing Date in a spec, which would have changed the capture's evidence rather than its accuracy. It is the same failure shape as a vacuous gate: an instruction that reads as authoritative, cannot be satisfied, and is not checked by anything. NOTE THE EDITOR CAPTURES ARE TIME-DEPENDENT BY DESIGN — the starter clock and the live chart values are real — which is why the correct replacement is not 'the editor also gets a fixed clock' but a sentence that says which captures the rule is about. The README ALREADY CONTAINS the narrower truth elsewhere: its `## Settings page` table names `desktop-host` and `publish` projects for the captures that drive the host. NOT FIXED IN TASK 9 because its brief scopes README changes to registering the new action, and because the right replacement sentence is a decision — the blanket claim about 'captures' has to become a claim about the player/host captures — which is the README owner's to make once. OWNER: whoever owns docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md. SEVERITY: low — documentation only; no capture is wrong today, and every editor capture that exists demonstrably works without either mechanism.
check: the README now scopes `?static=1` to player captures and says why the editor cannot

title: The drawing's token table is read as a set from the one element the width selector matches, so a token the drawing declares at the root or on a child of the drawn shell is invisible to the assertion that exists to catch it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-11) OF ITS OWN NEW ASSERTION, at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/re-review-task4-round1.md`. MEASURED BY READING THE READER: `mockup-values.ts`'s `mockupDeclaredProperties` resolves the drawing's table through the element that carries the table (`[style*="width:1180px"]`, unique in `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html`), and the new set-equality case asserts that element's declared token names equal the eleven the test maps. That closes the hole it was written for - a twelfth token added to that same declaration is now red, where before it was invisible, which is how `--hot` arrived unnoticed by a row that listed ten. What it cannot see is a token declared anywhere else the drawing draws from: `:root`, or a child element that re-declares a `--shell-*` shadowing the table. CONSEQUENCE: a palette role the drawing gains outside its own table would still be invisible, so the assertion's coverage is 'the table', not 'the drawing'. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawing's style block does declare anything at `:root` today - the shell's tokens are on the one element, and nothing was found elsewhere - so this is a ceiling rather than a live miss. What would settle it: a ruling on whether the reader should walk the drawing's whole style block for `--*` declarations, or whether the one element is the drawing's contract by definition and a token anywhere else is a drawing defect to correct. Related: `vg-304`, which records that a parity row is never checked against the property set its drawing declares.
check: `design-language.spec.ts:3160` "the shell drawing declares its token table at one site" reads **every** custom-property declaration in the drawing, keys them by kind and owner, asserts there is exactly one site, and carries a positive control — so a `:root` or child declaration reddens it. **Moved here from `work` on §7's second slice; see §8.14**

title: The settings drawing names the surface as an eyebrow inside the nav column while the product names it once as the dialog's title, and neither side draws the other's
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8'S FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW (2026-10-11), which caught the difference list claiming to be exhaustive without it: `adjudication.md` says task 10's list disposes of every drawing-versus-product difference still open after the re-run, and this one is in neither L1-L4 nor D6-D10 nor any row in `vg-316`-`vg-327`. MEASURED, both sides at `file:line`: the drawing draws `Settings` as a nav eyebrow - `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:23`, `font:600 10px/1`, `letter-spacing:.11em`, uppercase, `color:var(--faint)`, `padding:4px 8px 8px`, inside the `width:150px` column - while the product renders no nav eyebrow and names the surface once, above the whole nav-plus-panel row, as `<h2 class="editor-shell-dialog-lead">` at `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/settings.tsx:342`, which `editor-shell.css:1451-1455` sets to `--text-lg` (the declaration is `:1454`). Neither side draws the other's element. THE LICENCE CANDIDATE, and it covers half the difference: §2 `:51` gives `--text-lg` 15px to "Dialog titles", so the product's title role and its size are on-bible and are not a defect - the census's row `#5` rules exactly that, and the parity row `settings modal — lead type` holds it. THE QUESTION THE LICENCE DOES NOT ANSWER: whether the nav should ALSO carry the surface name, which is the duplication `task-2-report.md:49-53` refused when it ruled one name for one surface. That refusal was reasoned, so this is a design question rather than a defect - but it lived only in `task-2-report.md`, which is git-ignored scratch, which is why it is filed here rather than left to prose. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on whether the drawing's eyebrow is how the drawing labels a column (and the current set is the stale side, which `docs/design/mockups/README.md`'s treatment-copied-from-the-original rule argues against correcting), or whether it is a second place the surface is named and the drawing is stale on it - then a `PARITY` row either way, because the eyebrow is a value of one element on the drawing's side and nothing on the product's. IT IS NOT `vg-319`, which is the shared `h3` group heading's type at 11px / `.12em` against §2's eyebrow; this is the nav's missing eyebrow, a different element. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): one name. Plan 8 Task 2's refusal stands -- one name for one surface -- and section 2 (`:51`) already licenses `--text-lg` for 'Dialog titles', so the product's title role and size are on-bible and are not a defect; the drawing's eyebrow is how the drawing labels a column rather than a second naming. The refusal is written here because it lived only in `task-2-report.md`, which is git-ignored scratch. RE-READ UNDER `vg-330`: with Settings as a pane the surface is named once in the pane's own header rather than in a dialog title, so the PRINCIPLE survives and the location moves.
check: the user ruled it: one name, and §2 already licenses the title role

title: The plain single-object drag-snap now has no test, and whether it is a distinct path from the composed-selection drag is unestablished
detail: FOUND BY the one-off screenshot pass (task 1 of 2026-10-11), which deleted the capture block 'snaps a dragged object to a neighbour and shows a guide' from src/web/tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts (was :3642) with its PNG docs/evidence/screenshots/editor-snap-guides-desktop-chromium.png. NO ASSERTION WAS LOST: that block asserted only that the canvas was visible, and the guide it was named for is never read in it. WHAT IT WAS THE LAST TO DO: it was the only test performing a plain, unmodified, SINGLE-OBJECT drag across a snap line. Every surviving drag-snap assertion is a composed selection - 'snaps a two-object selection as a unit' (editor.spec.ts:3808) and the positive control inside 'refuses a snap gesture for a scaled text selection' (:3839) both call dragToLine on a two-object ActiveSelection and assert the left edge lands on the line - and the only single-object drag left is the Ctrl-modified one (:3716), which asserts the snap is SUPPRESSED. The guide-as-pixels assertion also survives, but for other gestures: positively for resize (:3805, snapped.guidePixels > 100) and as zero for the Ctrl resize (:3690). WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A LOST CHECK: whether a lone object and a composed selection reach the same drag-snap route is unestablished, and nobody owns that question. WHAT WAS READ, AND WHAT WAS NOT: the test citations above were read at HEAD; snap-manager's drag entry was read only far enough to see that one object:moving handler (src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/index.ts:343) serves every drag while startGesture branches on ActiveSelection for eligibility (:206-:210), which is a real difference between a lone object and a selection and is NOT evidence that the snapping itself differs. The resolver was not read. OWNER: whoever owns snap-manager's drag path. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: reading the drag-snap path to see whether a lone object and a composed selection take the same route - if they do, close this row with that reading rather than with a new test.
check: one `object:moving` binding serves every drag; `startGesture`'s only branch is selection eligibility

title: The unit display options are four hardcoded English strings while every other list in the editor is Intl-derived
detail: REFUTED, and the refutation was already in the code when this row was filed. TWO claims; neither survives. (1) "ask Intl for these rather than write them". The probe was already run and recorded at ui-copy.ts:386-401, and re-run here independently: Intl.supportedValuesOf("unitDisplay") THROWS RangeError, Intl.DisplayNames.of("unitDisplay") throws RangeError (its six types are language, region, script, currency, calendar, dateTimeField), and Intl.supportedValuesOf("unit") is the 45 sanctioned UNITS OF MEASUREMENT (acre, byte, celsius), not the ways to display one. None of the four labels is a platform string: short and long are the platforms unitDisplay VALUES with no name attached, none is rejected outright (Intl.NumberFormat unitDisplay:"none" throws RangeError), and "Default" is the ABSENCE of the key rather than a word. (2) "every other list in the editor is Intl-derived, so a theme authored in another language meets four English words in the middle of an otherwise translated inspector". Two halves, both wrong. requirements.md §35 states "Multiple locales are not in scope for product UI copy; a theme declares the language its own text is written in" - the inspector is not translated, so there is no otherwise-translated middle for four English words to sit in. And the other lists are not Intl-derived either: ui-copy.ts carries artboardOrientations, artboardResolutions and fitModes as hand-written tables in the same object as the unit options (lines 378-385). THEME_LANGUAGES is the one genuinely Intl-labelled list, and its comment says why the LIST is hand-owned while the LABELS are not. WHAT THE ROW GOT RIGHT, and why it is still not a defect: the options were once written twice, in runs.ts and in the chart panel, so a rename fixed one and missed the other. That is fixed - the four options now live once in ui-copy.ts as unitDisplayOptions and both panels read them. The table is an OWNER, not a localisation debt. NO CODE CHANGED: the fix the row asks for would replace four correct strings with four undefined ones.
check: the unit display options are four hardcoded English strings in `ui-copy.ts`, the one owner both panels read

title: The reuse gate watchlists the repo-root scripts/ as a prefix, so a script directory under src/web/ is never gated
detail: FOUND WHILE LANDING THE FONT CATALOGUE GENERATOR, whose task brief instructed me to write a decision note first because scripts/ is on the gate watchlist and src/web/scripts/ is under it. Measured: it is not. reuse-gate.mjs:53 resolves every candidate path against the repo ROOT, so the watchlist entry scripts/ matches only a path whose repo-relative form begins scripts/ - and src/web/scripts/generate-font-trios.mjs does not. Piping that path into the gate returns 0 (allowed), while scripts/anything.mjs returns 2 (refused). So the second scripts/ directory in the repo is ungated and an agent can add a generator there without ever meeting the seven rungs. I landed the note anyway, because being told to is right and the gap is not mine to close silently, but the gate is not doing what its watchlist reads as saying. The fix is a judgement, not a typo: either add src/web/scripts/ as its own entry, or widen the matching so a bare directory name matches at any depth - which is the same shape as the bare-gitignore-pattern rule the repo already follows and would also catch a scripts/ under packages/. Worth deciding deliberately, because widening it means deciding what else under a path called scripts/ is a mechanism boundary.
check: `matchesDirectory` matches a bare watchlist entry at any depth, so the reuse gate covers a script directory under `src/web/`; probe exits 2

title: Five more tests read the camera as a constant, found by changing the default camera after vg-136 was fixed
detail: FOUND BY THE SABOTAGE RUN AGAINST vg-136, which is why it is filed rather than never noticed: setting DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to `9:19.5` and rebuilding makes five more tests fail, and all five are the SAME defect class vg-136 just fixed - a measurement that reads the camera as a constant - and all five are PRE-EXISTING and outside vg-136's diff. THREE fail inside `assertBlur`. glass-probe.ts:261 builds the sampled band as `bandTop + Math.max(8, Math.floor(height * 0.25))`: the 0.25 term scales with the camera because `height` is the panel's device box, but the 8 is a literal DEVICE-row floor, so the two halves of one expression disagree about which space they are in. glass-authoring.spec.ts:207, :323 and :420 all land there. TWO fail on snapping.spec.ts's GUIDE_ROWS_PRESENT (50) and GUIDE_ROWS_ABSENT (20), which count device rows carrying the guide colour. The file's own comment says 'the artboard is 600 scene px tall, so a real guide covers hundreds of device rows' - hundreds AT THE ZOOM IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. At the artboard's full height in device rows that count is 600 * zoom, so the 50 floor is a floor on the camera in the same way RAW_TOLERANCE was, and reference-theme.spec.ts:1595 fails on the same measurement. THE POINT IS NOT FIVE FAILURES, IT IS THE SHAPE. vg-136 repaired three tests that read the camera as a constant and proved the repair under a changed camera; this row is the remainder of that same audit, and it exists because the audit's instrument - change the default camera and re-run - found more than the row it was run for. The device lens is not the first thing to move that camera: every one of these would break again on the next zoom control, the next lens, or a window resize, and none of them names the camera in its failure message the way the repaired snapping assertions now do. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: it is a different set of files from vg-136's three (glass-probe.ts is a shared helper read by several specs, and the guide-row constants sit among tests vg-136 did not touch), and it is a scope decision rather than a defect on its own. Worth deciding together whether the honest repair is per-constant derivation from liveZoom, or one shared helper that converts a scene measurement into the device pixels a given assertion is about - the second would stop the next row being needed. MEASURED on this Windows box by setting DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to 9:19.5, rebuilding the editor, and running the three specs under playwright.config.ts. Not verified on any other camera: portrait is the one that was measured, and Fit at 0.98 passes these today.
check: the camera's band floor and the guide rows derive from the same measurement; no test reads it as a constant

title: The plus cannot dismiss the chooser it opened, though it announces that it can
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, reasoned from source and not measured in a browser. shell-layout.tsx:487 is `onInsert={() => setInsertOpen(true)}`, unconditional, and InsertPopover renders no Menu.Trigger because it anchors to addRef instead (insert-popover.tsx:87-89). Pressing the + while the chooser is showing therefore cannot close it: the handler only ever sets true, and the outside-press dismissal is the only thing that closes the popup. That contradicts the buttons own contract, which Task 1 added: pane-bar.tsx:80-84 sets aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded from the same state, so a screen reader is told this is a menu button that toggles when it does not. Low severity and unclaimed rather than contradicted by the spec, which says only that the + offers both halves. NOT FIXED AFTER THE CLOSE because it is a behaviour change to a closed plan, and the register owns it: the fix is to make the handler toggle, and it then needs a browser case proving the second press closes rather than reopening.
check: `insert-popover.tsx` is deleted and with it the chooser the plus opened; no `InsertPopover` survives

title: The status strip's background flattens two tones the mockup draws differently
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 4's task review. The checked reference paints a background on the status strip at docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:226 whose VALUE is #0e1217 - the rail's tone - while the implementation uses var(--panel) (editor-shell.css:485), which is the header's --shell-surface tone. So the mockup draws the header lighter than the strip and the implementation makes them the same tone; the implementer's report claimed the strip 'matches the mockup', which is true of the presence of a background and false of its value. RULED defensible and kept: bible section 4 forbids the hex and there is no darker token in the palette to match #0e1217, so var(--panel) is the only on-scale choice available today. The difference is therefore a real divergence from the checked reference rather than a bug, and it needs listing rather than fixing. OWNER: Task 10's difference list (plan 2 phase 3) is the natural home - it exists to enumerate exactly this kind of gap between the design language and the implementation. SEVERITY: low - one tone where the mockup has two; visible only side by side. CORRECTED (§8.2) 2026-10-12: the citations above are the pre-fix stylesheet's, and one of them is gone at HEAD. Measured at HEAD: `editor-shell.css:485` is `--color-shell-edge` inside the `@theme inline` token block (`--color-shell-warm` is the next one but three, at `:489`), not the status strip, so the cited line holds nothing of this row; the strip's `background: var(--panel)` is at `:678` inside `.editor-shell-status` (`:669`). §8.2's mapping (`:1400` and `:1353-1357`/`:1368` for `:1503` and `:1470-1476`/`:1480-1486`) covers neither `:485` nor this rule, so the number was measured at HEAD rather than substituted from the mapping. The VALUE is unchanged — still `var(--panel)`, still one tone where the mockup draws `#0e1217` at `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:227`, `:226` being the blank line above it — so the finding stands and only its citation moved.
check: the Task 10 difference list records the status strip's background against the mockup and rules it defensible

title: The stored-document base and the save protocol gated on it are a domain with its own lifecycle living in the composition root, with no row in the ownership map
detail: FOUND by a read-only architecture survey the user asked for ('does any domain manager need clean-up — same domain spread across a few managers, a domain under another owner that should be its own'), run on 2026-10-09 with docs/architecture/ownership.md as the yardstick. Shape (b): a coherent domain nested inside another owner. editor-session.ts holds roughly 250 lines of a sub-domain — which stored document this session descends from, the hashes it declared, and the bytes a save may omit: LibraryBase/libraryBase() (:95-118), the field (:216), construction (:238-241), #saveLibrary (:756-775), #writeLibrary (:782-818), #libraryPayload (:835-858), #resolveConflict (:867-893), #openLibrary (:895-928), and the base cleared at :913, :934, :956 and :962. It has its own invariant (the base must be cleared at every document replacement, so four clear sites must be kept in step), its own failure mode (ThemeConflictError, surfaced as reload/overwrite/dismiss; transport at theme-library-client.ts:31-58) and its own payload policy (#libraryPayload is asset policy, not wiring). WHY IT IS A MANAGER QUESTION: the map has a row for 'Theme download — persistence-manager/' (:73) and for the v2 file boundary (:90), and NONE for the library base or the save protocol, so nothing states the rule 'a save with no base is a first save' (:835-841) in one place. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether it deserves a manager of its own or should stay in the session with a map row added — that decision is the deliverable. It is also the larger half of what puts editor-session.ts at 1246 lines against the repo's 800 stop. OWNER: unassigned. SEVERITY: low today (it works), medium as a reading hazard. CORRECTED (§8.8, §8.11) 2026-10-12: the citations above are pre-extraction, and the census verdict that confirmed this row is superseded. `248ff08f` extracted the sub-domain to `src/web/packages/editor/src/theme-library-manager/index.ts` (303 lines) and added the ownership map row for it at `docs/architecture/ownership.md:75` (`editor/src/theme-library-manager/`), so the owner path is no longer unassigned; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 248ff08f HEAD` is true, so `manager-census.md:397`'s verdict — 'still in `editor-session.ts`, and the map has no row' — predates that commit and is stale. `editor-session.ts` is 1077 lines now, not 1246, and delegates (`saveLibrary: () => this.#library.save()` at `:588`), so the line numbers above no longer hold. The census is not edited here; this note corrects the row.
check: `248ff08f` extracted `theme-library-manager/` and added the ownership map row for the stored-document base and the save protocol gated on it

title: The authored text box stores the scaled width, which the shared writer's own comment says would grow the box on every pass
detail: FOUND by a read-only architecture survey the user asked for ('does any domain manager need clean-up — same domain spread across a few managers, a domain under another owner that should be its own'), run on 2026-10-09 with docs/architecture/ownership.md as the yardstick. VERIFIED BY ME by reading both writers. authored-box.ts:196-197 documents writeAuthoredBoxDimension as 'The single write every geometry surface shares'. The writers half was fixed on 2026-10-12 by Task 9 candidate rank 4 (commit dd7c3365): all three now call the helper and both inline writers are gone. The units half survives — text-manager/index.ts still passes target.width * scaleX. The three disagree about units, and the source says which is right: authored-box.ts:70-74 'vigiliaText.box is scene units; Fabric's width is the same box before scaleX', and writeAuthoredBoxDimension seeds with the UNSCALED object.width/object.height under a comment (:216) reading 'Seeding with the scaled value would grow the box on every pass'. text-manager/index.ts:90 does exactly that — width: target.width * scaleX. Because boxFrom (authored-box.ts:42-62) multiplies by scaleX on read, storing the scaled value makes the read-back scaleX squared for a scaled object. (CORRECTED 2026-10-12, measured: the read-back is NOT scaleX squared -- the stored box and the object's own width are one number, because assertBox copies the box onto the width -- and what the scaled write does instead is shrink the object by scaleX on every resize. See the SETTLED paragraph below.) The inline writers also skip the helper's refusals: the value < 1 / non-finite guard (:203) and the sibling-dimension seeding (:209-223) that exists so an object never loses its width. NOT ESTABLISHED: reachability — the survey could not trace whether scaleX can be non-1 when adoptResizedBox runs, since the width guard puts object.width back before object:resizing reports and whether it resets scaleX is untraced. What would settle it: one browser check, scale a text object, drag a side handle, compare vigiliaText.box.width against width * scaleX. THAT RUN HAS NOW HAPPENED. SETTLED 2026-10-12 (Task 2.1 and its fix round 1, commit 6cec8acf): the check ran and the row's mechanism is right about the defect and wrong about its shape. At scaleX 0.7432 a 240-unit mr drag landed the edge 62.4156816858345 scene units short of the pointer -- 177.584 for 240 asked, the request times scaleX -- while the stored box and the object's own width agreed throughout (the log's boxAfter and fabricWidth are one double), because assertBox copies the stored box onto the width on the next pass. So the read-back is NOT scaleX squared; what a scaled write does is leave the object scaleX times the size the author dragged to, which is the user-visible half. Writing target.width unscaled in adoptResizedBox lands the same drag within 1.31 units and the case passes; restoring target.width * scaleX fails it on the landing arm (Expected: < 2 | Received: 62.4156816858345, C:/tmp/vg21/RUN-RED.json), so the close rests on a case that fails on this defect. The comparison this row asked for -- vigiliaText.box.width against width * scaleX -- is NOT the discriminator and is not asserted as one: the two are equal under either write, since assertBox makes them the same number. Reachability, the row's other open half, is answered: the resize path does run for a scaled text, with scaleX 0.7432 at the write, reached by a real corner drag. selection-inspector/index.ts is a file another agent is mid-task on, so that writer may be moving. NEAR ROWS: vg-057 (verified, the half-box), vg-109, vg-112 — none names the three writers. OWNER: scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts, which already claims the job and should hold the only writer. SEVERITY: medium if reachable, low if the guard makes it unreachable — hence the one check first.
check: `editor.spec.ts`'s "resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote" measures what the authored box stores when a scaled text is resized: the starter wordmark is scaled to `scaleX` 0.7432 by a real corner drag, its `mr` handle is dragged 240 scene units, and the case asserts the resized edge lands where the pointer asked (within 2 units). With the scaled write in `adoptResizedBox` that arm FAILS -- the 240-unit request lands at 177.58431831416544, so the shortfall is 62.4156816858345 (exactly `asked - landed`). CORRECTED 2026-10-12: this row also called that landing 'the request times `scaleX`', and it is not -- 240 x 0.7431987269831705 is 178.36769447596086, 0.78 units above the recorded landing. The equality that IS exact is on the box, which is the mechanism this row established: the pre-fix `boxAfter` 237.94593984979582 is the post-fix 320.1646224767875 times `scaleX`, and the pre-fix `boxBefore` 26.485265692492487 is the post-fix 35.6368555689039 times `scaleX`, so the scaled write shrank the object by exactly `scaleX` -- and with `target.width` unscaled it passes at 1.31 units; the same run also asserts the saved box is the object's own width, the reopened box is that saved number, and the reopened width is the pre-save width. Red-proved by restoring `target.width * scaleX` in `adoptResizedBox`, where the case fails on the landing arm (C:/tmp/vg21/RUN-RED.json, C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json) (desktop-chromium, --workers=1). WHAT EACH REPORT IS, corrected 2026-10-12 by Task 2.2 of the backlog-drain plan, which this task's re-review filed as a Minor: RUN-RED.json is NOT a run of the committed blob. It ran a pre-commit revision of `editor.spec.ts` (written 16:31:06 +07, committed 16:32:28 +07), whose case declaration sits 15 lines above the committed one -- the report's case at line 4206 against the committed 4221, its failing location at 4317 against the committed assertion block at 4329-4332 -- and its own stdout carries this fix round's log fields. The assertion it fails is the same one, with the same message ('the resized edge lands where the author dragged it') and the same `Expected: < 2 | Received: 62.4156816858345`, so the substance is corroborated rather than assumed; vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json is the run of the committed bytes, reporting the case at line 4221.

title: The editor's rotation gesture on the canvas is performed by no test now that the indicator capture block is deleted
detail: FOUND BY the one-off screenshot pass (task 1 of 2026-10-11), which deleted the capture block 'shows the rotation-angle indicator beside the pointer mid-rotation' from src/web/tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts (was :3899) with its PNG docs/evidence/screenshots/editor-rotation-indicator-desktop-chromium.png. The block asserted only that the canvas was visible, but it was the only test that performs the editor's rotation GESTURE - grabbing Fabric's mtr handle on the canvas and dragging it to rotate a selection. WHAT WAS SEARCHED, AND WHERE: git grep -n on the word mtr at base ad94e5ed under src/web/tests returns exactly one hit, that deleted block's own comment, so no test under src/web/tests drives the mtr handle; a case-insensitive grep for rotat over src/web/tests/e2e and over the editor package turns up only authored or bridge-written angles (host-theme.ts, host-player.spec.ts, and reference-theme.spec.ts:2408 setAngle, which writes through the bridge) and never a gesture. THE READOUT IS NOT UNVERIFIED, and neither is the rotation configuration: src/web/packages/editor/src/indicator-manager/index.dom.test.ts:76 fires object:rotating and asserts .vigilia-angle-indicator reads 30 degrees, then hides on object:modified; src/web/packages/editor/src/controls-manager/index.test.ts:11 asserts snapAngle === 1 and :26 asserts the mtr handle's cursor and offset. So the readout and the control configuration are unit-tested and only the canvas gesture is not. Rotation still exists in the product: controls-manager/index.ts binds mtr to ROTATION and renderRotationHandle, and indicator-manager/index.ts draws the readout (showRotationAngle defaults true). WHY IT MATTERS: a regression in the canvas rotation control now has no test that would notice. THIS ROW WAS FIRST WRITTEN TOO BROADLY: it claimed the gesture AND the readout were untested and that no unit test drove the rotation control, and both halves were false; an independent review found the counterexamples above and the row was narrowed in this task's fix round. OWNER: whoever owns editor-canvas gesture coverage. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a test that rotates through the canvas controls and asserts the resulting angle.
check: `editor.spec.ts`'s "shows the rotation-angle indicator beside the pointer mid-rotation" performs the canvas gesture no test performed: a Rectangle inserted through the Add pane, Fabric's own `mtr` handle swept by a real pointer down/move/up, and the readout required to name the object's own rounded angle, sit within 40px of the pointer, NOT contain the pointer, track it, and hide on release (desktop-chromium, --workers=1). The run reports what "beside" rests on: the product's own 16px offset on both legs, `containsPointer: false`, distance 21.7 (C:/tmp/vg21/vg-346-rotation-r1.json)

title: Nothing asserts that a paused clock makes two frames of one chart byte-identical, now the determinism case that did is deleted
detail: FOUND BY the schema-v1 retirement (task 1 of 2026-10-11), which deleted src/web/tests/e2e/display-fabric.spec.ts and with it its case "is byte-stable at a fixed clock on one platform": three captures of /?theme=stress through openPaused, an ink check first, then Buffer.compare of two captures required to be 0. That case measured exactly what src/web/tests/e2e/clock.ts exists to guarantee, that a paused clock draws the same frame twice. It went because every theme it captured came from fake-source/src/themes, deleted in the same commit along with the player's ?theme= fixture path, and no surviving spec compares two frames: tests/e2e now has no Buffer.compare, no screenshot equality and no second capture of one frame (searched byte-for-byte, deterministic, reproducib, toDataURL, pixelmatch). clock.ts itself survives and is live - installFixedClock is called at tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts:4413 and :4496, and openPaused is used across the suite - so the measurement still holds under a live subject while nothing in the suite would notice a regression in it. title: The checked drawing declares four values that contradict the bible - two 9px cluster radii, three #0007 cluster shadows and a bordered follow-the-system row - and no mechanism compares the drawing to the bible at all
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-10), adjudicating every region of the two measurements into .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md. MEASURED, each against a bible section that states the value: (1) `editor-shell.html:178` and `:185` put the identity chip and the view cluster at `border-radius:9px`, where `design-language.md:93` gives `--radius-xl` 10px to exactly those clusters (dock, view controls, identity chip) and section 3 declares the radius scale closed; (2) `editor-shell.html:178`, `:185` and `:195` write the cluster shadows as `0 8px 20px #0007` and `0 10px 26px #0007`, where `design-language.md:103` fixes elevation 1 as `0 8px 20px #00000059`; (3) `editor-shell.html:288` wraps the follow-the-system toggle in `border:1px solid #242b34;border-radius:8px;padding:9px 10px`, a bordered container section 5 has no vocabulary for and section 1 forbids in the words "Chrome does not decorate". CONSEQUENCE: spec section 13 says "A mockup that no longer matches the bible is worse than no mockup, because it is believed" and requires the bible, the mockup and the spec to move in one commit - but the drawing is compared only to the PRODUCT (this plan reads it as the acceptance instrument and pulls the product to it), so a value the drawing gets wrong is inherited by the product rather than caught. This is the mirror of vg-291, which records the product diverging from a current drawing; here the drawing itself is off the bible and is the artifact that is stale. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a 9px cluster radius or a #0007 shadow is a deliberate drawing gesture or drift - the drawing has no commit trail of its own and every value is a literal in one file. What would settle it: a ruling on whether section 3's elevation 1 and the 10px cluster radius bind the drawing as tightly as they bind the product, and if they do, the three cited lines corrected in one commit that names this row. NARROWED BY TASK 3 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11), reviewing `42283107` and `be54cfc5`. THE SHELL DRAWING'S PART IS DONE: the two `9px` cluster radii and the three `#0007` shadows are corrected in the current set, where the lines are `current/shell.html:150`, `:157`, `:170` - this row cited `editor-shell.html`, the frozen original, which stays as it was - and the correction went wider than the four values cited here: twenty-one literals were off section 3's closed scale (eighteen `7px`, three `5px`; seventeen dock buttons, three view-cluster buttons, the follow-the-system track) and each is now its section 3 or section 5 entry. REMAINING: the third case, the bordered follow-the-system row at `current/settings.html:89-93`, is the modal's and is plan 8's (`vg-303` is its `padding:9px`). AND THE INSTRUMENT CLAUSE IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: no parity row reads any of these literals - putting one `7px` back into the drawing at `be54cfc5` leaves `design-language.spec.ts` green (5 passed) - so the correction this row asked for is not one the suite can hold in place. What would settle the clause is a row that reads a drawing's `border-radius` against section 3's scale; Task 6's gate is its natural owner. DISCHARGED IN PART BY PLAN 7 TASK 6 (2026-10-11, artefact 43e24bc5): the radius clause now has its mechanism - `design-language.spec.ts:2397-2436` reads every border-radius the drawing declares (75 declarations) and asserts each is a section 3 scale step (4, 6, 8, 10, 999, transcribed from `design-language.md:86-94`) or one of three named degenerates (1px, 2px, 50%, each carrying its reason in the row), with a positive control so an empty read cannot pass. The check is the row itself: putting one 7px back into `current/shell.html` reddens it naming the file and line, where at `be54cfc5` the same plant left the suite green. STILL OPEN: this row's other two clauses - the three #0007 cluster shadows and the bordered follow-the-system row - are read by no row, so the title's claim that no mechanism compares the drawing to the bible at all is now false of radii and still true of shadows and borders. THE MECHANISM CLAUSE WAS AN OVERCLAIM FOR ONE ROUND, AND IS NOW TRUE (2026-10-11, artefact c64c4c16, the whole-branch review of the shell-parity plan). The paragraph above says the gate reads every border-radius the drawing declares; at artefact 43e24bc5 it read `MOCKUP_PATH` and the shell drawing alone, and the file it named in a failure was a hardcoded constant - so the clause was true of one drawing of the four in `docs/design/mockups/current/`, which is the same failure this row exists to record, one level up. THE CLASS HAD MOVED RATHER THAN GONE, and the review found it where the gate was not looking: `settings.html` still declared twelve `3px` swatch chips and a `26x14` toggle track at `7px`, `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` the identical track, and `settings.html` a `0 10px 26px #0007` shadow - the same off-scale values Task 3 corrected in `shell.html`, in three files no row opened. WHAT LANDED: the gate now reads the directory through `currentDrawings()` (`mockup-values.ts:104`, a sorted directory read, so a fifth drawing is read the moment it lands) and each failure names the file and line it is in, with a per-drawing positive control; the test now sits at `design-language.spec.ts:2445`. Each corrected literal takes its section 3 entry - `--radius-sm` 4 for the swatch, `full` 999 for the track, as `current/shell.html:338` already read - and the settings dialog frame takes section 3 elevation 3, `0 24px 60px #000000b3`, not the elevation 1 the fix brief implied: the element is the modal frame, its product counterpart `.editor-shell-dialog` paints `--elev-3` (`editor-shell.css:1302`, token at `:362`), and section 3 reserves elevation 1 for floating clusters. RED PROVED: a planted `7px` in `controls.html` reddens the gate naming `controls.html:159`. CLOSED 2026-10-12 BY TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN (2026-10-12, artefact 6f9b3492). BOTH REMAINING CLAUSES NOW HAVE THEIR ARMS, AND EACH ARM'S RED PROOF IS THE RUN'S OWN JSON REPORT. The drawings gate ("every literal the checked drawings declare is on §3's scale or §2's") gains TWO arms beside radius, spacing and type: an ELEVATION arm holding every box-shadow a drawing declares to §3's elevation table (level 1 `0 8px 20px #00000059`, level 2 `0 18px 44px #00000099`, level 3 `0 24px 60px #000000b3`, or no shadow at all, which is level 0) with only §5 rule 4's two marks exempt — the spread-only accent-at-18% halo and an `inset` shadow, both read by shape rather than named in an allow-list — and a BOUNDARY arm holding every `border`/`border-*` to §5's 1px hairline. Both read the whole file through `mockupDeclarations` and both carry a per-arm positive control, because a control drawing legitimately declares no shadow at all, so a class no drawing feeds reddens rather than passing over an empty read. RED PROOF (0 expected / 1 unexpected, read from the run's own JSON report at `%TEMP%/vigilia-drain/red-arms.json`): planting `0 18px 50px #0009` at `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:148` and `border: 2px solid var(--edge)` at `:129` reddens BOTH new arms, and each entry names its file and line - `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:148 box-shadow: 0 18px 50px #0009 - ... is not on §3's elevation table (1 ..., 2 ..., 3 ..., or no shadow at all) ...` and `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:129 border: 2px solid var(--edge) - ... is not on §5's boundary vocabulary - a 1px hairline ..., or no boundary ...`. Both plants were reverted and the drawing is `cmp`-clean against `git show HEAD:docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html`. The green run over this arm and the shell/settings parity test is `%TEMP%/vigilia-drain/final-green.json`, 2 expected / 0 unexpected / 0 flaky. THE ELEVATION ARM FOUND A LIVE ONE: `current/shell.html:148` drew the stage's artwork at `0 18px 50px #0009` — level 2's offset, level 2's colour, and a 50px blur where §3 prints 44 — so the drawing was the stale side and is corrected with the arm that reads it. WHAT THE BOUNDARY ARM DOES NOT CATCH, and why the row's third clause is a record rather than a gate: a declaration cannot tell a bordered CONTAINER from a bordered control, so the follow-the-system row cannot be refused by declaration — and it does not need to be, because §5 rule 2 positively admits it ("a switch row whose label fills the row inside a panel box ... is not a field row and keeps the shape it is drawn with"), read from §5 itself rather than granted here. §8.15 CORRECTION APPLIED: the row's text reads as though `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html` were missing — the file is present (33.6 KB) and frozen by design, the checked set is `docs/design/mockups/current/`, and every line this row cites (`:178`, `:185`, `:195`, `:288`) is the frozen original's rather than the current set's. §8.2 CORRECTION APPLIED: the two `editor-shell.css` lines this row cites have moved — `.editor-shell-dialog`'s `box-shadow: var(--elev-3)` is at `:1427` (the rule opens at `:1405`), not `:1302`, and the `--elev-3` token is at `:466`, not `:362`. Both old numbers now land on unrelated content (`.editor-shell-inspector [data-vigilia-crop-aspect]:hover` and `--shell-primary-text`), which is how the drift was confirmed rather than assumed.

title: The drawings now declare six values `editor-shell.css` contradicts, and no gate reads the product side of a drawing comparison
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 8 (2026-10-11), materialised from the six `Discovered, not fixed:` trailers in the fix commit `f5e6870d`. The implementation commit `80ae353f` carried the same six in prose only and no trailer, which is why they nearly reached the register as nothing at all. MEASURED, each verified at the line by the controller before filing: (1) the Close - `settings.html` draws `margin-top:16px`, `.editor-shell-dialog > button` declares `18px` (`editor-shell.css:1400`); (2) the rail - `shell.html` draws `gap:4px`, `.editor-shell-rail` declares `3px` (`:872`); (3) asset buttons - `controls.html` draws `padding:4px 8px`, the rule declares `4px 7px` (`:1146`); (4) asset-button text - the drawings say `12px`, the rule inherits `13px` (`:1147-1154`, a role disagreement rather than an off-scale value); (5) the Add pane body - `shell.html:62` draws `10px 10px 14px`, `.editor-shell-panel` declares `12px` (`:931`); (6) the nav column - `settings.html` draws `10px 6px`, `.editor-shell-settings-tabs` declares `padding: 0` (`:1460`) because the 150px is a border-box width and a padding there would shorten the content box the parity row reads (`:1438-1441`). WHY THE CORRECTIONS CREATED THEM: Task 8 moved 268 off-scale drawing literals onto section 3's steps and section 2's scale; where the product counterpart lives in `editor-shell.css` - which appears in no `design-tokens.gated.json` entry - the drawing lands on the step while the product keeps the old number. Three of the six are product-off-scale (18px, 3px, 7px), one is a role disagreement, and TWO ARE COMPOSITION DIFFERENCES WHERE BOTH SIDES ARE ON SCALE (the Add pane body and the nav column), so this is not a single remedy. WHY NOBODY OWNS THEM: Task 9 Step 3 explicitly refuses a fix that moves pixels ('a design decision ... belongs to vg-274's own pass - do not fold it in'), so the three off-scale values are not its work either, and plan 8's ten tasks name no product file for any of the six. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a correction should have been withheld where it created a divergence. The controller ruled it should not - the bible wins where the current set disagrees with it (`docs/design/mockups/README.md`) and spec `:481-483` makes a drawing that disagrees with the bible worse than no drawing - so the six are the price of the instrument being right, and the remedy is a product pass rather than a drawing retreat. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the two composition differences disposed of in Task 10's section 13 difference list if a predating citation exists (the nav column's border-box invariant is the strongest candidate, and it must be verified against a rule that predates this plan rather than against the `:1438-1441` comment plan 8 wrote), and the four scale and role differences as a named product pass of their own. IT IS NOT vg-231, which is the shell's four body regions at an off-scale 12px radius - a different set of values in the same file - and it is not vg-274, which counts that file's residuals rather than its disagreements with the drawings. PLAN 8 TASK 10 SUPPLIED THE DISPOSITION THIS ROW ASKED FOR (2026-10-11, b78ee264), and the answer is NOT the candidate the row proposed: the `editor-shell.css:1438-1441` comment is one plan 8 itself wrote (Task 2, 5e8ba2b0), and a comment the plan wrote cannot license the plan's own divergence, so it was refused rather than cited. The nav column's `padding: 0` was disposed instead as the other face of the composition difference the census already records for its rows 4 and 7 - the product places the dialog's inset on the frame at `20px 24px`, which section 3 (`design-language.md:79`, the 20-24 between-regions and dialog-padding row) positively licenses, so its children declare none; a literal fix of the nav column alone would give it a 10px inset IN ADDITION to the frame's 24px, matching neither the drawing nor the product. The Add pane body's inset was disposed the same way, licensed by section 3 (`design-language.md:77`, the 12-14 section-padding and panel-gutter row; a first pass cited `:79`, which is the other row). Both composition differences are therefore dispositioned rather than open, and the four scale values remain a named product pass - capped and counted by name in the ceiling Task 9 landed (`vg-274`): margin-top 18px at `editor-shell.css:1400`, gap 3px at `:872`, and padding 4px 7px at `:1148` and `:1189`. CORRECTED 2026-10-12 (§8.2 stale citations): the `editor-shell.css` lines this row cites have moved — `:1400` is `.editor-shell-dialog > button`'s `margin-top` at `:1503`, `:872` is `.editor-shell-rail`'s `gap` at `:975`, and `:1146`/`:1148`/`:1189` are the two plain-DOM button groups' `padding` at `:1251` and `:1292`. Each old number now lands on unrelated content, which is how the drift was confirmed rather than assumed. The product-side arm prints the RULE's line rather than the declaration's — `.editor-shell-rail`'s `gap` reddens as `:970` — because the shared reader reports a `<style>` rule by the line its SELECTOR starts on. CONFIRMED 2026-10-12: this row carries no citation other than those, and `vg-296` and `vg-314` carry only the two §8.2 corrections applied to them here (`vg-296`: `:1302`→`:1427`, `:362`→`:466`; `vg-314`: `:1107`→`:1229`), while `vg-313` is Task 2.3b's row and takes its own. CLOSED 2026-10-12 BY TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN (artefact 6f9b3492). BOTH REMAINING HALVES LANDED. The PRODUCT SIDE instrument, the inverse of the drawings gate the title asked for: "the shell and the settings modal are what the drawings draw" now parses `editor-shell.css` itself through the same `mockupDeclarations` reader a drawing goes through, and holds four of the six residuals to the drawing that owns each — the dialog button's `margin-top` to `current/settings.html`'s Close row, the rail's `gap` to `current/shell.html`'s rail, and the Add pane's asset-button group and the inspector's plain-DOM button group to `current/controls.html`'s drawn button box — with an empty-read control per row so a selector the product dropped fails rather than agreeing. The PRODUCT PASS then moved all four onto the drawings' §3 values, which is a fix and not a re-record: the bible wins where the current set disagrees with it, and `editor-shell.css` is in no `design-tokens.gated.json` entry, which is why the drawings moved in Task 8 and the product did not. RED PROOF (0 expected / 1 unexpected, read from the run's own JSON report at `%TEMP%/vigilia-drain/red-product-line.json`): reverting `.editor-shell-rail`'s `gap` to `3px` reddens the product side with `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:970 `.editor-shell-rail` gap: 3px; the drawing declares 4px (§3)`. title: The boundary assertion names its chrome and cluster sets as literals on the test side, so an element added later escapes half the check
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-11) as two Minor notes, both non-blocking, and filed rather than fixed because what should define membership is an instrument decision and not a patch. NOTE A: `shell-appearance.spec.ts`'s `GLASS_CLUSTERS` is a literal pair (`[`.editor-shell-dock`, `.editor-shell-zoom`]`), so a further element carrying `editor-glass` is read for translucency and shadow but never for the sheen that class gives it - the escape is invisible precisely because the new element resembles the two that are checked. NOTE B: the chrome half holds every surface's rendered alpha against a probe painted `var(--panel)`, while the header paints `--shell-surface` in its own rule, `.editor-shell-header`'s `background: var(--shell-surface)`; the two are equal only because all six palettes alias `--panel: var(--shell-surface)`, so a palette that decoupled them by alpha would false-red the header and one that decoupled them by colour alone would pass. MEASURED BY THE REVIEWER rather than carried from the report: `--panel` is declared on `:root` and on `[data-shell-palette=`light`]`, both on the element `choosePalette` writes (`shell-palette.ts:66`), so the body-appended probe does read the palette's value and the assertion is not vacuous. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether either note is worth closing - a set derived from the stylesheet can hide the same gap in the other direction (an element that loses `editor-glass` leaves the sheen check silently), and Note B is a fact about today's aliasing rather than a defect. SETTLED BY THE INSTRUMENT, NOT BY THAT RULING (Task 2.3b, 2026-10-12): no ruling exists or is scheduled on whether an assertion may name the elements it covers, and the boundary is settled by derivation instead - the assertion reads membership out of the stylesheet, so nothing on the test side names an element. MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED: a rule in `editor-shell.css` whose `background` is `var(--panel)` or `var(--shell-surface)` classifies the elements its own selector matches - **chrome** when the fill is flat (`box-shadow: none`, or a `border-top`/`border-bottom`), **glass** when the fill is lifted (`backdrop-filter` starting `blur(`), and **sheen** when a lifted fill also carries a `gradient(`. The literal pair this row names as `GLASS_CLUSTERS` is now the derived `SHEEN_CLUSTERS`, and a further element carrying `editor-glass` is read with the rule that paints it instead of having to be added to a list. The authored stylesheet is read rather than the loaded one because the built one cannot classify its own glass: Lightning CSS emits the blur as `-webkit-backdrop-filter` alone, this Chromium supports the unprefixed property alone, and a declaration the parser cannot use is dropped from CSSOM - which is `vg-311`'s dead blur. RED PROOF: adding a further element carrying `editor-glass` with its own blur rule reddens the cluster arm in all six palettes, naming `7:.editor-shell-probe-cluster.editor-glass` - an element the literal lists read with nothing - and the plant was reverted byte-exact (`cmp` against `git show HEAD:<path>` for `shell-layout.tsx` and `editor-shell.css`). WHAT THE DERIVATION DOES NOT CLOSE: a surface that loses its rule leaves the set silently, so a derived set can hide the same gap in the other direction, exactly as this row's own NOT ESTABLISHED says, and the three `toBeGreaterThan(0)` guards are positive controls on an empty read rather than assertions that cannot fail. §8.2 APPLIED: the stale `editor-shell.css` line citation above is replaced by the rule that owns it. WHAT THE RED PROOF DOES AND DOES NOT SHOW, AND ONE HOLE THE RECORD MISSED (whole-branch review of Task 2.3b, 2026-10-12, commit 8658f24b): the plant is a further element carrying `editor-glass` with its own blur rule, and its eleven failure lines name `[data-treatment-probe="7:.editor-shell-probe-cluster.editor-glass"]` -- five fill lines and six shadow lines, `light` dropping only the fill line because its `--panel` is 75 %, which is exactly what the per-palette alpha predicts. It DOES NOT EXERCISE THE SHEEN ARM: the plant's rule carries `background: var(--panel)` and no `gradient(`, so the element entered the cluster set and was caught on the fill and shadow arms, and no `no glass gradient` line appears in the report -- and a gradient-bearing plant could not redden that arm either, because a rendered `background-image` is non-`none` whatever it holds. So this is the only red-provable direction rather than a gap a later run can close, and it matters because this row's Note A is specifically about the sheen. THE DERIVATION ALSO HOLDS A FILL-SHORTHAND HOLE, and the row records it here rather than leaving the review's sentence standing: the classification reads the `background` SHORTHAND alone, so a surface declaring its fill as `background-color` or `background-image` -- or as `background: var(--panel, ...)` -- joins neither set, and all three arms skip it silently. That is this row's own escape re-opened by a styling shape instead of by a list. Nothing is misclassified today: all nine fills of `var(--panel)`/`var(--shell-surface)` in `editor-shell.css` use the shorthand. The blind spot already recorded here is the OTHER direction, a surface that LOSES its rule leaving the set silently.
check: `shell-appearance.spec.ts`'s boundary assertion derives its chrome, cluster and sheen sets from `editor-shell.css` rather than naming them, so a further element added later is read with the rule that paints it; planting a further element carrying `editor-glass` with its own blur rule reddens the cluster arm in all six palettes - 0 expected / 1 unexpected in the red run's own JSON report at %TEMP%/vigilia-drain/red-313.json, naming `7:.editor-shell-probe-cluster.editor-glass` - and the plant was reverted `cmp`-verified against HEAD.

title: The canvas context menu's e2e spec never asserts the menu lands where the pointer was, so the pointer anchoring the whole library ruling turns on has no browser coverage
detail: FOUND WHILE CORRECTING THE PLAN AFTER THE USER RULED FOR BASE UI, checking what the browser actually proves about the one surface that stopped plan 9's Phase 1. THE SURFACE: src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/canvas-context-menu.tsx computes a synthetic zero-size rect from the right-click coordinate (lines 146-157) and hands it to Base UI's `Positioner anchor`, because Radix cannot anchor a menu to a point and that is what eliminated it. That behaviour is now the load-bearing reason for the library choice (0038). THE MEASUREMENT: src/web/tests/e2e/editor-context-menu.spec.ts is 195 lines with one test, and its own readMenu() helper returns popupTop -- and nothing asserts it. Grepping the file for popupTop gives two hits, both inside the helper: the declaration in the return type and the read in the evaluate body. No expect() consumes it, and the click coordinate (point.x, point.y) is used for page.mouse.click and for nothing else, so the popup is never compared to the point it was opened at. What the spec does assert is that the menu opened, that its scrollHeight exceeds its clientHeight, that popupBottom is inside the viewport, and that End then Enter reaches and fires the last entry. All of that passes on a menu anchored to the wrong corner. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY: the fix needs a design decision this row cannot make, and it is not just an added assertion. The spec deliberately runs in a 420px window against a 470px menu, so Base UI is flipping or shifting the popup by necessity and the pointer coordinate is not where the popup goes -- an assertion written in this window would pin the flip rather than the anchor, and a correct-looking failure would be the test being wrong. Pinning the anchor needs a second case in a window tall enough to leave the popup unshifted, which is a new test rather than an edit, and it needs a decision on what tolerance counts as anchored, since the renderer and the popup round to different pixels. WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT ACADEMIC: the surface whose inability to migrate is the stated reason for the library ruling is the one surface with no browser assertion of the behaviour that made it special, and plan 9's Phase 1 is about to touch the library under it. If the anchor silently broke, every assertion in this file would still pass. SEVERITY IS MEDIUM: nothing is known to be broken today -- the menu visibly opens at the pointer when driven by hand -- so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect, filed because it is the gap between what 0038 claims is verified and what a run actually checks. SAME CLASS AS vg-159/vg-160, plan 4's verification bullets that were never delivered as tests.
check: the new case in editor-context-menu.spec.ts right-clicks two empty canvas points in a 1000px window and asserts each menu's left and top edges are the pointer's, within 2px and 8px, and that a second click moves it by the same distance

title: The editor header overflows horizontally at 390 px, putting the publish surface off-screen
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 2.3 while capturing the rendered proof for the header's publish surface, and left as a Discovered, not fixed trailer because its dispatch forbade writing the register. Measured, not inferred: at 390 px the header overflows horizontally and PHONE ADDRESS, the §145 warning, the pairing expiry and the QR are all off-screen. Evidence is src/web/test-results/publish/header-390.png beside header-desktop.png at 1680 px, where the same surface renders correctly. THOSE FILES DO NOT PERSIST and should not be looked for: Playwright clears its output directory at the start of every run, so the PNGs exist only until the next suite runs. Task 3.5 regenerated and described them and they are gone again. The durable evidence is the measurement, not the file -- at 390 px documentElement.scrollWidth equals innerWidth, so there is no horizontal scrollbar and the overflow is CLIPPED rather than scrollable-to; the publish root is 327.3 px wide starting at left 232.5, the address code runs from 243.5 to 401.9 with its last ~12 px cut off, and the QR begins at 413.9, wholly past the right edge and unseen. Anyone who wants a lasting picture has to put it under docs/evidence/ and register it, which is what that directory is for. Nothing pins a phone-width header, and tests/e2e/surface.ts gates every editor spec to a desktop surface, so no test covers this and none would have caught it. Not fixed there: the header's layout is not that task's owner, and whether the editor should have a usable phone-width header at all is a design question rather than a layout bug -- the editor is a desktop surface by decision, so the honest answer may be that this is acceptable and should be said out loud rather than fixed. It matters more than a cosmetic overflow because the surface that goes off-screen is the one that tells an author where their phone should point. WIDENED ON 2026-10-07 by Task 3.3: the publish control now renders its off state on every host, including a loopback-only one, where it previously rendered nothing at all — so the header carries a button, the §145 warning and (when the LAN is on) the address and a 135 px code, and the pressure this row describes is now on every editor, not only a LAN-bound one. Task 3.5 is the first browser proof that reads this surface at 390 px.
check: the publish spec now asserts at 390px that the publish surface, its address code and the QR each begin at or right of 0 and end at or before window.innerWidth; planting width 420px with max-width none reddens the surface arm (0 expected / 1 unexpected), and the restored bundle is green
