title: A menubar test that clicks a Base UI menu trigger stalls for 50 to 90 seconds under jsdom, timing out tests whose own code is fine
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 2 FIX ROUND 2, while reconciling the shell-layout.dom.test.ts / .tsx pair. In packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.dom.test.tsx, once "opens every View setting's choices instead of toggling on a bare click" has run, requestAnimationFrame stops firing for every test after it in the file, so a test that awaits a frame dies on Test timed out in 20000ms rather than on anything about itself. MEASURED, by bisect with vitest -t rather than by reasoning: the two scroll tests in shell-layout.dom.test.ts pass alone (-t "returns the layer list", 1 passed in 4.8s); they pass with the immediately preceding test (-t "inserts the same objects|returns the layer list", 2 passed); and they fail with the View-menu test (-t "opens every View setting's choices|returns the layer list", 1 failed, 80.9s). The whole file run prints no unhandled error and no jsdomError, so this is NOT the vg-100 shape - nothing throws, the callbacks simply stop. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED beyond that bisect; the View-menu test opens two nested Base UI popups and calls layout.destroy() without unmounting either, and the file already works around Base UI under jsdom (a stubbed ResizeObserver, a stubbed Element.getAnimations, an afterEach Escape). NOT FIXED here because it is not the task: the work that exposed it was a file merge that turned out to be the wrong shape anyway - renaming the scroll tests to shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts removes the shadowing without moving them, which is what shipped. It matters because the file's own eighteen tests pass only because none of them awaits a frame, so the first person to add one - or to move the scroll tests across - gets a 20-second timeout pointing at their own test. Needs an owner; the surface to look at is what the View-menu test leaves mounted, not the scroll tests. || DIAGNOSED, NOT FIXED. The row asked for an owner and said the cause was not established; it is established now, and it is NOT what the row guessed. EVERY PART OF THE ROWS MECHANISM IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. (1) "requestAnimationFrame stops firing": it does not. Measured inside the View-menu test, between the menu click and the next read - requestAnimationFrame is still the native function, document.visibilityState is visible, document.hasFocus() false, and a requested frame arrives in 18ms. Frames were arriving the whole time. (2) "a later test that awaits a frame times out": the test that times out is NOT a later one - the View-menu test itself times out at 20s IN COMPLETE ISOLATION (-t "opens every View setting", 1 passed 16 skipped), so there is no cross-test contamination and no leaked mount to find. The row bisect was an artefact of the file being run in order. (3) "the whole file run prints no unhandled error and no jsdomError": true, and that is the actual shape - nothing throws. WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING, bisected by stamping every step of the test body: a bare setTimeout(0) BEFORE any click costs 2ms; the SAME setTimeout(0) immediately AFTER menubarEntry(root, uiCopy.menus.view).click() costs 58592ms. The next one costs 5ms and the one after 5ms, and rAF between them is 18ms. So it is a ONE-SHOT ~49-59 SECOND STALL INSIDE A SINGLE SYNCHRONOUS CLICK, not starvation and not a dead scheduler - everything after it is fast again. That is why a frame awaiting test still times out: it is not waiting for a frame that will not come, it is waiting out a stall that a macrotask boundary is what finally drains. THE CLICK PATH IS BASE UI POPUP MOUNT, and two candidates were eliminated by measurement rather than reasoning: removing the Element.prototype.getAnimations stub does NOT fix it (27.3s with the stub gone vs 25.2s with it), and BASE_UI_ANIMATIONS_DISABLED - Base UIs own documented global, declared in its global.d.ts and read at the one line of useAnimationsFinished that decides whether to call fnToExecute directly - does NOT fix it either. Both were the obvious answers and both are wrong. STILL NOT FIXED because the remaining candidate needs a real bisect of Base UIs popup mount under jsdom, which is a different piece of work from this row, and I would be guessing past the measurements. NO SOURCE CHANGED. WHAT WOULD FINISH IT: instrument the click itself rather than around it - time the synchronous span inside ShellMenuBar/Menu.Trigger onClick - and the stall will show up as a long synchronous block with a name on it. The two candidates above are the ones already ruled out, so the next agent should not re-run them. || TITLE CORRECTED 2026-10-07, BY PLAN 6, because the old title asserted the mechanism the detail above refutes: it said jsdom stops firing requestAnimationFrame, and the measurements show frames arriving throughout. Anyone searching this register for a slow or timing-out menubar test was looking for starvation and would not have found a stall. The measurement that prompted the correction: at 9d334e09 the whole file run in isolation fails 1 test, and at 79f9a0b0 it fails 3, at 91s / 96s / 118s / 67s against a 20s timeout - so the same one-shot stall now makes the FULL unit suite red, not just a single file run in order. Nothing about the diagnosis above changed. RE-MEASURED BY PLAN 7 TASK 4.2 at `5a2f051a`, file-only run of `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx`: **21 tests, 20 passed, 1 failed**, file wall time about 6 minutes. Every non-menu test ran in 25-2035 ms; the five menu-driven ones took **43.5 s, 94.5 s, 109.5 s, 67.7 s and 29.4 s**, and the 94.5 s one -- `inserts the same objects from the Insert menu as the Add pane offers` -- is the single failure, `Error: Test timed out in 20000ms`. **That a test stalling past 20 s can still PASS is consistent with the stall being synchronous rather than a slow call**, which is this row's own diagnosis: the timeout timer cannot fire until the block ends. Reported as consistent with the record, not as a new mechanism.
check: `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` is 23 passed in ~8s with no menubar menu trigger stalling: the stall measured as one 20s timeout on the publish-surface case and 17-52s on the View, Insert and Edit cases comes back only when jsdom's `:modal`/`:popover-open` selector stub is neutralised, which is the stub `3fe3f22e` added.

title: a Base UI menu opened earlier in shell-layout.dom.test.tsx stalls a later dialog's unmount, so the sheet test only passes because of where it sits in the file
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 3.4 OF PLAN 7 while placing its own test, and reported in that commit as `Discovered, not fixed:`. MEASURED BY THE EXECUTOR, NOT REPRODUCED BY THE ROOT: the root verified the test passes (361 ms, exit 0) and verified its position at `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:180`, ahead of every menu-opening test in the file, but did not re-run the failure itself. The row is open on that basis. THE MEASUREMENT: with the sheet test appended last, a file-only run of `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` gives **4** failures; with the same test placed after `it("mounts the editorial palette, menus, pane bar, inspector and dock hosts")` the same run gives exactly the **3** expected `vg-135` timeouts, and the sheet test passes. Bisected by moving it: preceded by `it("prints the chord on the menu rows the shortcut table binds")` -- the file's last menu test -- the sheet test times out at 20 s; preceded by a non-menu test such as `it("shows one pane at a time and routes the dock through the bridge")` it is green. THE FAILING STEP IS THE CLOSE, NOT THE OPEN: the test's first read is synchronous and succeeds, and what times out is the `vi.waitFor` waiting for `[role="dialog"]` to become null after the close button is clicked. So the dialog opens and never finishes unmounting. THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the hypothesis below is the executor's rather than a finding: Radix unmounts through `Presence`, which waits for a frame; a Base UI menu opened earlier in the same jsdom environment is said to leave that frame pipeline stalled, so the frame `Presence` waits on is never delivered. That is plausible and untested -- what is measured is the ordering, not the mechanism. WHY IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS `vg-135` BUT NOT THAT ROW: `vg-135` is one Base UI menu-trigger *click* blocking 50-90 s synchronously in whatever test opens it. This is a *later, different* test failing because an earlier one opened a menu -- a cross-test leak through shared jsdom state rather than a slow call. The two were also observed to be independent in the same session: the three `vg-135` timeouts did **not** reproduce in the executor's `npx vitest run packages/editor` run (where only `ui-copy.test.ts` was red) and appeared only in the file-only run, so `vg-135` is intermittent while this one was reproducible by test order. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the fix needs a decision about which mechanism to change -- isolating the DOM between tests, giving the sheet test its own file, driving Radix's unmount without `Presence`, or finding the Base UI leak -- and more than one owner could make it. THE WORKAROUND NOW IN THE TREE IS AN ORDERING DEPENDENCY, which is the part that will bite: the test passes because of where it sits, so inserting a menu-opening test above it, or running the file with a shuffled order, silently turns it into a 20 s timeout that reads as a regression in the sheet. The test carries a doc comment saying so, which keeps it from being a trap, but the dependency is real. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-08 BY PLAN 9 TASK 1.1, AFTER THE DIALOG MOVED FROM RADIX TO BASE UI (decision 0038), because the change removed the mechanism this row's hypothesis named. **The ordering dependency survives; only the symptom softened, and the hypothesis is now weaker rather than stronger.** Same file, same command, two runs on one commit: with the sheet test in its guarded place it is green in **126 ms**, and appended last -- after every menu test -- it is green in **20 656 ms**, up from the hard 20 s timeout the executor measured. That is a 164x stall inside the same test, on the same assertion (`vi.waitFor` for `[role='dialog']` to go null after the close), so the close still does not settle promptly when a menu ran earlier, and the ordering guard is still doing real work rather than guarding a dead hazard. WHAT THAT SAYS ABOUT THE CAUSE: the row's hypothesis was Radix's `Presence` waiting on a frame the stalled pipeline never delivers, and **Base UI has no `Presence`** -- its dialog keeps the popup in the document behind a `hidden` attribute until the close settles. A different implementation stalling the same way, in the same place, is evidence that the shared jsdom frame state is the cause and the library was the messenger. That is an inference from two implementations, not a measurement of the pipeline, so the cause is still **not established**. THE TITLE WAS CORRECTED rather than left describing a library the file no longer uses; the ordering dependency it names is unchanged. Nothing else in the row is affected -- the root still has not reproduced the executor's 4-failure run itself.

RULED 2026-10-12: DOM ISOLATION — tear down the earlier menu inside the test that opened it, so no test in the file depends on where it sits. The cause is not established, and a fix follows the evidence that does exist: two different libraries stall in the same place in this file, which points at shared jsdom document or frame state rather than at either library's implementation, so a fix aimed at a library's internals is a guess at a mechanism nobody measured. A separate file is rejected because it MOVES the dependency instead of removing it — the stall follows the pair into whichever file holds both — and chasing the leak is the same unestablished hypothesis with a longer investigation. The proof that isolation worked is the sheet test running FIRST in the file and still passing; until that is shown the ordering guard stays.

RULED 2026-10-13: THE ORDERING DEPENDENCY IS REFUTED, BY MEASUREMENT, and the paragraph above is false at HEAD. `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` is 23 passed in about 8s; the sheet test passes FIRST in the file (0.17s) and LAST (0.1s), so no test depends on where it sits; and no menu popup outlives the test that opened it -- probed inside the View case, `.editor-shell-positioner` is 3 with the menu open and 0 after that test's own `layout.destroy()`. The stall returns only when jsdom's `:modal`/`:popover-open` selector stub is neutralised, and that stub is `3fe3f22e` (2026-10-10), which landed two days AFTER this row's last re-measurement (`5a2f051a`, 2026-10-08) -- so both of this row's claims were read against a commit HEAD had moved past, and the cure predates the change that closed it. What landed is the ruling's guard inverted rather than its remedy: an `afterEach` asserting no menu popup outlives its test, red with that teardown disabled (3 failures). The `closeMenus()` helper the remedy implied was written, measured to remove zero nodes, and deleted before committing, because the file already isolates per-test through `layout.destroy()`.
check: the sheet test passes both first in `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` (0.17s) and last (0.1s), so no test in the file depends on where it sits, and no menu popup outlives the test that opened it — the `afterEach` check that fails with the teardown disabled proves it.

title: packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts states its own module contract twice, so the file has two doc comments claiming one thing and neither is marked as the owner
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1.2 OF PLAN 7 and verified here at the source rather than taken from its report. `ui-copy.ts:1-2` is the file header: `/** Typed package-local visible editor copy (§35). Authored theme text, telemetry values and developer errors stay outside this module. */`. `ui-copy.ts:85-86` repeats that sentence **word for word** as the doc comment on `export const uiCopy`, which is the file's entire export. (The executor reported `:83-84`; the verified lines were `:82-83`. **Task 1 of plan 6 re-measured them at `:85-86`** -- the file grew above them, so this citation drifts with every insertion, and it is why these line numbers are a location to re-check rather than a fact.) WHY IT MATTERS, and it is small: this is the module that claims every visible editor word, so its contract is the thing a contributor reads before adding a string. Two copies mean a later edit to one leaves the other asserting something the file no longer does, and nothing detects it. It is the same shape as a duplicated constant, minus the compiler. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED ON THE FLY, and this is the reason: AGENTS.md allows a fix without a row only when a regression test is obvious, and **no test can catch a duplicated comment without a bespoke lint rule** -- so the fix would leave nothing behind that stops it recurring, which is the exact condition the rule exists to prevent. It is also not this task's region: Task 1.2 added one `shortcuts` block further down the file and correctly left this alone. Cosmetic in effect and it blocks nothing. One of the two copies should go; **which one is a judgement rather than a lookup** -- dropping `:85-86` leaves the export undocumented in an editor that shows hover text, and dropping `:1-2` leaves the module without a header -- which is the second reason it is a row and not a drive-by edit.
check: `ui-copy.ts` states its module contract once — the file header keeps it and the duplicate doc comment on `uiCopy` is gone.

title: The copy walk reads no opened menu popup, no Settings Keyboard/About tab and no canvas context menu, though all four are reachable in jsdom
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 6 TASK 5'S REVIEW (2026-10-11), which checked the implementer's claim that these surfaces were Task 9's and found the claim false: Task 9 is the browser PARITY capture, so it will not close a unit-test coverage hole. THE MEASUREMENT, from the reviewer's own walk of the source: opened menu popups ARE reachable -- `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx:1042` opens the View menu and `:1159` the Edit menu, both reading `[role=menuitem]`; the Settings Keyboard tab is reachable -- `accessible-names.dom.test.ts:586` clicks the `[role=tab]` named `uiCopy.settings.keyboard`, and the About tab is the same gesture; and the canvas context menu is reachable -- `canvas-context-menu.dom.test.tsx` mounts it and reads its `[role=menuitem]` after a `contextmenu` dispatch. All four are reachable in jsdom, so the hole is the copy walk's. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED, and the reviewer's sweep is the reason it is not urgent: NO LITERAL CURRENTLY LIVES IN ANY OF THE FOUR. The walk's author swept every non-test source for a literal-valued `aria-label`/`title` and found none besides the three Task 5 moved and `document-identity.tsx`'s `title={documentName}`, which is the document's own name and therefore data. So this is a coverage hole, not a live defect -- and the controller's ruling was to state the boundary in `ui-copy.test.ts`'s doc comment rather than pay for it now, because opening a menu under jsdom costs 50-90 s (`vg-135`, measured in `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx`) and three opens plus new gestures is a poor trade for a hole with nothing in it today. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the walk mounts the opened Edit/View/File popups, the Settings modal's Keyboard and About tabs, and the canvas context menu, each with the per-surface non-empty assertion the walk already uses for its four mounted surfaces. The cost is the jsdom menu-open time, so whoever closes it should decide whether those cases belong in the focused gate or in a slower tier -- that decision is why this is a row and not a task. RELATED: the boundary is stated in `ui-copy.test.ts`'s own doc comment, which names these four and the reason, and the commit that recorded it is `869da1a9`.
check: The copy walk mounts and reads the opened menu popup, the Settings Keyboard and About tabs and the canvas context menu, each asserted non-empty; removing the menu-row read turns the case red.

title: ui-copy.ts is 869 lines, past the 800-line stop, and the copy table is growing while nothing records an exemption for a data table
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER PREPARING PLAN 6 TASK 6 (2026-10-11), while checking that task's own instruction to add two cases to `ui-copy.test.ts`. THE MEASUREMENT, at `7ae6d519`: `wc -l` gives `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts` **869** and `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts` **783**. The repo's rule is 500 lines a signal and 800 a stop for a normal source file, and this register already carries the same class three times -- `vg-209` (`layer-panel.tsx` 838), `vg-255` (`selection-inspector/index.ts` 822) and `vg-276` (`shell-layout.tsx` 916) -- so the observation is not new, only this file's. THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT A TASK: `ui-copy.ts` is a string table, most of its bulk being doc comments that state why each word is the word. The stop is written for source files and the repo does allow an explicit exception for proven vendored source, so the honest questions are whether a copy table is a file the stop aims at, and if not whether the exception should be written down rather than assumed. Splitting it by namespace (menus, panels, inspectorFields, view, actions) is the obvious repair if the stop does apply, and the test file would follow the split. THE IMMINENT HALF, which is why this was noticed now: plan 6 Task 6 instructs two new cases in `ui-copy.test.ts`, which sits at 783 -- so the task that owns the copy rules is the one that would take the test file past the stop. The controller's instruction to that task is to record the crossing explicitly rather than let it happen silently, and to prefer a focused file if the additions would cross. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an exemption written down with its reason, or a split of both files with the test following. Nothing is broken by the length itself; what is broken is that the rule exists and this file is past it with nothing said.
check: `ui-copy.ts` records its exemption from the 800-line stop in its own header, so the file is a data table and its lines are the table rather than a count to obey.

title: The copy walk reads no paragraph text, so shell-layout.tsx renders a hint with no owner in uiCopy
detail: FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING plan 6 Task 6 (the copy defects). src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:908 renders a paragraph whose only text is: Move and lock the selection with the canvas dock. It renders whenever a selection exists, and the sentence is a literal - not in ui-copy.ts and returned by no accessor. ui-copy.test.ts reads a surface through label text, aria-labels and button text (spokenIn), and the pictograph rule sees only the table, so a paragraph is read by neither net: a word an author reads with no owner, which is the class the copy rule exists to catch. MEASURED across packages/editor/src for a bare JSX text line: this is the one rendered instance (composition-pane.tsx:629 is the same shape inside a comment, not rendered); single-word and inline forms were not exhaustively enumerated, so the class may hold more. NOT FIXED HERE because the regression test needs the walk to read paragraph text, which is Task 5 own net and outside Task 6 file set, and whether the net should read every text node or only these three kinds is a coverage decision rather than a one-line edit. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: widen spokenIn (or the copy rule) to the surface own text nodes, then move this sentence into uiCopy behind an accessor.
check: The copy walk reads a surface's paragraph text, and the shell hint is `uiCopy.selectionHint`: disabling the fix leaves the unowned literal in shell-layout.tsx and the case goes red.

title: renderer-core's plan.ts carries a raw NUL byte in an Intl.NumberFormat cache key, so grep and ripgrep treat the file as binary and silently return no matches for it
detail: FOUND WHILE VERIFYING vg-176, in the file the fix had just changed. renderer-core/src/scene/plan.ts:604 builds a composite cache key for Intl.NumberFormat as `${themeLanguage}\0${minimumFractionDigits}\0${maximumFractionDigits}` -- and the two separators are RAW NUL BYTES in the file, not the escape `\u0000`. TypeScript accepts them and the cache behaves correctly; nothing fails at runtime. THE HARM IS NAVIGATION, and it was demonstrated rather than reasoned: the Grep tool reports "binary file matches (found \"\\0\" byte around offset 17257)" and SUPPRESSES the matching lines. A grep for `planArtboard` across packages returned hits in five files and none in plan.ts, which read as "the extracted helper has no call site" and would have had the controller report a working fix as broken. It is the only NUL-bearing tracked source file in src/web/packages, so the blind spot is exactly one file -- the one an agent most needs to read when working on the plan. git is unaffected: its binary sniff reads only the first 8000 bytes and the NUL is at 17257, so `git diff` and `git diff --stat` render normally and the fix commit was reviewable. THE FIX IS A REPRESENTATION CHANGE, not a behaviour change: writing the escape `\u0000` produces the identical string, so the cache key, the grouping options and every caller are unchanged. One owner (renderer-core), no design decision, and it does not block anything -- which is why it is a row rather than a same-commit fix inside a reviewed fix commit. NO REGRESSION TEST IS OBVIOUS, and that is the honest reason it is not fixed on the fly: the check that would catch it is a repo-wide source-hygiene sweep for NUL bytes, which no script in scripts/ performs today.
check: plan.ts writes the escape for a NUL separator instead of raw bytes; the source-hygiene reader reddens on any source file carrying a raw NUL byte.

title: No Playwright config sets outputDir, so concurrent runs share test-results and delete each other's traces, reporting false failures
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's fix round (its Discovered, not fixed item 6); mechanism CONFIRMED by the controller, measurement by the implementer. All five configs - playwright.config.ts, playwright.display.config.ts, playwright.glass-shapes.config.ts, playwright.parity.config.ts and playwright.rebuild.config.ts - omit outputDir, so every run writes into the same default test-results/ root and its .playwright-artifacts-N directories. Running two configs at once therefore makes the first to finish clean up the other's artifacts, and the survivor reports browserContext.close: ENOENT ... .trace as TEST FAILURES. MEASURED: playwright.rebuild.config.ts reported 2 failed / 7 passed under a concurrent display run and 9 passed / 0 failed alone. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TASK: it is a false-red generator, so a browser run on this box is not a measurement while another run is in flight - this is the mechanism under the 'a single sample of a flaky spec is not a measurement' rule AGENTS.md already carries, and it means running two configs in parallel to save wall-clock buys phantom failures instead. OWNER/FIX: unassigned - giving each config a distinct outputDir (e.g. outputDir: 'test-results/rebuild') is the obvious fix and is a config change rather than a task. SEVERITY: medium - no product effect, but it corrupts the evidence the verification process rests on.
check: Each of the five Playwright configs sets its own outputDir under test-results; verified the five values differ.

title: The compaction banner reads two unwritten conventions, so rewording STATUS.md or a ledger heading blinds it silently
detail: FOUND BY the controller (2026-10-12), reading the banner after a context loss. `scripts/sdd-checkpoint.mjs:258` takes the active plan from a bullet matching `**Active plan:** <backticked path>`, and `:335` takes task states from lines matching `Task <n>: <state>`. Neither convention is written down where a document author would see it, and both fail SILENTLY rather than loudly. OBSERVED: STATUS.md's bullet had been reworded to `**The active plan is [name](path)**` after 2026-09-26 -- the 14 checkpoints on disk split 9 naming a plan and 5 saying `STATUS.md names no active plan` -- so the banner told every resumed session that the plan it was running was not authoritative. Because activePath also gates the dispatch section, the same run reported `nothing is in flight` while a subagent was running, and listed the live dispatch under `Dispatch records under plans STATUS.md does not name -- these do NOT make those plans active`. That is worse than silence: it invites a resumed controller to treat running work as stray. INDEPENDENTLY: 6 of the 18 ledgers under `.superpowers/sdd/` use the canonical `Task <n>:` form and 12 do not, so this plan's task-status list was empty too. BOTH HALVES WERE REPAIRED BY HAND the same day -- STATUS.md carries the marker again, and the sweep's ledger gained a `## Task status` section -- which is why this row is about the guard, not the breakage. NOT FIXED, and this is the finding: nothing asserts either convention, so the next reword or the next prose-heading ledger blinds the banner again with no failure anywhere to notice. `scripts/sdd-checkpoint.mjs --self-check` cannot catch it: it tests the script against a SYNTHETIC STATUS.md the check writes itself (`:109-120`), which is exactly why this drifted undetected for weeks. SEVERITY: high for recovery, low for the product -- the banner is the only input a resumed session trusts, and AGENTS.md names re-dispatching completed tasks the most expensive failure observed in real sessions. What settles it: one assertion in `scripts/check-status.mjs`, which already reads STATUS.md at `:142` and runs before every completed-task commit, that the marker parses and names an existing plan file -- removing the class rather than fixing this instance of it.
check: The banner now states the marker problem loudly, and check-status.mjs asserts the real STATUS.md marker parses and names an existing plan.

title: `runs.dom.test.ts` asserts the run preview against a clock it reads after the render, so the test fails on a minute boundary
detail: FOUND BY Task 5's lane during the dead-code sweep (2026-10-12) and attributed by its independent review, which could NOT reproduce it: the lane's full-suite run reported 1 failed, the review's re-run at the same commit `fd32a420` reported 770 suites / 3287 tests / 0 failed. What the review did establish is more useful than a base run could be -- `packages/editor` is byte-identical between base `742305d3` and HEAD, so the sweep's diff cannot be its cause. THE MECHANISM, read at HEAD: `packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/runs.dom.test.ts:220-221` pins a run's time zone through the UI and then asserts the preview text equals `formatInstant(instantIn(Date.now()), "HH:mm", "Asia/Tokyo")`. `Date.now()` is evaluated when the assertion runs, AFTER the component rendered, so a render at 07:40:59.9 and an assertion at 07:41:00.0 ask for `07:41` against a rendered `07:40` -- the lane observed exactly that pair, `07:40` versus `07:41`. The race fires roughly once in sixty runs of this case; it passed 4/4 when run alone. WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX ON THE FLY: it is not this sweep's code and the sweep's lane is not the owner, so repairing it there would have put an unrelated test fix inside a dead-code commit, and the fix is a real choice -- read the clock once before the interaction and assert against that value, or freeze time with `vi.setSystemTime` so the assertion and the render share one instant. The second is the deterministic one, since the first still compares two reads. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the same pattern appears in other inspector tests; no register row exists for this class, and `vg-363` is a different non-determinism (a fixture whose theme mtimes tie on a bare editor mount). CONSEQUENCE IF LEFT: the full suite reads red about once in sixty runs and the failure is misattributed to whichever commit is nearby, which is how this one arrived. VERIFIED at HEAD by the controller, which read the assertion and its `Date.now()` call directly.
check: runs.dom.test.ts pins Date.now with vi.spyOn so the preview render and the assertion share one instant.

title: The conversion to React field views left tests silently vacuous — a selector that no longer matches and a raw change event that no longer commits both still pass, so two instances were known and one is still live (the stale-opacity case; the Position accessible-name audit is fixed at 7841ec2d) and nothing detects a third
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 4. `index.dom.test.ts`'s 'refuses a stale opacity event rather than mutating the old selection' (base line 662) drives `[data-vigilia-opacity]` the pre-plan way — `input.value = "10"; input.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"))`. Task 3 converted Layer's opacity to a plan-1 `ControlNumber` (commit on blur, value held in React state), so the raw assignment is suppressed by React's value tracker and no commit is attempted. The case still passes because both its assertions — `rect.opacity` stays 0.5 and `saveState` is not called — are equally true when nothing was committed. WHY IT MATTERS. Task 4's brief names this test as the control for Step 2's requirement that the stale-draft refusal survives the conversion, so the plan believes a refusal it cannot fail is covered. The refusal does exist one layer down: `view.ts`'s `editRefusal` compares the revision the view was projected from with the live `targetRevision` and returns "stale", and `view.test.ts`'s 'reports a stale draft ahead of the lock it would also fail' proves that unit. What is missing is a DOM-level proof, and the architecture makes one hard to write deliberately: a republish keys each row by `${revision}:${fieldId}`, so a control bound to a superseded object is unmounted and can deliver no event. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a DOM proof is worth having, or whether the `editRefusal` unit case plus the four 'a draft and the object it describes' cases are the whole contract. This row is the same class as Task 3's leftovers: a case that reads green because the markup it drives moved. OWNER: whoever owns the inspector's test suite, alongside Task 7's locator sweep. SECOND INSTANCE, FOUND IN THE SAME PLAN, TASK 4 TASK REVIEW (2026-10-09, agent a6d8ea92dc02ac4bf). panel.dom.test.ts:550 ("gives every field on a %s an accessible name") selects ".vigilia-field > input, .vigilia-field > select, .vigilia-field > textarea, .vigilia-field-row input". The converted fields render through plan 1 control set, which emits data-vigilia-* hooks and Tailwind classes and no .vigilia-field at all, so as Position converted, the selector narrowed to fewer and fewer controls while the case kept passing. Its own guard is what let that happen silently: expect(controls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0) cannot tell "every field" from "one field". An accessible-name assertion that has narrowed is worse than a missing one, because the coverage it appears to give is counted. WHY ONE ROW AND NOT TWO. Both instances are the same problem, and the repair is the same job: a test that predates the conversion has to be re-pointed at what the converted surface actually emits. Filing them separately would hide that the class is at least twice as large as either sighting, and the real fix is a sweep rather than two patches. WHAT A SWEEP HAS TO DECIDE. Whether each re-pointed case is still needed at all: src/web/packages/editor/src/accessible-names.dom.test.ts (added by plan 3 task 3) audits accessibility for a FIXED list of mounted panels. It is NOT a duplicate of the Position case and must not be used to justify deleting it: that audit mounts the inspector on two specific selections (its own words at :224-234, the richest being a text object with a run bound to a clock), while panel.dom.test.ts case is it.each(SHAPES) and sweeps every shape kind, which the audit does not. The audit is explicit that its panel list IS its coverage and that a green run there must not be read as the editor being clean. So the repair is to re-point the per-shape case at what the converted surface emits and to STRENGTHEN its controls.length > 0 guard, not to delete it. PATH CORRECTED 2026-10-09: an earlier revision of this row said editor-shell/, which is wrong; the file is at the package root. That is a judgement per case, which is why this is a row and not a one-line fix. NOT ESTABLISHED: how many instances exist. Two were found by two different reviews reading different files, which is evidence of a class rather than a count. A sweep should look for every test whose selector or event predates the control set, in the selection-inspector and anywhere else a plan-3 task has converted a surface. RECORD HARDENED 2026-10-09 by plan 3's final whole-branch review, which found the count reading high: the Position accessible-name instance is FIXED at HEAD (7841ec2d, the audit's skip rule), so only the stale-opacity case is still live. Re-measured at the controller's hand: index.dom.test.ts:713-724 still drives [data-vigilia-opacity] with `opacity.value = "10"; dispatchEvent(new Event("change"))`, and that element is now a SLIDER by plan 3 Task 9's fix, so a raw change can no longer reach a commit path at all - the conversion made the remaining instance more vacuous rather than less, and its two assertions (opacity stays 0.5, saveState not called) are both true when nothing was attempted. The detection gap the title names is unchanged and still open.
check: The stale-opacity case now drives the converted slider and fails when the row's revision guard is removed, so it is no longer vacuous.

title: moveFocus's ArrowRight and ArrowLeft branches are exercised by no test

title: No document the test harness can load carries metadata.version, so the About tab's release row has no rendered proof and the parity gate cannot give it one

title: Base UI's popover cannot be closed under jsdom, so the close half of any popover contract is browser-only
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's fix round while restoring the address case in src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/publish-control.dom.test.tsx. Re-adding an assertion that the surface closes throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name') from inside Base UI's own close path, with no reachable stack. MEASURED: jsdom only - the same close IS proved in tests/e2e/publish-header.spec.ts, where a real browser hides the surface on a second press on the control. CONSEQUENCE: a dom test in this repo can assert that a popover OPENS but not that it CLOSES, so the close half of a popover contract is browser-only; whoever writes that assertion next and sees it throw will reasonably conclude the component is broken, when the harness is. The case was left asserting the open half, and the close half lives in the browser spec. OWNER/FIX: unassigned - a jsdom shim for whatever property Base UI reads off the close event would move it, but keeping close-path assertions in e2e is the honest fix until then. SEVERITY: low - a test-harness limitation with no user-visible effect.

RULED 2026-10-13: THE LIMITATION DOES NOT REPRODUCE AT HEAD, so the row closes on its finding being falsified rather than on a fix — and THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Probed independently by Task 7.4's reviewer and by its implementer: a close assertion on the surface passes under jsdom by second press on the header control, by Escape on the popup, and in the address case, and `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` appears nowhere. The row was measured 2026-10-09; the same close is proved in a real browser at `tests/e2e/publish-header.spec.ts:246-247` and always was. **The implementer's attribution of the cure to the `:modal`/`:popover-open` shim is REFUTED and must not be repeated:** that shim entered at `2eeb4516` (2026-10-09 06:04:23), about an hour BEFORE this row was filed (`deca4b80`, 2026-10-09 07:03:34), and was present in the file at that commit, so it cannot be what removed the trigger — something else changed between then and HEAD that nobody has named. What the shim does explain is the SHAPE of the failure without it: a 20s timeout (64s wall), never the throw the row cites. The case is landed rather than the row closed bare, because a close no dom test asserts is the gap the row named; `artefacts` names that commit and nothing else, since nothing was fixed — nothing was there to fix.
check: A close assertion on the Base UI popover under jsdom passes — second press and Escape both close it, and no TypeError is thrown — so the popover's close half is no longer browser-only and the row's named limitation does not reproduce at HEAD.

title: The gradient editor is missing from the accessible-name audit, so its control names are attested by nothing
detail:
FOUND WHILE REVIEWING plan 6 Task 4 (2026-10-11). Its first evidence line went stale on 2026-10-11 and is corrected here rather than left to mislead: Task 4's fix round 1 (`a512efb7`) made `control-icon-button.dom.test.tsx` import and mount `GradientEditor`, so the grep that returned nothing no longer does. THAT MOUNT DOES NOT CLOSE THIS ROW, and reading it as closure would be the mistake: the icon-only census excludes the stop dots by its own glyph clause -- a control is icon-only when its whole content is a glyph, and the dots draw none -- so mounting the editor there attests nothing about their names. The gap is the NAMING audit: `accessible-names.dom.test.ts`'s `mountPanels` still does not list the gradient editor. THE CONTROL THAT PUT THIS IN VIEW: `components/ui/gradient-editor.tsx:72-74` renders each stop as a drag handle carrying an `aria-label` built from the row's own label and the stop's index, plus `aria-valuenow` -- so it IS named, deliberately, in source; it simply is not checked by any test. WHY THAT IS THE DEFECT AND NOT A TIDY-UP: the same file's own doc comment states the contract in words -- adding a panel to the editor means adding it to `mountPanels`, and an unmounted panel is not audited, rather than audited and clean -- a distinction it learned from `vg-114`, where the asset pane and the new-theme chooser had gone years without appearing. The gradient editor is that case again, in a file this plan has since touched. WHAT MAKES IT SHARPER RATHER THAN MERELY STALE: Task 4 ruled the stop dots out of the icon-only census on the grounds that a drag handle draws no glyph, which is defensible on its own terms -- but it means the population that covers icon-only controls excludes them AND the population that should cover their names does not mount them, so the control sits between two audits with neither looking at it. The Task 4 fix round removed the weaker half of that complaint (the census now mounts the editor and is explicit about why the dots are outside it); the naming half is what remains. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the gradient editor joins `mountPanels`, or a stated reason says why it cannot be mounted there and what covers it instead. RELATED: `vg-114` is the same contract failing once before; this row is its third known instance rather than a new rule.

RULED 2026-10-13: THE ROW'S PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD AT HEAD, so it closes on the finding being falsified rather than fixed. Probed independently by Task 7.4's reviewer: `mountPanels` already reaches both `gradient-stop-*` handles through the palette panel (`selectPaletteToken(root, "glow")` → `TokensPane` → `PaintList` → `GradientEditor`, `paint-list.tsx:304`; the handles at `gradient-editor.tsx:72-74`), so they are in `FOCUSABLE`, they are `reached`, and the file's own generic case `gives every control an accessible name` (`accessible-names.dom.test.ts:121`) already asserted their names non-empty — before `2ed4e55b` and at filing, since the palette panel held the editor as a React child from `ebe1743b` (2026-10-10). **It is NOT closed on the second branch's "it cannot be mounted there":** the editor could be mounted directly; it is simply already reached, and a direct mount would add a second control with the same name. The exact names are now pinned by `2ed4e55b`; nothing was missing to fix.
check: The accessible-name audit reaches the gradient editor's two stop handles through the palette panel — its generic case already named them — and their exact names are now pinned by a case that reddens if the editor leaves the mount, so the row's premise does not hold at HEAD.

title: The font catalogue spec says a facet keeps untagged entries, and the shipped query drops them
detail: FOUND IN TASK 4 REVIEW, on the spec's own wording, not on the code's. Two sentences in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md disagree with what ships: the Facets-are-derived paragraph (~:118-119) says "A pairing carrying no matching tag stays reachable by search: facets narrow the list, they never remove an entry from it", and the Verification > Browser paragraph (~:195) turns it into a gate, "a facet filters without hiding untagged entries". font-catalog-query.ts does the opposite and is right to: matchesFacet() returns values.includes(facet.value), so an untagged entry is dropped from the list. Strict filtering is the only reading under which "facets narrow the list" is true — keeping the union of tagged and untagged is the whole list, so the control would never filter anything. The operative guarantee the spec means is the narrower one, "stays reachable by search", and the code honours it in the one place it literally applies: queryFaces() keeps a face when ANY seeding trio carries the tag, since the face itself carries no tags. So the fix is a SPEC AMENDMENT, which is Task 8's line, and the browser gate has to move with it in the same edit or it asserts the opposite of the code and records a false pass. Task 6 should not be blocked on this: its picker ships strict filtering, which is correct either way.
owner: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md:118-119,195 (amendment and browser gate are Task 8's line)
check: The font catalogue spec now states the shipped query rule: a facet narrows the list to the entries that carry its tag, so matchesFacet drops an untagged trio and queryFaces keeps a face while any seeding trio carries the tag. The Facets paragraph and the Browser verification bullet are both amended, and no source change was needed because the shipped query was already right.

title: A parity row is never checked against the property set its drawing declares, so a row - or its prose - can claim a comparison it does not make and still pass
detail: FOUND by plan 7 Task 8 fix round 2 on 2026-10-11, from the same audit family as vg-292. WHAT HAPPENED: `control-well.tsx`'s `ControlShape` doc said the boxed and headed shapes' `border-radius`/`gap` are read from their drawings 'rather than chosen here'. Reading was true. But both `PARITY` rows compared `border-radius` alone (`tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts`) while the drawings declared `gap:10px` and `gap:6px` too, so the product's `gap-[var(--space-10)]` and `gap-[var(--space-6)]` were compared to nothing. Round 2 added the two gap rows and each was shown failing against a one-step drift, and the controller reproduced the drift independently. WHY IT GENERALIZES: the failure is SILENT - a row that over-claims its coverage still passes, and only a reader who cross-checks the drawing notices, which is the same shape as vg-292 and vg-299 and the reason this plan exists. A `PARITY` row names exactly one `mockupProperty`; nothing relates that to the set the drawing selector actually declares, and nothing fails when the two disagree. Owner: the reader and the `PARITY` table (Task 1's instrument), which plan 7 has closed, so this needs either a small hardening task or a Task-6-style ratchet. What would settle it: a check that a row naming a property its drawing selector does not declare throws - the same 'fail loudly rather than resolve to nothing' rule the reader already applies to an unresolved or ambiguous selector.
check: vitest: `tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts` — `assertParityRowProperty` throws when a parity row names a property its drawing's selector does not declare, and throws the other way when a row marked `mockupSilence` names a property its element does declare; both halves were shown red with the rule disabled (commit dc8d0e1b).

title: A drawing's value that is on §3's scale but not the original's treatment is read by no gate, so the keyboard drawing shipped a 4px row container where the original draws 6px and only a reviewer's eye caught it
detail: FOUND IN PLAN 8 TASK 4 (2026-10-11), and found the only way it can be found today: the task review read `current/settings-keyboard.html` against the frozen original by eye. MEASURED: the row container carried `border-radius:4px` where `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:311` draws `border-radius:6px` and `docs/design/mockups/README.md:120-123` says the treatment - 'colour, spacing, radii, type, elevation, hairlines' - 'is copied from the original drawings' and 'is never redrawn from the product'. WHY NO GATE SAW IT, which is the finding rather than the value: the drawings gate asserts membership in §3's CLOSED SCALE - `design-language.spec.ts`'s 'every literal the checked drawings declare is on §3's scale or §2's', whose closed set is `const RADIUS = new Set(["4px", "6px", "8px", "10px", "999px"])` (both read at this close: `:3075` and `:3085`; §8.6 corrects the row's `SCALE` at `:2541`) - and 4px IS on that scale, being `--radius-sm`, 'swatches, inline chips, the slider thumb's container' (`design-language.md:90`). So the gate answers 'is this a value §3 has?' and never 'is this the value the original draws?', and a drawing can diverge from the original in any on-scale direction while every gate stays green. THE OTHER INSTRUMENTS CANNOT REACH IT EITHER: no `PARITY` row names that container, because it paints no fill and no border, so no colour or border row can address it; and plan 8 Task 8's widening to spacing and type is scale-based the same way, so it inherits the hole rather than closing it. The value was fixed in `3b46efb8` (4px to 6px, all 20 rows) after the review named it. NOT ESTABLISHED: what the right instrument is. Two candidates, and they are not equivalent - (a) a gate comparing the declarations of the elements a drawing COPIES from its original (the frame, the navigation, the Close control, the row containers) against the original's declarations, which needs a named list of copied elements because the current set is redrawn with the product's real content and a whole-file diff would be noise, or (b) the copied treatment declared once and imported by every drawing so it cannot drift, which is the stronger fix and changes how a drawing is authored. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those two, plus a ruling on which elements are copies rather than redrawings. RELATED: `vg-314` is the sibling class - a surface the drawing OMITS is one no gate can check - and this row is a value the drawing STATES wrongly; both are gaps in the drawing-versus-something comparison rather than in a value's own legibility. NOT THE SAME AS `vg-296`, which was a file nothing read at all.
check: vitest: `tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts` — `copiedElementDrift` compares the elements a drawing copies from `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html` and reports a value that drifted, including the keyboard drawing's row container at 4px where the original draws 6px; a full drift is named, one drifted row of twenty is refused as an unsettled address, and a comparator answering `[]` was shown red (commit 2bb9cdf0).

title: Four glyph-button hover rules wash the background where section 5 rule 6 requires an acquired --muted border
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 6's task review (low severity) and SCOPED BY MEASUREMENT by the controller before filing, so the row names a real set instead of an impression. UPDATED when Task 7 landed: the dock's instance is fixed, so the set is THREE, not four. Bible section 5 rule 6 is explicit: hover raises --edge to --muted, and on a glyph-only control with no resting border 'it is the border it acquires on hover. Nothing moves, nothing scales.' editor-shell.css carries 12 :hover rules, six of which set a background. THREE are glyph-only buttons that still hover with a wash where rule 6 prescribes the acquired border: .editor-shell-rail button:hover (:1024), .editor-shell-dialog > button:hover (:1557), .vigilia-layer-row button:hover (:2039). Two instances have since been fixed and are recorded here as the pattern the remaining three want. .editor-shell-view-step:hover was introduced by Task 6 and fixed in that task's own fix round (resting border 1px transparent, hover border-color: --muted, box-sizing: border-box declared on the rule so acquiring the border moves nothing). .editor-shell-dock button:hover was fixed by Task 7 the same way (editor-shell.css:847-849), which is the ruling applied consistently: the task that owns a surface fixes that surface's own rule, and a closed task's surface is left for the sweep. EXPLICITLY NOT PART OF THIS SET, and the row should not grow to include them: the menu item and menuitemradio hovers (:621, :623) and the menubar buttons (:574) are list-row and menu affordances, which are not in section 5's closed control vocabulary at all; .editor-shell-palette:hover (:682) is a swatch well, which already carries a resting border, so rule 6's second clause does not reach it. IMPORTANT FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: Task 8's ratchet CANNOT catch it. That guard reads hex literals and off-scale px values and is blind to a semantic rule, so this sweep needs its own owner and its own check rather than being assumed into the ratchet's coverage. OWNER: unassigned; Task 8 is the nearest home by subject but does not cover it by mechanism. SEVERITY: low - a hover affordance that differs from the prescribed one on three controls; nothing breaks, nothing is unreachable, and the deviation is consistent with itself today. RULED 2026-10-13 (plan 8.3 step 3, the section 8.2 line correction): the three citations above moved. At HEAD the rules they name are `.editor-shell-rail button:hover` (`editor-shell.css:1024`), `.editor-shell-dialog > button:hover` (`:1557`) and `.vigilia-layer-row button:hover` (`:2039`); the old `:801`, `:1119` and `:1400` now hold a closing brace, a closing brace and the `prefers-reduced-motion` selector list. Read at HEAD, only the rail's is still a wash and that is the one `7a92d0fe` fixed: the dialog's raises a resting `--shell-edge` to `--shell-accent`, and the layer row's acquired nothing at all, so this row's premise held for one of its three. Both are recorded in `7a92d0fe` and in `triage-B3.md`.
check: hovers the rail and the layer row's glyph slots in the browser and asserts the --muted hover border they acquire, reddening when either rule goes back to a background wash

title: A dialog's own body type resolves no §2 role — it inherits the portalled document's 13px (`packages/editor/index.html:21`), so the `?` sheet's rows render at §2's `--text-md` by accident where §2 gives list rows `--text-sm`
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 3 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `51245173`). MEASURED: `packages/editor/index.html:21` declares `html, body, #app { font: 13px/1.5 ... }`, and `.editor-shell-dialog` declares no base `font-size` of its own, so every dialog opened through the portal inherits that 13px — the `?` sheet's 20 rows included. §2 (`design-language.md:49`) gives list rows the 12px role, and `:50` separately names the 13px role for panel bodies, so the sheet's rows land on the right number for the wrong reason: no rule in the dialog's own sheet chose it, and the day the host document's base moves the sheet's rows move with it. WHY PLAN 8 TASK 3 DID NOT FIX IT IN PASSING: that task moved two rules whose values were wrong (`.editor-shell-dialog kbd` to `--text-xs`, `.editor-shell-dialog > button` to `--text-sm`), each of which declares its own size; this one is a size nothing declares, and giving the dialog a base role would set the type of every surface inside every dialog — five leads, two titles, the settings navigation, the palette grid and both sheets' rows — which is a region each of plan 8's later tasks owns and none of them would find green afterwards. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §2 role on `.editor-shell-dialog`'s own body rule, chosen per region rather than as one blanket base, with plan 8's drawings gate reading the row that lands on it, and the §13 capture in Task 10 showing the sheet. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the intended fix is a base on the dialog plus per-region overrides, or per-region declarations alone — the first re-moves Task 2's lead row if the override is missed, and the second leaves the portalled document as the base for anything a later surface adds.
check: reads the `?` sheet's rows resolving the dialog body's role at 12px in the browser, and reds when the dialog's own body rule drops the §2 role and the portalled document's 13px is inherited again

title: A dark-reporting OS's pre-attribute frame still takes editorial's display face and control paper, because the dark base omits the three tokens four palettes inherit from the bare root
detail: FOUND BY the vg-351 fix (2026-10-12), which repainted the pre-JS base under a prefers-color-scheme media query and then had to leave one corner of it editorial. WHAT: the dark base block in src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css deliberately omits --vigilia-control-bg, --shell-display and --shell-flat. WHY IT HAD TO: the media query matches :root with a palette resolved exactly as it does with no palette resolved, and :root and [data-shell-palette=x] have equal specificity, so a token declared there wins over the palette blocks by later source order. Those three are the tokens ember, moss, plum and light INHERIT from the bare root rather than declare for themselves, so carrying graphite values for them into the dark base would move four palettes' settled values on any dark-reporting OS -- a worse defect than the one being fixed, which is why the fix stopped. COST, and it is visible: on a dark OS a fresh profile's first frame is graphite's ground and text but editorial's display face and control paper, so the flash is reduced rather than eliminated. NOT the same finding as vg-351, which is closed: vg-351 was the base painting a palette the resolver never returns, and this is a base that returns the right palette while three of its secondary tokens come from somewhere else. CLOSE THIS by giving the four inheriting palettes explicit declarations for those three tokens, so the dark base can carry graphite's without moving anything -- which is the change the fix declined to make. Evidence: the stylesheet records the omission and its reason; the fix report is .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-design-md-replaces-the-bible/vg-351-report.md (git-ignored).
check: the pre-attribute frame of a dark-reporting OS reads graphite for all three tokens, and the token test reds when the dark base omits them

title: The bridge republishes the whole shell snapshot on every document change, so menus, dock and display switch re-render per edit
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 5 (the implementer raised it against itself) and judged by its task review. To make a rename reach the new identity chip, bridge.ts:145 subscribes input.session.subscribeDocumentChange(notify) unconditionally. A rename moves no Fabric object, so no canvas event fires for it - but subscribeDocumentChange fires on far more than renames: editor-session.ts:224 (#announceChange) is called from editor:edit-committed, object:added/removed (:268-273), every envelope write (#writeEnvelope, :1010) and saves (:725, :817). So the whole EditorShellSnapshot republishes, and the menus, dock and display switch re-render on committed edits, token/binding/metadata edits and saves - not only on a rename. RULED 2026-10-13 (the date THIS PLAN re-ratified and normalised the ruling; the row's own prose carried it undated, and no revision of either register ever held an earlier dated marker -- `git log -S "RULED 2026-10-09"` over both files returns nothing): acceptable as landed, not a defect: re-renders are idempotent, no correctness is lost, and the review judged it not a 'behaviour change' under the plan's Global Constraint (same fields, gates, refusals, markers). It is avoidable in roughly three lines - the bridge could cache the pulled name and call notify() only when it differs, since only documentName needs this signal (selectedCount/locked/activeKind already ride the canvas events) - without adding any session API. The implementer's claim that 'the session exposes no name-only signal' is literally true but half the story. OWNER: unassigned; the review's recommendation was to keep it and narrow only if a later task measures a cost. SEVERITY: low - re-render churn, no correctness loss.
check: `editor-shell/bridge.ts` republishes the whole snapshot on `session.subscribeDocumentChange` (`grep -n subscribeDocumentChange packages/editor/src/editor-shell/bridge.ts`), and `bridge.dom.test.ts`'s "carries the document's name, and republishes it when the theme is renamed" pins it — the behaviour the ruling accepts, not narrowed.

title: Every chart repaint asks the whole canvas to redraw, and charts re-apply their options 30 times a second
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-081, which is where that fix's work stopped. Two costs, both on the idle path, both now the largest that remains. (1) scene-fabric/src/chart-object.ts:227 — every ECharts rendered event asks Fabric for a full-canvas render, measured at 525 of 624 canvas renders across 3 s of doing nothing at all. One chart's animation frame redraws the whole document. (2) ChartManager.refresh re-applies every chart's option at the chart refresh rate whether or not that chart's data moved; the rate is the author's own chartRefreshRate control, which is why this is a decision and not a patch — the View menu offers 30 FPS and 1 FPS and an author who picks either is choosing this cost. vg-081 removed the TEXT side of the same argument and the idle cost fell 14x; this is the other half. LEFT ALONE because chart-manager/ belonged to another agent during that pass and because (2) touches a control the user sets. Worth pairing with the decision the user already has open on vg-086's menu, since that is where the rate is chosen.
check: `ChartManager.refresh` re-applies only the charts whose newest sample moved and `VigiliaChart._onEngineRendered` no longer asks the canvas to redraw, pinned by `chart-manager/index.dom.test.ts` — "is not drawn again, and is drawn the moment the reading moves" and "is a chart with no bindings: drawn once, and never for the loop again" — and by `chart-object.dom.test.ts` "asks the canvas to redraw for its own repaint, and not for the engine's"; both cases red when their half is reverted.

title: The document's name-else-id reading is spelled in three places in editor-main.ts
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 5's implementer and carried in its commit as a Discovered, not fixed trailer. The rule 'the document's name, else its id' now appears at editor-main.ts:271 and :387 (the status line) and at :294 (the bridge's projection of EditorShellSnapshot.documentName added by Task 5), so a change to how an unnamed theme is identified must be made in all three or they will disagree about what the document is called. The implementer named the cause but did not unify them, on the grounds that doing so reaches the status line's own wording, which no test pins. OWNER: unassigned - the natural fix is a single exported helper that both the status line and the bridge projection call, which is also what 'one owner per concept' asks for. SEVERITY: low today - the three spellings are identical, so nothing disagrees yet; the risk is a future edit that changes one. NOTE: this is the duplicate-reading class the same plan's Task 2 addressed for object-action eligibility with objectActionsFor(gate). UPDATE 2026-10-09 after plan 2 Task 5 fix round 1 (cf82c14f): the bridge projection no longer spells the rule - Task 5 moved it into a testable seam (bridge.ts input documentIdentity?: () => {name, id}, with the fallback taken there), so editor-main.ts:294 now hands over raw facts. That leaves the rule spelled at :271 and :387 (the status line) versus the bridge, and the divergence is now OBSERVABLE rather than theoretical: for a schema-valid theme whose metadata.name is empty, the identity chip shows the id while the status line still writes a blank "Opened ". The implementer filed that as a Discovered, not fixed trailer rather than changing the status line wording, which is a behaviour change outside Task 5 scope. This strengthens the case for the single exported helper: the two spellings have already drifted once.
check: the name-else-id reading is spelled once in `packages/editor/src` — `documentNameOf`, in `editor-shell/bridge.ts`, called by both status lines in `editor-main.ts`, by the snapshot's `documentName` and by the publish control's `Showing …` line — pinned by `bridge.dom.test.ts` "names the document once, so the status line and the chip cannot disagree" (reds on the old `??` spelling) and by `publish-control.dom.test.tsx` "names a document the theme never named by its id". The host's library listing spells a FIFTH spelling for its own entry (`host/src/themes/store.ts:555`) -- `envelope.metadata?.name ?? id` where this row's `documentNameOf` uses `||` -- outside this row and filed as `vg-427`: on `metadata.name === ""` the host keeps the empty string where the editor falls back to the id, and `schema/theme-document.schema.json:30` permits it (`maxLength: 200`, no `minLength`).

title: The Document pane still sets a panel marker named style, and the reason it was kept has expired
detail: FOUND BY THE WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW of the composition-panel plan (`2026-10-06-the-composition-panel.md`). selection-inspector/style.ts:83 sets root.dataset["vigiliaPanel"] = "style" on what is now the left columns Document pane references panel. editor.spec.ts:2152 reads that value, so it works, but the name says Style tab for a panel that is not one. THE MARKER WAS DELIBERATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT, and that is why this is a row rather than a correction: Task 8s brief kept data-vigilia-panel="style" on purpose because renaming it would have broken the very locator Task 9 was rewiring in the same plan, and Task 9 then rewired that locator to openPane(page, "Document"). The reason it was kept has therefore expired, which leaves a rename available now that was not available then. Not done here because it is a product-source change touching a spec locator, and plan 4 is closed.

title: A browser spec hard-codes a copy object id that the sibling spec states is the allocators to choose
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW. tests/e2e/insert-popover.spec.ts:129 locates a card this test inserted as `[data-vigilia-layer="card-group-time-card"]`, and tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:1002 states the rule that breaks: a copys id is the allocators to choose. It is deterministic today, because card-library.ts:97 sets COPY_PREFIX to card and createWidgetIdAllocator mints past what the destination already holds, so the first copy of the clock into an empty starter is card-group-time-card. The objection is not flakiness but ownership: the id is a product decision restated in a second place, so a change to the copy prefix or to the allocator moves the product and leaves this spec asserting a string it no longer controls. Low severity. The review also noted that this case now overlaps Task 6s second composition-panel case, both inserting a Clock from the + and reading its row, because the plan ordered Task 3 before Task 6.
check: the Add pane spec counts the Clock rows the insert adds rather than naming the id the allocator mints for the copy — the sibling `composition-panel.spec.ts` states a copy's id is the allocator's to choose. Red-proved by setting `card-library.ts`'s `COPY_PREFIX` to `copy`: the old id locator failed, the counted one passed.

title: The host re-spells the assignable-device-id union inline in server.ts rather than deriving it from the settings module that owns it
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.2 OF PLAN 7, the judgement walk, while adjudicating what `npm run ownership:sweep` reported. Pre-existing, in `packages/host`, and outside every plan of the current redesign. THE MEASUREMENT: `cd src/web && npm run ownership:sweep` exits 0 with `mapRows: 99`, `sourceFiles: 257`, and reports exactly two vocabulary hits plus the same two pairs again as `subsetReSpellings` -- vocabulary 'Device assignment and display names', owner `packages/host/src/settings/devices.ts`, re-spelled in `packages/host/src/main.ts` and `packages/host/src/server.ts`, sharing `system-disk`/`data-disk` (2 of 3). THE OWNER IS `ASSIGNABLE_GROUPS` at `devices.ts:15`. THE TWO HITS ARE NOT THE SAME: `main.ts:203-208` only INDEXES `storedDevices.assigned["system-disk"|"data-disk"]`, which is a consumer reading the owner's ids and is the rule working; `server.ts:394` writes the union out again as a parameter type, `group: "gpu" | "system-disk" | "data-disk"`, and `server.ts:398-399` repeats the literals. That second one is a genuine second owner of the vocabulary: adding a fourth assignable group to `devices.ts` can never reach it, and nothing would fail. Adjudicated by the walk and re-read by the root; the sweep's own output is the evidence. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is not this plan's task, it is in another package, and the fix is a small question about where the type should be exported from rather than a one-line change in place. Cross-reference `vg-184`, which is the sweep being unable to see a vocabulary spelled as a type union at all -- the reason this row had to be found by reading the tool's output rather than by the tool naming it directly.
check: `server.ts` takes `AssignableGroup` from `settings/devices.ts` rather than spelling the union again — `main.ts`'s indexing of the same ids is a consumer reading the owner and is left alone. Pinned by `server.test.ts` "keeps the assignable-device vocabulary in the one module that owns it" (reds when the union is re-spelled) and "publishes every group the settings module declares it can assign" (reds when a fourth group is added to the owner).

title: The draft/commit keyboard decision is duplicated between control-text.tsx and control-number.tsx
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 1 (gates-and-the-control-set) FINAL CODE REVIEW and PARKED by the controller, not fixed. src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-text.tsx:73-88 and control-number.tsx:137-150 each re-implement the same draft/commit keyboard decision - the composing ref, the Enter/IME guard, and the Escape reset - and both copies are currently correct. Extracting a helper is a real refactor of the two most intricate controls at the moment the plan closes, for a drift risk that has not bitten, so it is filed rather than fixed. OWNER: plan 3 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-the-inspector.md, the per-kind inspector), the next plan to touch the text/number pair. The exit is one shared hook the two controls call; leaving it risks the two copies drifting before plan 3 reaches them. OWNER REACHED, NOT DISCHARGED (recorded 2026-10-09 when plan 3 closed): plan 3 did touch this pair - three commits, 07774ce8, 612cfdd9 and 07869755, +119/-49 across the two files - and the duplication survived it intact, so the copies are still two and both still correct. The line citations above are now stale for the number control: its composing ref is at control-number.tsx:76 and its Enter/Escape guard at :142-157, where control-text.tsx's ref is at :54 and its guard at :75-88. Plan 3's plan file now lives at docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-the-inspector.md, so the owner this row names is spent: IT NEEDS A NEW OWNER, and plan 4 - the panes - is the next work over this same control set.

title: WidgetIssue invalid-id is unreachable, because sanitizeId always returns a string that matches STABLE_ID_PATTERN
detail: FOUND while rewriting packages/renderer-core/src/theme/widget.test.ts during the schema-v1 retirement (2026-10-11). createWidgetIdAllocator sanitises `${prefix}-${original}`, and sanitizeId (theme/widget.ts:60) replaces every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] with "-" and slices to 64, so the result is non-empty whenever the input is and a single "-" already satisfies STABLE_ID_PATTERN (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/). The guard at theme/widget.ts:36 can therefore never fire, and no ids the allocator mints can carry the code. The old widget.test.ts did not cover it either, so it has never been exercised. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the member is part of the exported WidgetIssue union, and the editor switches on it (card-library.ts and clipboard-manager/index.ts both build WidgetIssue[]), so narrowing the union is a public change to two callers rather than a local cleanup. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether an id can arrive here carrying no usable character at all; if it cannot, delete the branch and the member together.
check: `sanitizeId` is total — its only input is `${prefix}-${original}`, which carries the `-` and so is never empty, and it replaces every other character with `-` — so `WidgetIssue["invalid-id"]` was unreachable and is deleted together with its branch; `widget.test.ts` "is not a member and has no branch to reach, read off `widget.ts`" reds when either is restored.

title: Delete is marked destructive in the dock only, from a second owner declared inside the dock
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 7's task review, which judged it an OWNER VIOLATION rather than acceptable per-surface emphasis at LOW severity. canvas-dock.tsx:20 declares DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS = new Set(["delete"]), which re-decides inside the dock a fact about the registry entry (object-actions.ts:195, in the module whose own comment at :100 reads 'One owner for object actions: what each is, when it applies, how it runs'). The same registry is rendered by two other surfaces - the layer panel's footer and the canvas context menu - and NEITHER marks Delete as destructive (grep for --hot or 'destructive' across both files returns nothing), so one concept, 'this action destroys', is now expressed on one of the three surfaces that render it. The author-visible consequence: Delete is --hot in the dock and ordinary in the layer footer and the context menu, which reads as the dock warning about something the other two do not. Bible section 4 places 'destructive' on the action, so the owner is the registry entry: add a destructive flag there, let one marker be shared by all three surfaces, and delete the dock's set. Deliberately NOT fixed in Task 7 even though the mark itself came from that task's brief: object-actions.ts is outside its file set, and un-marking the dock to match the two older surfaces would trade a correct new surface for consistency with incorrect ones - the same line Task 6 drew when it fixed its own hover rule and left the rail's. It breaks nothing today: the added data-vigilia-destructive attribute is additive and leaves both equality selectors (editor.spec.ts:3877, snapping.spec.ts:581) and every aria-label untouched, which the review verified from source. OWNER: the object-action registry. SEVERITY: low.
check: Delete is `--hot` — not merely `data-vigilia-destructive` — in the dock, the layer footer and the canvas context menu: all three carry the registry's `destructive` mark and paint it from the one `[data-vigilia-destructive] { color: var(--hot) }` rule, held by `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts`'s allowlist over every colour-bearing rule whose selector names a button or a menu item, and settled in the browser by the dock-versus-menu-versus-footer computed-colour case in `editor.spec.ts`.

title: gradient-editor.tsx draws a 1px outline with a raw #000 literal, which is a colour value no token owns
detail:
FOUND WHILE REVIEWING plan 6 Task 4 (2026-10-11); reported by the implementer as pre-existing and left untouched, which is the right call for a task about accessible names, but unfiled is not the same as recorded. `components/ui/gradient-editor.tsx:79` sets `boxShadow: "0 0 0 1px #000"` — a raw hex where every other value in the editor comes from plan 1 tokens (bible section 4 names colour ROLES, and `editor-shell.css` owns the palette). [STRUCK 2026-10-13 because it is FALSE: `git log -S "gradient-editor.tsx" --all -- scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` returns no commits ever, and the list is the files ALREADY CONVERTED -- a listed file must be clean, so one holding a raw `#000` cannot be on it. The literal was found by reading plan 6's Task-4 diff, not by a scanner. See the correction at the end of this detail.] CAUSE IS ESTABLISHED AND IT IS NARROW: a hard-coded outline colour. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and is why this is filed rather than fixed: which ROLE that outline is. It reads as a hairline separating a stop dot from the track beneath it, which could be section 4 boundary (the focus boundary already has a 3:1 requirement per the user ruling on `vg-200`) or a shadow role (`--elev-*`), and picking one is a read of the drawing and of what the outline is for rather than a substitution anyone can make from the literal alone. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the role named, the literal replaced with its token, and the gated count falling by one.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller as a code/architecture correctness question: THE 1PX RING IS SECTION 4'S BOUNDARY ROLE, AND THE LITERAL BECOMES THE BOUNDARY TOKEN. gradient-editor.tsx:79 writes boxShadow 0 0 0 1px #000 to separate the dot from the track behind it, which is separation rather than altitude -- and it cannot be an --elev-* role, because none of the ladders five declared values (editor-shell.css:492-499 at HEAD; the ruling's `:462-466` is stale) is a 1px spread ring; they are all offset-and-blur depths. The role is named and the raw literal replaced, which also drops the gated count by one. COST IF WRONG: one hairline's colour moves to the shell's edge token, visible on the gradient editor alone. CORRECTED 2026-10-13 BY TASK 8.3B'S SEAT AND CONFIRMED BY THE CONTROLLER: THE ROW'S STATED CAUSE IS FALSE AND THE RULING REPEATS IT. `grep -c gradient-editor scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` is 0 -- the file was NEVER in the token scanner, while 17 other `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/` files are -- so "Task 4 added this file to `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`" did not happen and the literal did not come into view through the scanner; a reviewer found it. The consequence is that `vg-334`'s CLOSE cannot be, and is not, "the gated count falling by one": `npm run design:check` does not move, and the fix is verified by the rendered dot alone. THE DECISION THE FALSE PREMISE WAS STANDING IN FOR -- whether that file belongs in the scanner -- is not settled here and is filed as its own row.
check: The gradient editor's stop-dot outline draws section 4's `--edge` boundary token instead of the raw `#000` literal, read off the rendered dot in `gradient-editor.dom.test.tsx`.
