title: The built stylesheet emits only the prefixed -webkit-backdrop-filter, so the glass blur applies in no browser that has dropped the alias and the cluster treatment is a gradient and a shadow alone
check: No rule in `editor-shell.css` declares `backdrop-filter` at all: the cluster treatment is the chrome's own 95% fill and §3's `--elev-1` shadow alone, so there is no blur left for the build to prefix away, and `shell-appearance.spec.ts` asserts every floating cluster computes `backdropFilter: none` and paints no gradient. [CLOSED 2026-10-13: this retires the SYMPTOM, not the cause. The editor's `vite.config.ts` still names no `css.lightningcss.targets`, so lightningcss remains free to ship only a prefixed form of any property — that cause is filed as `vg-430`, and this row's own text already called it "a configuration gap rather than a stylesheet one".]
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11) while writing the treatment boundary assertion, which wanted to read a cluster's `backdrop-filter` and found it unreadable under every palette. MEASURED IN THE BUILT BUNDLE: `packages/editor/dist/assets/index-*.css` carries `-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(10px)saturate(135%)` and `-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(6px)` and NO unprefixed `backdrop-filter` declaration at all (a `[;{]backdrop-filter:` sweep returns zero matches), while `editor-shell.css` declares both properties on both rules. MEASURED IN THE BROWSER: in this Chromium (HeadlessChrome/153.0.8010.12) `CSS.supports("backdrop-filter","blur(1px)")` is true and `CSS.supports("-webkit-backdrop-filter","blur(1px)")` is false; `getComputedStyle().backdropFilter` reads `none` on the dock, the view cluster and the identity chip under all six palettes; and a probe that sets the STANDARD property inline computes `blur(10px) saturate(1.35)`, so the property works and the shipped declaration is what does not. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this Chromium has dropped the alias or the packaged build differs from Chrome stable; what is established is that the bundle ships only the prefixed form and this browser does not apply it. The build is Vite 8 (Rolldown) with the editor's `vite.config.ts` setting no `css.lightningcss.targets` and no browserslist, so lightningcss picks the prefix and the standard longhand is dropped - a configuration gap rather than a stylesheet one. NOT FIXED IN TASK 5: the fix is a build target, and Task 5 owns the treatment boundary, not the toolchain. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE: the cluster half of the boundary is asserted as translucency + gradient + elevation shadow and cannot assert the blur as a computed value, which is also why `shell-appearance.spec.ts` had already chosen `box-shadow` rather than `backdrop-filter` as its discriminator. TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the browser half this row owed is taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3. CSS.supports('backdrop-filter','blur(1px)') is true while CSS.supports('-webkit-backdrop-filter','blur(1px)') is false; getComputedStyle().backdropFilter reads 'none' on the dock ([data-vigilia-canvas-toolbar]), on the view cluster (.editor-shell-zoom) and on the identity chip (.editor-shell-identity); and the freshly built stylesheet, index-BCKGgSdQ.css, carries THREE -webkit-backdrop-filter declarations and ZERO unprefixed backdrop-filter longhands (a [;{]backdrop-filter: sweep returns nothing against a raw count of FIVE -webkit-backdrop-filter occurrences, FOUR of which carry the colon and three of which are declarations, the two non-declaration sites being the @supports not ((-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(1px)) or (backdrop-filter:blur(1px))) condition, which carries the colon, and a transition-property value list in which -webkit-backdrop-filter and backdrop-filter sit among filter and display, which does not). Both halves of the row now reproduce. STAYS OPEN: the fix is the editor's build target, and which browsers the editor's stylesheet targets is a support-matrix decision that rewrites the whole built stylesheet — the opposite of a line this task may guess at.

title: `npm run gate` calls itself the one command that means green and omits `npm run design:check`, so a red design:check survives every local close until CI
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13 BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE FIXING `vg-319`'S SECOND FACT, WHICH IS NOT THE TASK IT BELONGS TO. MEASURED: on a clean tree at `3be574fe`, `npm run design:check` exits **1**, naming `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1071 right: 7px` -- "holds 1 violation(s) the record does not, above its ceiling of 0 -- re-record the file's residual set". A `git stash` of the working change re-ran it identically, so it was red at HEAD and not red because of the edit in progress. CAUSE, NAMED. `src/web/package.json`'s `gate` is `biome check .. && npm run gates:self-test && npm run test`; `design:check` is `node ../../scripts/design-tokens.mjs && npm run design:md`. **They are different commands and CI runs both, as separate steps** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:56` runs `npm run gate`, `:63` runs `npm run design:check`). So the local recipe and CI differ by exactly one step, and the local one is the one every close in this repo uses. `gate`'s own `//gate` comment in `package.json` reads "The one command that means green (D1's ruling, 2026-10-12 ...)" -- and it does not mean green while a step CI runs is red. `gates:self-test` does include `design-tokens.mjs --self-test`, which is why the gate is green: it runs the instrument's own fixtures and never the instrument over this repo's files. WHAT INTRODUCED IT: Phase 8's rail fix `8b1b9106` set `right: -7px` on `.editor-shell-rail button[aria-pressed="true"]::before` to compensate the 1px a `§5` rule-6 transparent resting border insets the padding box by -- a correct measurement -- and did not record it in `scripts/design-tokens.mjs`'s `CEILINGS`, whose `max` is `0` over that file. WHAT MISSED IT, AND THIS IS THE FINDING: **Phase 8's close and Phase 9's close both ran `npm run gate` and nothing else**, and the drain's ledger rule names that command and its exit code as a close's evidence. Two consecutive closes therefore reported green over a red check, which is the exact failure that rule was written to prevent -- the rule got the exit code right and the command wrong. Had anything been pushed, `ci.yml:63` would have failed on a commit whose close said green. FIXED 2026-10-13, and the fix is the violation rather than the recipe: the missing `CEILINGS` entry was added by name with the reason it is not a step, and `npm run design:check` now exits **0** with `counted: 0` and `dead: 0`. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE REST: a decision this row does not take -- either `design:check` joins `gate`, which makes the comment true and lengthens every local gate run, or it stays a separate step and `gate`'s own comment stops claiming to be the one command that means green, with the drain's close rule naming both commands and both exit codes. Either way the close recipe in `docs/superpowers/plans/` and `AGENTS.md`'s verification section need to agree with whichever is chosen rather than naming `npm run gate` alone. NEAR ROWS: `vg-434` (no check resolves a reference into the plans directory) -- a different missing instrument, and the same shape: a rule the repo believes is enforced and is not. `vg-327` (a ceiling count sees a rise and not a swap). OWNER: `src/web/package.json`'s scripts together with `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which is the statement of what CI actually runs. SEVERITY: medium -- nothing behaves wrongly in the product, and the cost is not the 1px. It is that a close can report green while a check CI runs is red, which is the one thing a close's evidence rule exists to make impossible. CLOSED 2026-10-13, AND THE OPTION TAKEN IS THE FIRST OF THE TWO THE ROW NAMED. `design:check` joins `gate` rather than the close recipe learning to name two commands, and the measurement is what decided it: the check runs in **1536 ms** on this box, so the "lengthens every local gate run" cost the row weighed is negligible against a close that can report green while a check CI runs is red. **It is also the only option available that does not require editing `AGENTS.md`**, which is user-owned: its verification section names `npm run gate` alone, and that is now complete rather than wrong. The row's other propagation ask is satisfied by the same move -- the close recipe in `docs/superpowers/plans/` names `npm run gate` alone, which is now the whole local gate, so no plan text needed changing. What did need changing was the drain plan's Task-level annotation at `:593`, which had restated CI's step list (`vg-384`'s rot, in the very annotation that warns about it); it now names the command rather than enumerating the steps, and records that the separate CI step went with the change.

title: The `--text-*` line-height companions are declared and consumed at one site of twenty-three, so the settings dialog reads 1.5 where DESIGN.md section 2 states 1.4
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13 while checking whether the settings dialog still matches its drawing after the 2026-10-13 chrome fixes. **MEASURED, in a browser against a bundle built from HEAD.** `.editor-shell-dialog` computes **12px / 18px (1.5)** and `.editor-shell-dialog-lead` **15px / 22.5px (1.5)**, read with `getComputedStyle` off the live sheet. DESIGN.md section 2 states `--text-sm` **1.4** (16.8px) and `--text-lg` **1.3** (19.5px), and the drawing this surface is pulled to, `docs/design/mockups/current/settings-about.html`, declares `font: 12px/1.45 system-ui`. **Three values for one element, and the shipped one is the loosest.** **THE MECHANISM, AND THE COUNT IS THE FINDING.** The six companions are declared in the `@theme static` block (`editor-shell.css:478-489`, `--text-2xs--line-height` through `--text-xl--line-height`), and the note above them says they are "stated, not inherited" -- with the reason that Tailwind computes its own from a size the token no longer has. But the only shape that consumes a companion is Tailwind's own utility: the built CSS carries `.text-sm{font-size:var(--text-sm);line-height:var(--tw-leading,var(--text-sm--line-height))}`, while a rule that writes `font-size: var(--text-sm)` directly takes the size and drops the companion, leaving the element on `html`'s preflight `line-height: 1.5`. **Measured across the shell: 22 `font-size: var(--text-*)` declarations, 3 literal line-heights (`1.2` at `:1266`, `1.35` at `:1932`, `1` at `:2119`), and one Tailwind `text-*` utility in the whole editor-shell -- `settings.tsx:234`'s `text-sm`.** So one site of twenty-three receives the companion section 2 states, and every other shell surface inherits 1.5. The `@theme static` note anticipates declared-and-never-consumed tokens and points at the `design-tokens.gated.json` ratchet, but that file gates *files* against the design language, not token consumption, and it names no `line-height` -- so this is not already-recorded debt. **WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX.** The correct value is a design decision with three candidates already in the repo (section 2's stated companion, the drawing's 1.45, or accepting the inherited 1.5), and the fix is either "state the companion wherever a size is stated" across 22 sites or "set it once on the shell root and retire section 2's companions" as a scale member. Neither is an on-the-fly edit. **NOT ESTABLISHED.** Whether 1.5 was ever chosen: no comment in `editor-shell.css` mentions a line-height outside the `@theme` note and those three literal sites, so the divergence reads as unexamined rather than decided. And only the dialog's two elements were measured -- the other 21 sites are inferred from the rule shape, not from a reading per site. NEAR ROWS: `vg-326` (the same token family from the other side: the drawings' `font` shorthand sets no line-height, so drawn row heights are font-metric-dependent); `vg-317` (the `--text-sm` decision that gave the dialog its size and did not give it a companion); `vg-435` (same class -- a rule the repo behaves as though something enforces). SECOND MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-13 -- THE PROPERTY IS UNREAD ON BOTH SIDES OF THE COMPARISON, AND ITS VALUE IS ALREADY PINNED WHERE A UTILITY IS USED. Three results from looking for the check that should have caught this, and one of them corrects this row's own first reading. **(1) The expected value is already asserted, for the utility.** `shell-appearance.spec.ts:424-429` pins `text-sm` to `{ "font-size": "12px", "line-height": "16.8px" }` and `text-xs` to `14.3px` -- 12 x 1.4 and 11 x 1.3, exactly section 2's companions. So 16.8px is not merely stated in prose, it is a value the repo tests; the dialog computes 18px on the same token. **(2) The drawing side cannot read it either, and says so.** `design-language.spec.ts:3054-3057`, in the row that owns section 2's type scale, reads: "What this row cannot read, and does not claim. `line-height`, `font-weight` and `letter-spacing`" -- with the reason that a drawing's `/1` on a one-line label is a box rather than a reading step. So no instrument reads this property on either side of the parity comparison, which is how it survived a gate that is otherwise thorough. That limit is a dispositioned one, not an oversight, and this row is not re-opening it: what it did not cover is the product's side, where the value is stated and pinned. **(3) The drawing's 1.45 is page furniture, not a competing value -- correcting this row's first reading.** `settings-about.html:10` writes `font: 12px/1.45` inside the file's `<style>` block, which is the page body; the modal inside it declares no line-height and inherits that one. The same comment at `:3058-3065` says the page furniture is read like everything else and passes today only because its values happen to be on the scale. **So this is not a three-way tie between 1.4, 1.45 and 1.5: the drawn surface states no line-height of its own, and section 2's companion is the specified value.** **WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN IS SCOPE, NOT VALUE.** The question is whether section 2's companion binds every direct `font-size: var(--text-*)` in the shell -- 22 sites, all in one stylesheet, each taking its own token's companion -- or only Tailwind's utility. It stays a row rather than becoming a fix for two reasons: the first reading changes rendered line boxes across the whole shell by roughly 7%, and no existing check can see the property, so the change lands green either way and only a browser assertion proves it. **ALSO MEASURED, AND NOT FILED AS ITS OWN ROW BECAUSE IT IS ALREADY DISPOSITIONED.** Of the drawings' 47 declared property kinds, the two readers between them cover 14 -- `ParityRegion`'s eleven plus the declaration-level reader's `border`, `box-shadow` and `margin-top`. The unread remainder is mostly layout scaffolding (`display`, `flex`, `position`, `align-items`, `margin`, `overflow`, `min-height`), and of it only the three properties `design-language.spec.ts:3054` already names are design-language subjects. Colour is not among the gaps: `SHELL_ROLES`' eleven-token table compares the drawings' palette tokens against the product's `--shell-*` values. NO NEW ROW: filing the remainder would re-report a limit the code states in its own words. NEAR ROWS: `vg-326` (the same class from section 3: a drawn rule no gate reads); `vg-317` (the size decision this one is the missing half of). THIRD MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-13 -- WHAT THE DRAWINGS ACTUALLY RENDER, WHICH MAKES THE VALUE CONTESTED THREE WAYS AND CORRECTS THIS ROW'S SECOND READING. Each of the six drawings in `current/` was loaded in Chromium and every element holding its own text was tallied by its resolved `font-size`/`line-height`, so this is the drawings' rendered rhythm rather than the declarations they inherit it from. **THE DRAWINGS' 12px TEXT RENDERS AT 1.45, NOT AT SECTION 2's 1.4.** `settings-about.html` 7 elements at 12px/17.4px; `settings-keyboard.html` 24 at 12px/17.4px; `settings.html` 4 at 12px/17.4px; `shell.html` 7 at 12px/17.4px. Every one is 1.450, and not one element in any drawing renders 12px at 1.4. **THE 11px TEXT DOES THE SAME**, at 15.95px = 1.45: 12 elements in each of `controls.html` and `controls-light.html`, 12 in `shell.html`, 7 in `settings.html`. Section 2's companion for `--text-xs` is 1.3. **So there are three values for the same role, and no instrument compares any of them.** The product computes **1.5** (Tailwind preflight, inherited); DESIGN.md section 2 states **1.4**; every drawing renders **1.45**. The parity gate reads no line-height at all (`design-language.spec.ts:3054`), so the drawing side was never compared and the three coexisted unseen. **THIS CORRECTS THE SECOND MEASUREMENT, WHICH WAS TOO DISMISSIVE.** It read `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` as page furniture and concluded that the drawn surface states no line-height of its own, so section 2's companion was simply the specified value. The furniture reading is right about where the *declaration* lives (`:3058-3065` explains that the furniture is read like everything else and that a furniture value off the scale would redden that row) and wrong about the consequence: the ratio reaches every drawn element, and 1.45 is what the acceptance instrument shows. **The value is therefore contested between the instrument the user ruled is the acceptance instrument and the contract DESIGN.md states, and that is the user's call, not this row's.** **METHOD, AND ONE THING IT DOES NOT MEASURE.** Elements whose computed `line-height` is `normal` were excluded rather than counted: the probe substituted size x 1.2 for them, which is a guess at the font's own metric and not a reading. So the counts above are explicit values only, and the drawings carry more text at `normal` than the tally shows. Repeating this must exclude `normal` or it will report a number nobody set. **WHAT A FIX WOULD BE, FOR WHICHEVER VALUE WINS.** Twenty-two rules declare a size from a token and state no line-height; one more (`.vigilia-add-label`, `editor-shell.css:1265-1266`) pairs `var(--text-2xs)` with the literal `1.2`, which is that token's companion written out. All 23 are in one stylesheet, and the three rules that *do* state a line-height (`:1266`, `:1932`, `:2119`) are deliberate and unaffected. A browser assertion and a pairing contract on the stylesheet would hold whichever value is chosen. VALUE RESOLVED AND THE PRODUCT FIX LANDED, 2026-10-13; WHAT REMAINS IS THE DRAWING. The second and third measurements left the value contested between the acceptance instrument and DESIGN.md and gave the choice to the user. It is not contested, on four readings taken 2026-10-13. (1) DESIGN.md section 2's table gives `--text-sm` line-height 1.4 and its own front matter reads `typography: # --text-* with their stated line-height companions`; the same six ratios are declared in `editor-shell.css`'s `@theme static` block, whose note says they are stated rather than inherited. (2) `shell-appearance.spec.ts:424-429` already pins the utility path to 12px/16.8px and 11px/14.3px - those ratios - so 1.4 is a value this repo tests. (3) The file's own shape: `.vigilia-add-label` paired `--text-2xs` with its companion, and the scale pin in `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts` already ends 'every size states its own', so one rule doing it is what makes the other 21 omissions rather than choices - no comment in the file mentions a line-height at any of them. (4) The drawings' 1.45 is page furniture, `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` on the page body, and the drawings README states the precedence in its own words: 'Where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins and the file is stale.' `design-language.spec.ts:3058-3065` adds that a furniture value off the scale would redden that row, and 1.45 is not one of section 2's six ratios, so the furniture is off-scale by the spec's own rule and unread only because no reader reads the property. **LANDED.** `editor-shell.css` now pairs all 22 sites with `var(--text-N--line-height)` (21 added, 1 literal replaced). `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts` gains the source contract 'pairs every stated size with that token's own line-height', which listed exactly those 22 sites before the change (exit 1) and none after (exit 0). `shell-appearance.spec.ts`'s density test now reads the shell's own rules in a browser: 18px / 16.5px / 15px / 22.5px against the pre-fix bundle (exit 1), and section 2's 16.8px / 14.3px / 12px / 19.5px against the rebuilt one (exit 0). `npm run design:check` exit 0 with `editor-shell.css` at 0 violations under a ceiling of 0; the editor-shell unit suite 26 files / 317 tests green; the six specs holding the changed selectors 46 passed / 0 failed serially. `editor.spec.ts` ran 80 passed / 5 failed in parallel and all five passed serially in 28.3s, which is this suite's recorded load behaviour rather than this change. **WHAT REMAINS, AND WHOSE.** The drawings' furniture still renders 1.45, so the acceptance instrument is now the stale side by its own README's rule - and the correction is not one value: section 2's companions differ per size (1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.3, 1.3, 1.2), so a single page-body ratio cannot express them and each drawn text element would have to state its own. That is the drawing owner's act, filed as `vg-440`. The frames beside those drawings were already stale before this change and nothing re-shoots them (`vg-402`), so this deepens that row rather than creating it.

title: Two hairlines the control-set drawing draws have no counterpart in the product: the read-only rows' dashed dividers and the section headers' trailing rules
detail: FOUND BY RE-MAKING PLAN 1'S PARITY COMPARISON (2026-10-13, read-only; the census is on `vg-390`). WHAT: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` draws each read-only row with `border-bottom:1px dashed var(--edge2)` (`:176` and `:180`) and draws each section header as eyebrow + count + a `flex:1;height:1px;background:var(--edge2)` rule + chevron (`:31`, `:43`, `:119`, `:126`, `:152`, `:171`). The product renders neither: the read-only rows are `flex items-baseline gap-…` carrying no border (`selection-inspector/column.tsx:196-202`), and the section header ends at the chevron's `ml-auto` (`components/ui/inspector-section.tsx:83`), the section's own separation being a top `border-t border-edge` (`:58`). WHY NO GATE SEES IT: the two comparisons that still read this drawing read the label column's width (`tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:913-934`) and the plain-DOM box's padding (`design-language.spec.ts:2540-2552`), and no row reads a divider. WHAT THE RULE SAYS, AND WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN EDIT: §4 *describes* `--edge-2` as 'A boundary, and a fainter one (dividers inside a section)' (`DESIGN.md:100`) — a definition of the role, not a requirement that any element carry it — so neither hairline is backed by a cited rule, and no §5 entry names either. WHAT SETTLES IT: the user's ruling of 2026-10-10 makes the drawing the acceptance instrument, so the default reading is to draw them; but a decoration no rule requires and no instrument reads is the ruling owner's call rather than a fixer's, and the same question is open on the inspector's selected-state headers, which draw the same rule. TWO WAYS IT CLOSES: implement both hairlines from the drawing, or record them as deliberate and give the item's second clause the rule it is missing. NEAR ROWS: `vg-443` (the same header's family, where the drawing and §2 agree against the product), `vg-442` (a drawn value no instrument reaches), `vg-402` (a capture that compares nothing for a region the drawing draws). RESOLVED IN TWO HALVES ON 2026-10-13, AND THE CENSUS THAT FILED THIS ROW MISSED A RULE FOUR LINES ABOVE ITS OWN EVIDENCE. HALF ONE, THE READ-ONLY ROWS' DIVIDER, IS BACKED BY A CITED RULE AND IS NOT A DEFECT: `selection-inspector/column.tsx:191-194` carries the product's own note — 'A read-only row is not a control: no well, no border, because a border means editable (DESIGN.md §5.1)' — which is exactly the clause this row said did not exist, so the drawing's `border-bottom:1px dashed var(--edge2)` (`controls.html:176`, `:180`) is the stale side and the class-4 entry the census gave it on `vg-390` is corrected there. HALF TWO, THE SECTION HEADER'S TRAILING RULE, IS IMPLEMENTED: `components/ui/inspector-section.tsx` now renders the drawn `flex:1;height:1px` line in `--edge-2` between the count and the chevron, carrying `data-vigilia-section-rule`, and its docblock records why this half is a difference the drawing wins where half one is a difference a rule wins — nothing in the product or in `DESIGN.md` argued against it, and the docblock's four recorded decisions (the header is the button, a read-only section says so in words, the 24×24 target, the count's place) do not mention it. RED FIRST, on a build from this tree: `toHaveCSS("height", "1px")` failed `Error: element(s) not found` against the pre-fix bundle, and the whole spec passes after the rebuild (12 passed, exit 0). **So this row is closed: implemented for the header, and backed by §5.1 for the divider**, and nothing in the inspector is left of the drawing's hairline question — the neighbouring instrument gaps are `vg-402` (a capture that compares nothing for a region a drawing draws) and `vg-442` (a drawn value no instrument reads).
check: `inspector-sections.spec.ts` "the section header takes the drawing's rule, §2's mono count and §4's faint, and the subject name §2's 600" asserts the trailing rule (`[data-vigilia-section-rule]` is 1px, in `--edge-2`) and passes red-then-green on a built bundle; the read-only rows' dashed dividers are the rule-backed half — `selection-inspector/column.tsx:191-194` cites §5.1 — so both hairlines the drawing asked for are settled

title: The case named 'names where to choose from when nothing is selected' pins a literal that names no place, so §7.4 is counted met by a check that cannot fail
detail: FOUND WHILE CHECKING PLAN 2'S DEFERRED ADJUDICATIONS (2026-10-13). WHAT THE RULE REQUIRES: §7.4 — 'With nothing selected the column is empty and says where to choose from' (`DESIGN.md:279`). WHAT THE PRODUCT DOES: it renders `Select an object to inspect it.` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts`'s `inspectorFields.nothingSelected`, drawn by `selection-inspector/inspector.tsx:60-66`), a line that names no place an author can choose from, so the product is off the clause. WHAT THE CHECK DOES: `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts:635` is named 'names where to choose from when nothing is selected', and its assertion (`:647`) pins that same literal — which the jsdom case compares against `uiCopy.inspectorFields.nothingSelected` itself (`:643-646`) — so the case's *name* asserts §7.4 while its *assertion* pins the string: it passes whether or not the line names a place, and it would pass if the copy got worse. THE ARCHIVED LEDGER ALREADY COUNTED IT MET: plan 6's acceptance records the inspector's empty state as naming where to choose from, on this case, which is how a §7.4 gap survived a plan whose subject was copy and whose instruments were its own. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the fix is a string and two authorities disagree about what it should say — the drawing's second line is `Pick something on the canvas` (plan 2's table row 20), which names the canvas rather than the Add pane the author actually inserts from — so which place the line names is a copy decision, and it is also the half of the item that `vg-445` leaves open. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a line that names where to choose from, plus a case that fails against the present string — the two together, since either alone leaves the clause counted met by nothing. RESOLVED 2026-10-13, BOTH HALVES THIS ROW NAMED. THE LINE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts`'s `nothingSelected` now reads 'Select an object on the canvas to inspect it.' The place is the canvas because that is the surface an existing object is chosen on; the Add pane inserts a new one, which is a different act and not what §7.4's 'choose from' names. THE CASE: `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s 'names where to choose from when nothing is selected' now asserts the property the clause states rather than the literal — `toHaveText(/canvas/i)` — so it registers a line that stops naming a place, which the literal pin could not; the string's provenance stays pinned in jsdom, where it is compared against the constant itself. RED FIRST, on a bundle without the fix: the case failed `unexpected value "Select an object to inspect it."`; it passes after the rebuild, and the whole spec file passes 12/12. Gate `npm run gate` exit 0 (255 files, 3,363 tests). **Nothing of §7.4 is left uncounted**: the clause is now asserted by a case that can fail, and the neighbouring row `vg-445` closes on the same commit for the second half of its pair.
check: `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts`’s case "names where to choose from when nothing is selected" asserts the place the line names (`toHaveText(/canvas/i)`) rather than the literal, so it fails when the line stops naming a place; it was red against the pre-fix bundle (`unexpected value "Select an object to inspect it."`) and passes after the rebuild, with `ui-copy.ts`’s `nothingSelected` reading "Select an object on the canvas to inspect it."

title: Two differences plan 2 deferred to later plans were never landed: the Add group headings are still singular, and the inspector's empty state still carries the capture's one-line wording
detail: FOUND BY CHECKING PLAN 2'S TWELVE DEFERRED ADJUDICATIONS AGAINST THE PRODUCT (2026-10-13, read-only; the census is on `vg-390`). Plan 2's parity table (`docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:731-757`) defers twelve of its differences to plans 3, 4 and 5, and the tally at `:768-771` names them; nine landed, and these two did not. ONE, the Add group headings — plan 2's row 9: the drawing writes `CARDS / SHAPES / CHARTS` (`:743`) and the product renders `Card` / `Shape` / `Chart` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts:709-711`). Plan 4's completion report calls these 'plan 4's copy', and the history contradicts the claim: `bd36733d` (2026-10-04, 'a card is insertable as a unit') introduced `cards: "Card"`, four days *before* plan 2's comparison was taken, and no later commit changed them. TWO, the inspector's empty state — plan 2's row 20: the drawing draws two lines (`Nothing selected` over `Pick something on the canvas`, `:754`) and the product renders one, `ui-copy.ts`'s `inspectorFields.nothingSelected` (`selection-inspector/inspector.tsx:60-66`); plan 3 built the surface (`f1a35b82`) and left the wording as the capture had it. WHY THE FIRST MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: a plan recorded a difference as deliberate on the strength of a later plan's ownership, and that plan asserted the same ownership while changing nothing — so the difference has been owned by nobody since 2026-10-08 while two completion reports read as if it were settled. WHY THE SECOND IS NOT PURELY COPY: §7.4 requires the empty column to say where to choose from (`DESIGN.md:279`), which the product's line does not do, and that half is filed as `vg-446`. WHAT SETTLES BOTH: the drawing is the acceptance instrument, so the plural headings and the two-line empty state are the target, and `vg-154` records the neighbouring case where plan 4 declined the mockup's dashed import row on purpose — the difference here is that no record declines these two. NEAR ROWS: `vg-269` (the third unlanded deferral, which plan 4 declined *and* filed, which is the correct handling these two did not get), `vg-154`, `vg-446`. RESOLVED IN TWO HALVES ON 2026-10-13, AND THE FIRST WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN BUILT. HALF ONE, THE ADD GROUP HEADINGS: there is no difference left to land, because the target moved to the product's own words. The current drawings write `Card` / `Shape` / `Chart` / `Asset` — singular strings at `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:63`, `:96`, `:116` and `:128`, uppercased by CSS (`text-transform:uppercase`), which is the form plan 2's table transcribed as `CARDS / SHAPES / CHARTS`. The plural belonged to the frozen original `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:91` ('Cards'), which the drawings README says is 'the record of the first cut, not the target', and the same README requires the current set's copy to be taken string by string from `ui-copy.ts` — so the drawing and the editor cannot disagree about these words by construction. The process half of what this row recorded stands and is worth keeping: a plan called the difference deliberate on the strength of a later plan's ownership, and that plan asserted the same ownership while changing nothing (`bd36733d`, 2026-10-04, introduced `cards: "Card"` four days before plan 2's comparison), so the difference was owned by nobody until the target absorbed it. HALF TWO, THE EMPTY STATE: landed on the same commit as `vg-446`, whose clause is the same clause — `ui-copy.ts`'s `nothingSelected` now names the canvas. **So this row closes**, and the third of plan 2's unlanded deferrals, `vg-269`, remains the one that was handled correctly: plan 4 declined it and filed it.

title: The Composition row's role word is painted over by the layer-state slot at the rail's normative 246px - it is covered, not clipped, and the row's own proposed check would pass
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 11 (2026-10-10) WHILE CAPTURING THE PANES FOR THE PARITY GATE, NOT BY A FAILING TEST - and that half of it stands: no gate in this repo renders the panes (design-language.spec.ts's spacing gate reads [data-fixture-root] *, carried only by the synthetic control-fixture.tsx), so the only way this was going to be seen is a person looking at a capture. WHAT THE CAPTURES SHOW: in three registered captures - composition-panel-starter, composition-panel-two-hundred and the new pane-composition - the last glyph of every row's role word is not fully rendered at 1x (Networ / Storag / Cloc / Tex), while the name column beside it ellipsises properly. RE-MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-10, built bundle at 788f1448, live editor preview, default Composition pane, all ten rows), AND THE FRAMING CHANGES: the role word is not clipped, it is COVERED. Nothing reports overflow - .vigilia-layer-role's glyph extent equals its box on all ten rows (a Range over the text node gives Network 250-291 = 41px against a box of 250-291, and Performance trends 196-291 = 95px against a box of 196-291), the element is overflow: visible with text-overflow: clip, and .vigilia-layer-row reports scrollWidth == clientWidth == 220 with its box at 75-295 and the grid column at 62-308. THE CAUSE IS A SLOT THE ROW PAINTS OVER ITSELF: .vigilia-layer-state is position: absolute with left: 212.4px, right: 2px and width 6px, so it occupies x 287-293 - inside the row's own 220px box, but 4px across the role's right edge at 291 - and it carries background-color: rgba(239, 249, 242, 0.75). It is empty (, no children, no ::before/::after content), so that fill is all it paints, and a 75%-opaque six-pixel panel-coloured block laid over the role's last glyphs is what reads as a cut glyph at 1x. THIS ALSO CLOSES THE ARITHMETIC THE ROW COULD NOT CLOSE: nothing consumes the missing width, because no width is missing - the 289-293 range the row measured the cut at IS the state slot's own box. The row had the answer in hand and filed it as a width puzzle: it named the state controls as laid over the row edge by position: absolute, then asked only whether they consume width. They do not; they cover. WHAT THIS DOES TO THE ROW'S OWN CLOSURE CHECK: it would pass, so it is not the gate. 'The role element must not report scrollWidth > clientWidth inside the row at 246px' is satisfied today (41 == 41) and will stay satisfied however the overlap is fixed. The check has to be geometric or painted: the role's box must not intersect the state slot's box, or the capture must assert the last glyph's pixels. FILED RATHER THAN FIXED (AGENTS.md): the cause is now established, but more than one owner could fix it and the fix is a design decision - reserve the slot's width in the row's layout so the role stops before it, take the state out of the role's tail, or move it - and no plan owns that yet, so it needs a ruling first. HOW TO CLOSE IT: make one capture-driven geometric check (role.right <= state.left at 246px) and re-capture the three Composition images. READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, default Composition pane, all ten rows): the geometry the row describes measures the same — `aside.editor-shell-panel` is 246px (box 46-292, scrollWidth 245 == clientWidth 245, so the column does not scroll); every `.vigilia-layer-role` box ends at right 275 and every `.vigilia-layer-state` slot occupies x 271-277 (6px, `position: absolute`, computed `background-color: rgb(18, 22, 28)` - graphite's panel), so the overlap is 4px on all ten rows. That is the same 4px the row measured, at a different absolute x because the column moved (46-292 today against the row's 62-308), and the fill is now opaque rather than the 75%-alpha block the row found. The row's own closure check still passes and is still not the gate: role `scrollWidth == clientWidth` on every row (41/41, 37/37, 95/95, 30/30, 24/24, 21/21, 21/21, 26/26, 19/19, 19/19). Geometry can be stated at this width: role.right 275 against state.left 271 fails today by 4px on all ten. RESOLVED 2026-10-13, AND THE FIX WAS NOT THE ONE THE ROW PROPOSED — WHICH IS WHY THE ROW'S OWN CHECK WOULD HAVE PASSED. What the captures show is real and was still there at HEAD: measured on a built bundle at 1280×720, all ten starter rows lost the last glyphs of their role at rest. But the cause the row settled on was half of it. The slot is `position: absolute; right: 2px` and carried its panel fill and its 6px `padding-left` unconditionally, so an EMPTY slot — and at rest every slot is empty — laid a six-pixel opaque block over the role's tail: 4px of overlap on all ten rows, `slotWidth` 6. THE FIX: the fill and the lead-in belong to the slot's buttons (`.vigilia-layer-state:has(button)`), so a slot holding nothing paints nothing and has no width, and the room the buttons need is reserved by the row's own `padding-right` rather than by a margin on the key column — because the column under the slot is the key on some rows and the ROLE on a row whose selection reads nothing, which is the row the row's own reading measured. The four `:has` arms keep the arithmetic they had (`4 + 2 + 6 + 26n + 4(n - 1)`, the same 32px at n=1) and `design-tokens`' ceiling records the four new sites in place of the three old ones. THE CHECK IS THE GEOMETRIC ONE THE ROW ASKED FOR, with one correction: it asserts the state the three captures were taken in — nothing selected, nothing hovered — rather than every state, because the attended row is a second defect with its own cause. RED FIRST: the case read a 4px overlap on all ten rows before the fix and passes after the rebuild; the file's 11 cases pass and `npm run gate` exits 0 (255 files, 3,363 tests). The four Composition captures beside the drawings were re-taken (`composition-panel-starter`, `-two-hundred`, `-document`, `pane-composition`). WHAT THE ROW DID NOT SEE: once the slot holds real controls, a row whose reserved strip is wider than its columns can spare runs the role under the slot — 45.3px at three controls, 53.8px at four — and no column may yield, since the mark, the name's floor and the role are each recorded as never giving way. That is filed as `vg-447`, and it is the reason the row's own proposed closure ('the role element must not report scrollWidth > clientWidth') was never the gate: it is satisfied in both states, as the row itself said.
check: `composition-panel.spec.ts`’s case "the state slot does not cover the role, at rest or with the row attended" reads every row’s role box against the slot’s box at the rail’s 246px and finds no overlap, red first at 4px on all ten starter rows against a 6px empty slot; `.vigilia-layer-state:has(button)` now owns the fill and the lead-in, and the room is the row’s own padding-right

title: The Tokens pane overflows the rail's 246px column sideways by 205px, because the font-trio well's value cannot shrink
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 11'S CAPTURE (2026-10-10, commit 788f1448) AS A MEASUREMENT IT DID NOT FILE, AND HANDED TO TASK 12; RE-MEASURED, AND THE CAUSE NAMED, HERE. Measured with Playwright against the same built bundle the capture photographed: with the Tokens pane showing, `aside.editor-shell-panel` reports `scrollWidth` 449 against `clientWidth` 244 (box 62-308), so the column scrolls 205px sideways; the widest descendant is `div.ml-auto flex flex-1 items-center justify-end gap-[var(--space-6)]` (components/ui/control-well.tsx:211) inside the ControlSelect the preset list labels Font trio (panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx:403), whose button is 433px wide (x 75-508) around the value "Yaldevi Libre Franklin — Yaldevi + Libre"; its own `span.flex-1 truncate` cannot help - REASONED FROM THE CSS, NOT MEASURED, because the span's own box was not recorded; what was measured is the column's scrollWidth/clientWidth and the widest descendant's box. The CSS argument: `white-space: nowrap` makes the whole string the flex item's min-content width and the item carries no `min-w-0`. The other three panes do NOT overflow (each measured `scrollWidth == clientWidth == 244`), and the four captures could not show it: the column image is the scroll origin. NOT FIXED HERE because the fix site is not one owner — shrinking the value is the well's (plan 1's control set, whose row structure makes the whole pane grow) while the trio's name and the pane's own layout are plan 4's — and whether the answer is truncation, a shorter trio name or a stacked label is a design decision.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, Tokens slot, both its sections showing): the overflow the row measured is not there today. `aside.editor-shell-panel` reports scrollWidth 245 against clientWidth 245 (box 46-292) - overflow 0px, against the row's 205px. The Font trio `ControlSelect` (`[data-vigilia-font-trio]`) is mounted and 139px wide (x 140-279) inside the 221px pane, its value span 110.38px at `white-space: nowrap`, truncating rather than widening the column. THE CAUSE, AND WHAT IT IS: the well's flex row now reads `flex min-w-0 flex-1 items-center justify-end gap-[var(--space-6)]` in `components/ui/control-well.tsx`'s `column` shape - it carries `min-w-0` (computed 0px) where the row's cell recorded none, and carries no `ml-auto` - and that string arrived in `0e7b3405` ("one geometry for a field row, and the legacy rules under it", 2026-10-11), an ancestor of HEAD. That ancestry is not a red proof: removing `min-w-0` was not tried, so nothing here shows it restores the 205px. What is measured is the no-overflow reading today, and `min-w-0` present on the row whose absence the row named. The pane's other two selects (`[data-vigilia-font-face]`, `[data-vigilia-type-preset]`) measure the same 139px, so the trio is not the odd one out. RESOLVED 2026-10-13, ON A READING AND THEN A RED PROOF. The 2026-10-12 reading already found the overflow gone (`aside.editor-shell-panel` scrollWidth 245 against clientWidth 245, the Font trio's `ControlSelect` 139px inside a 221px pane, its value span truncating at `white-space: nowrap`), and named `min-w-0` as the difference — present on the well's column row now, absent in the cell the row measured, arriving in `0e7b3405`. What the row did not have was anything that would notice a return, which is the same gap the row itself complains about elsewhere: the capture cannot show it, because the column image is the scroll origin. THAT IS NOW CLOSED: `tests/e2e/editor-rail.spec.ts` has a case, 'no pane's column scrolls sideways', that opens each of the four slots in turn and fails on any pane whose column scrolls sideways, naming the slot in the failure. RED FIRST, AGAINST THE CAUSE THIS ROW NAMED RATHER THAN AGAINST A STUB: with `min-w-0` removed from `control-well.tsx`'s column shape the case fails on Tokens by 198px — the row's 205px on a pane whose metrics have moved — with the other three panes clean, which is the row's own account of the defect reproduced; the file was restored byte-identical (`cmp` against a copy taken before the edit) and the case passes on the rebuilt bundle, along with the rail spec's other ten cases. `npm run gate` exit 0 (255 files, 3,363 tests). **So this row closes: the difference is fixed, and the instrument that would catch its return exists.** The neighbouring rows are `vg-260` (the same row's geometry at the rail's 246px, which is a decision) and `vg-447` (the attended layer row, filed 2026-10-13).

title: The rail's slot is a 34px icon-only control, outside section 5's 26-30px icon button
detail:
FOUND BY the controller while correcting a stale STATUS claim about who owned the value, and MEASURED before filing. editor-shell.css:789-790 sets the rail slot's width and height to 34px, and rail.tsx:33 documents it as 'a 34px icon-only control whose one word is both its tooltip and ...'. Bible section 5 states its control vocabulary is CLOSED - 'A control is one of these, or it is not a control' - and its icon button is 'a 26-30px square at --radius-md, glyph only'. A 34px glyph-only control is therefore either an icon button outside the range the bible states for it, or a control the closed vocabulary does not contain. NOTHING OWNS THE DECISION, which is the part worth recording: the shell plan never mentions 34; scripts/design-tokens.gated.json's designLanguagePx array is [3, 11, 14, 26, 30, 32, 36, 46, 246, 276, 999, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8] and contains no 34; and the value lives in editor-shell.css, which is deliberately UNGATED - Task 8 records that file's hex count as a before-state for plan 3 rather than adding it to the guard - so the guard never sees it. rail.tsx IS a gated file, but it carries the 34 only inside a comment, which the guard does not read. So the one mechanism that could have caught this is blind to it twice over. Same family as vg-202 (a well's horizontal padding at 6px where section 3's table assigns 4px): a value off the bible's own table that no gate watches. OWNER: whoever owns the rail's control size - either the rail moves into 26-30px, or designLanguagePx gains 34 and section 5 gains the entry the slot needs. SEVERITY: low, and note the direction of the risk: a target larger than the bible's range is safer than one smaller, so this is a conformance gap rather than an accessibility defect.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller on the user's direction that the rail icons be 'a bit bigger than right now', with the code/architecture half judged rather than asked. THE SLOT GOES TO 36PX, SECTION 5 GAINS A RAIL-SLOT ROLE RATHER THAN STRETCHING THE ICON BUTTON RANGE (26-30px is the icon button's and stays), AND designLanguagePx GAINS 36 so the value stops living in a comment the ratchet cannot read. The rails dependent arithmetic is re-derived in the same change -- the 6px gutter, the centred slot and the 46px rail at editor-shell.css:957,966,1000 are all written against 34 -- and the result is inspected in the browser rather than asserted. COST IF WRONG: the slot is one number and the rail's arithmetic is local, so reversing it is cheap; leaving 34 in place while enlarging only the glyphs was rejected because it splits one control's size across two owners. RESOLVED 2026-10-13, ON THE RULING'S OWN RECIPE AND THEN MEASUREMENT. The slot is 36px and section 5 now names it: a **Rail slot** row — a 36px square at `--radius-lg`, glyph only, one of §7.2's four panes — sits beside the icon button whose 26–30px range the ruling refused to stretch, so the one control larger than an icon button has a vocabulary entry of its own. `designLanguagePx` needed no edit: 36 was already on the list for §5's slider well, so the value is readable to the ratchet the row says is blind to it. THE RAIL'S ARITHMETIC WAS RE-DERIVED AND THEN MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: the strip's 1px right hairline and its 1px left inset leave 44px of content, and a 36px slot centred in that reads 5…41 with a 5px gutter each side, so the slot's padding box ends at 40 and the accent bar's offset is `-6px` — 46 − 40 — not the drawing's `-5px`, whose spans carry no resting border. Measured on the built bundle: rail 0…46, slot 5…41, bar 44…46, the bar's outer edge on the rail's inner edge. THE SIZE AND THE OFFSET ARE PINNED TOGETHER AND BOTH WERE PROVED RED: with the bar left at the stale `-7px` the case fails on a bar at 45…47, one pixel into the pane; against `423c557f`'s copy of `editor-shell.css` it fails on `34` where §5 asks 36. The case now asserts the slot's own width as well, and each restore was verified byte-identical with `cmp` before the green run on the rebuilt bundle. The drawing moved with the code — `current/shell.html`'s five slot spans to 36px and its bar to `-5px` — and the shell captures kept beside the drawings are re-shot, together with the six palette captures the rail is also in. WHAT THE CHANGE DOES NOT DO: the glyph stays the 17px the rest of the chrome uses. The ruling moved the slot — the control, its hover boundary and its accent wash — and named no mark, so the user's "a bit bigger than right now" is delivered as a bigger control rather than a bigger icon; growing the glyph is one number and is deliberately not taken here. **So this row closes: the difference §5 had no row for is fixed, §5 has the row, and a browser case fails if either the size or the bar's offset moves back.** Its neighbour is `vg-448`, the slot's radius, filed from this work.
check: editor-rail.spec.ts's 'the slot is section 5's 36px rail slot' assertion on the rebuilt bundle, plus the red proof against 423c557f's copy of editor-shell.css

title: The shell ships two competing cluster treatments, and the glass one sits off the elevation ladder in both directions
detail:
FOUND BY the controller while ruling on plan 2 Task 6's cluster surface, and then MEASURED before filing rather than filed from the ruling. The product has two floating-cluster treatments. (1) The identity chip states bible section 7.5 literally: --panel at ~95%, blur(6px), elevation 1. (2) The dock (canvas-dock.tsx:126) and the view cluster (display-switch.tsx:104) carry .editor-glass (editor-shell.css:375-400), whose base is box-shadow: none - section 3's LEVEL 0, flat - and whose five non-editorial palettes override with a gradient background, two inset highlights, 0 18px 40px #0000004a and backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(135%). Against the bible that is off the ladder twice over: 0 18px 40px is section 3's LEVEL 2 (overlay) value, not the LEVEL 1 (0 8px 20px #00000059) that section 3 assigns to floating clusters over the canvas, and blur is 10px where section 3 says clusters blur their backdrop at blur(6px). Section 7.5 independently calls a cluster --panel at ~95% with backdrop blur, 1px --edge, elevation 1. So in five palettes a cluster renders at overlay elevation and in editorial it renders at no elevation at all. Worth recording precisely: the bible contains NO per-palette glass rule - section 4 says only that colour is a runtime palette of six - so 'editorial is flat and the other five are glass' is an IMPLEMENTATION choice pinned by shell-appearance.spec.ts from the earlier authoring work, not an instruction that outranks section 7.5. That matters because the tempting resolution (match the chip) reddens that spec for all six palettes, which is why Task 6 kept the glass and filed this instead. OWNER: first a design-language decision - which of the two treatments is the product's, whether the ladder's level 1 or the glass palette's overlay value wins, and what editorial does about elevation when it is deliberately flat - and then whoever owns the two surfaces. Task 10's difference list inherits it. SEVERITY: medium - nothing fails and nothing is unreachable, but two settled-looking treatments disagree in the same window and the ladder has no answer for editorial. AMENDED BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11), which moved the treatment boundary: `.editor-glass` is now the CHROME default (`background: var(--panel)`, no shadow, no blur) and the two clusters opt into the glass by name (`.editor-shell-dock.editor-glass`, `.editor-shell-zoom.editor-glass`), so this row's citation of `editor-shell.css` line numbers and of a base that is `box-shadow: none` with five per-palette overrides is a stale landmark rather than a description of the file. THE FINDING IS UNCHANGED and so is the treatment this row measures: the dock and the view cluster still paint a gradient, two inset highlights, `0 18px 40px #0000004a` and `backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(135%)`, and Task 5 gave `editorial`'s two clusters the same treatment, so the off-ladder cluster surface now reaches all six palettes where it reached five. Task 5 did not absorb this row: the elevation-2 shadow and the 10px blur against section 3's elevation 1 and `blur(6px)` are untouched, and the identity chip's competing treatment is untouched too.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE IDENTITY CHIP'S TREATMENT IS THE PRODUCT'S CLUSTER TREATMENT -- elevation 1 with blur(6px). The dock and view clusters come down to the ladder rather than section 3 gaining the level their glass implies, so the off-ladder surface that Task 5 spread to all six palettes is retired rather than documented. CLOSED 2026-10-13 AS VERIFIED, AND THE CLOSE IS ONE MEASUREMENT PLUS ONE LEFTOVER THE RULING COULD NOT SEE. The ladder half: `d0c67844` took the dock and the view cluster to the chrome's own 95% `--panel` and section 3's `--elev-1`, under the user's later ruling on this same surface (asked for Graphite, answered "All six palletes, all flat"), so the `135deg` gradient, the two inset highlights, `0 18px 40px #0000004a` and `blur(10px) saturate(135%)` that Task 5 spread to every palette are gone, and elevation is now the whole difference between chrome and a cluster. The chip half: this row's ruling makes the chip's treatment the product's, and the chip still declared `backdrop-filter: blur(6px)` with its `-webkit-` twin - the last declaration of the glass treatment anywhere in the product, and invisible to every computed read because the build emits the prefixed form alone (`vg-311`, whose cause is `vg-430`) and this Chromium does not apply it. So the stylesheet asked for a blur while the case that reads all six palettes was green over it. `f7f838dc` deleted the two declarations and gave `shell-appearance.spec.ts` the read that catches the state it was in: the treatment-boundary case now also scans the authored text for `backdrop-filter:`, prefixed forms included, red on both lines before the deletion. THE RULING'S BLUR CLAUSE IS THE ONE PART NOT CARRIED, AND THE USER SUPERSEDED IT THE NEXT DAY by ruling the product flat for all six palettes; DESIGN.md section 3 and section 7.5 were propagated with that decision, so `blur(6px)` is no longer a value the language assigns to any cluster rather than a value these two lack. Measured: the treatment-boundary case exit 1 with the scan over the undeleted declaration and exit 0 after, on rebuilt bundles; `npm run gate` exit 0 (255 files, 3,363 tests; design:check 315 citation sources). One by-product worth recording: `vg-311`'s verified check says no rule in `editor-shell.css` declares `backdrop-filter` at all, which was loose when it was written and is now literally true.
check: The shell ships one cluster treatment, not two competing ones: `shell-appearance.spec.ts` derives the boundary membership from the stylesheet, then reads all three of section 7.5 floating clusters - the dock, the view cluster and the identity chip - as a set in all six palettes on the built bundle, asserting each is translucent over the palette own `--panel` and carries section 3 `--elev-1` with no gradient and no blur; and it scans `editor-shell.css` for `backdrop-filter:` with the prefixed forms included, so the glass treatment two off-ladder values (elevation 2 `0 18px 40px` and `blur(10px)`) are retired rather than documented
